News.title: Girl, 10, reveals moment mum said ‘we’re going to die’ before ‘crashing car on motorway and trying to stab her & sister’
News.content:
‘I’M GOING TO KILL YOU’ Girl, 10, reveals moment mum said ‘we’re going to die’ before ‘crashing car on motorway and trying to stab her & sister’







Next

A 10-YEAR-OLD girl has revealed the moment her mum allegedly said they were “all going to die” before crashing her car.

Janieka Ellington, 35, allegedly slammed her SUV into a concrete barrier then tried to stab her two children, 10 and 15, to death.



Police said she smashed into the left-side barrier, before veering onto the right shoulder, then went left again and hit a lorry in the middle lane.

Cops said Ellington then continued to the left and smashed into the concrete barrier again.



The car rolled over on the passenger side and stopped, police said.

But when witnesses rushed to help, Ellington allegedly began to chase her teen daughter with a knife while threatening to kill her.

Three good Samaritans, including two soldiers intervened and disarmed the attacker.

The horrifying crash took place in Dupont, near Seattle on Monday morning.

Ellington faces four counts of attempted murder and a vehicular assault charge.

Witness Nathan Wilkinson was driving to work when he saw people struggling on the road by the crash.



He told Komonews: “In the moment, it happens so quickly.”

“You just see a bunch of people wrestling and stuff and trying to understand what’s going on.

“I’m not sure if she screamed ’cause she’s being attacked or what was going on, and then I saw them jump on top of this person and wrestle the knife away.”

Ellington’s younger daughter told authorities her mum had thought they were being followed, shouting that “they were all going to die” before crashing the car.

Court documents said that once out of the car, Ellington brandished a knife chased her kids, yelling “I’m going to kill you”.



Both girls were rushed to hospital after the crash.

One was left with a broken ankle, and another with several broken bones, a spine injury and stab wounds.

The lorry driver was reportedly uninjured after the crash.

Sgt. Alexis McKay, a Washington National Guard combat medic, said the two soldiers who stepped in may have saved the kids lives.

She said: “The sergeant first class that was involved was able to hold the arm in place with the assistance of the 15-year-old daughter, trying to keep it off of her stomach.



“They were able to disarm her and then pin her to the ground while I pulled the 15-year-old away.”

“His reaction time is why we have two living children today,”

Cops believe Ellington was under the under the influence of alcohol and having suicidal thoughts at the time of the crash.

The mum has been ordered to undertake a mental health evaluation.

She is being held without bail awaiting trial and is next due in court on October 20.

News.title: Even millennials want return of death penalty in UK. Some monsters deserve it, but here’s why it would never work
News.content:
Next

I AGREE with the death penalty. I’m perfectly happy for the most despicable murderers in our society to be rubbed out.

Why should someone who has, say, tortured a 19-year-old girl to death be allowed to continue to draw breath? Good riddance, I say.





Let’s save the victims the heartache of knowing they still inhabit the Earth, and let’s save the millions we’d spend keeping them alive for full-life terms (we shelled out £11million while Peter Sutcliffe, the Yorkshire Ripper, was in Broadmoor).

But here’s the thing, I also disagree with the death penalty.

My problem is this: Once you’ve worked out who gets it (and I think only those whose crimes are beyond any doubt should qualify, so yes to Axel Rudakubana but no to Lucy Letby), how the hell are you actually going to do it?

Who administers the fatal charge/injection/bullet? And how can we guarantee that we get it right? The thing is, we can’t ensure we will get it right.

The extraordinary case of Christa Pike, a twisted murderer who tortured her 19-year-old victim, Colleen Slemmer, to death, is further proof that those who use the death penalty just keep on cocking it up.

Pike is still alive and has now started speaking, despite two supposedly “lethal” doses of pentobarbital.

Like some sort of horror film where the beast Just. Will. Not. Die.

The death penalty has been going for no less than 3,779 years, when folk were put to death for as little as breaking and entering.





“If a man breaks into a house, they shall kill him and hang him in front of that very breach,” declares the Code of Hammurabi, an Old Babylonian legal text from around 1753 BC. Yet executioners are still buggering it up.

Yes, yes I know some of the older methods were a little more, shall we say, effective (arsonists were often thrown into the fires they started as punishment).

But even in these less barbaric times — and the US constitution bans “cruel and unusual punishments” — many executions have not worked.

Just four months earlier in Tennessee, the same state where Pike’s execution failed, another lethal injection proved to not be so lethal.

Executioners faffed around for ages trying to find a vein in triple murderer Tony Carruthers before eventually postponing it until next year.

In 2024 Idaho executioners had the same problem with serial killer Thomas Creech.

He remains in custody after the aborted attempt and now prosecutors want him dispatched by the apparently more reliable firing squad, a method still used in five US states.

But, incredibly, even getting riddled with bullets from expert marksmen is no guarantee of success.

One fella, Wenceslao Moguel, was shot nine times by a Mexican firing squad in 1915 and when that failed, he was blasted at point blank range and still survived.

Meanwhile, there have been problems with hanging and electric chairs too, which have led to “cruel and unusual punishments” when things went wrong. All this troubles me.



I lose no sleep over the death of society’s worst specimens, but even a hard-hearted bastard like me winces at the thought of subjecting them to an unnecessarily painful and chaotic death.

Even if that is a courtesy they did not extend to their victims.

We abolished the death penalty in this country in 1965, with killers Peter Allen and Gwynne Evans the last to be executed — by hanging — the previous year.

Now there are moves to bring it back, led by the excitable folk in Reform UK, who think it makes them look “tough on crime” and all that.

They and their even more hardline offspring, Restore Britain, want a referendum on its return.

No doubt they are buoyed by surveys that typically show many of us support it — a More In Common poll last year revealed 55 per cent would support bringing back capital punishment.

Incredibly, the percentage was higher (58 per cent) among millennials. So the appetite appears to be there.

But to those who crave it, I ask this: Do you trust the state to not screw it up, to not administer “cruel and unusual punishment”?

Because I don’t.

A REAL STUPID TUCKER



RARELY does a week go by without some American tosspot having a pop at Britain.

This week it was the turn of weirdo podcaster Tucker Carlson.

If you haven’t heard of him, he’s a sort of Simpsons-style caricature with a love of conspiracy theories and a tic that sees him burst into involuntary cackles.

This cartoonish cretin made himself look incredibly dense while interviewing Jacob Rees-Mogg by suggesting Britain was daft to go to war with Hitler, scoffing “who cares?” if he’d conquered us and we all spoke German.

Rees-Mogg calmly called him out and told the Lego-haired lunatic that actually we rather like our country and didn’t fancy it being overrun by murderous racist Nazis.

The silly Tucker soon went viral and was denounced by those on the Left and the Right.

Republican Mike Huckabee, the US Ambassador to Israel, spoke for many, insisting: “He needs help. Serious help.”

He certainly does. Perhaps one way of helping would be for sensible people to stop going on his ludicrous show.

KEM KEY TO SWAY VOTERS

KEMI Badenoch has had a good party conference.



So much so that I feel I don’t need to say who she is any more.

But as she returned from Birmingham after her confident keynote speech, she will no doubt have been painfully aware that all the positive “vibes” and front pages she generated in the last few days are just that.

Because while many of her announcements – punish the idle, reduce inheritance tax, boost defence – will have caught the attention of the well-heeled former dyed-in-the-wool Tories who flounced off in 2024, the rest of Britain will be wondering: “And what are you going to do for ME?”

They may now know who she is and what she stands for – and credit to her team for rescuing her from her once prickly self – but from what we’ve heard so far I suspect the vast majority of lapsed Tories will still be making plans for Nigel.

ONLY ten per cent of people now smoke, new figures reveal.

Can’t say I’m surprised.

Judging by the incessant pong pervading the streets near me, everyone has swapped cigarettes for spliffs.

IT'S IN THE AIR MORE than half of us believe the key to happiness is spending time outdoors, inhaling the smell of fresh rainfall and the woods, according to a new survey. Hear hear! I am firmly in that camp (presumably those who don’t agree are all gamers?). And as autumn rears its golden head I look forward to many life-affirming – and bracing – walks in the English countryside. I’m reminded of Bill Bryson’s wonderful observation that it is a unique quirk of us Brits that with our love of “taking some air” we have turned breathing into a leisure activity. Race you to the rope swing!

HARRY LEVEL WITH SHILTON, BUT CAN HE OUT-SCORE RONALDO? SURE HE KANE

GETTING to and from Wembley is always a grind, even if, like me, you live only ten miles away.

But it was worth queueing for sardine-packed Tubes to watch England’s impressive 3-0 win over Czechia on Tuesday night.



I still have no idea what the Nations League is, but it was lovely to watch Harry Kane bang two in (and get an assist for Vladimir Coufal’s own goal . . . ouch!) on a night when he equalled Peter Shilton’s record 125 caps.

Kane is a gold-plated goal machine and, with 91 in the bag for England, has now set his sights on beating Cristiano Ronaldo’s international tally of 146.

With an average of 0.73 goals per game for England, that means he has to play in just another, er, 76 matches.

And I’ll have to wait in many more long queues for the train home.

It’ll be worth it. Come on, Harry!

News.title: Disabled woman, 87, dies weeks after forced eviction from her home in Spain sparked protests & led to snap election
News.content:
TRAGIC END Disabled woman, 87, dies weeks after forced eviction from her home in Spain sparked protests & led to snap election







Next

A SPANISH woman who was evicted from her Madrid home, sparking protests and a snap election, has died aged 87.

Maricarmen Abascal sadly died today, according to Madrid’s tenants’ union.



Spain’s Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez expressed his condolences in a post on X saying: “All my love to Maricarmen’s family and loved ones. A hug as well to all of us who feel this loss as our own today.”

Maricarmen had been hospitalised since she was carried out on a stretcher after being forcibly removed from her beloved Madrid home in September.



She had lived in the property for 71 years, but was evicted following a lengthy court battle, sparking public outrage.

Sanchez announced an early election for November 29 due to the backlash and demonstrations following the eviction.



It comes as the Prime Minister failed to pass measures to address the country’s housing crisis.

Maricarmen’s plight made her a symbol of the country’s housing crisis, with hundreds of thousands of protesters turning out on the streets.



Rent prices have increased by more than 100 per cent over the last decade, according to property site Idealista.

Some have blamed the shortage of available housing for pushing up sky-high rents and pressuring the government to build more new homes.

Controversy first began when an investment firm hiked Maricarmen’s rent by 275 per cent.

Armed officers then stormed the property when she was inside with loved ones, including her cousin and niece.

Supporters of Maricarmen, including Javier Bardem’s brother Carlos and singer Ana Belen, camped outside her building as part of the protest.



She was eventually allowed to return to her long-time home, paying a similar rent under a new eight-year lease with the building’s owner.

Protesters welcomed the decision, however Madrid’s Tenants’ Union has called on the government to approve deeper housing reforms “so that there are no more Maricarmens”.

Maricarmen sadly died just weeks after the forced eviction.

Her father first rented the property in 1956 and she continued as a tenant following her parents’ death.

During this time there was a cap on the rent.



Spain’s Housing Minister Isabel Rodriguez Garcia said she tried to purchase Maricarmen’s apartment but Urbagestion flatly turned it down.

The local government also said she had declined the offer to stay in an elderly care home.

A ministry source said: “They want to throw her out, that’s all.

“They don’t want to hear about solutions.”

Maricarmen’s lawyer, Beatriz Duro said: “There is a police deployment as if this were a military operation.



“This is the fourth time [they’ve tried to evict her] but the first time they’ve come right to the door of the property.

“It’s completely disproportionate.”

News.title: How Kemi killed off ‘Unite The Right’ with one-line put-downs that cut Reform open – and proved she came for a fight
News.content:
Next

WAS it the moment the “Unite The Right” campaign was officially pronounced dead?

Kemi Badenoch strode on to the conference stage yesterday and crushed the prospect of a deal with Nigel Farage beneath her golden stilettos.



Those still hoping for a Tory–Reform alliance were left in no doubt she had come to Birmingham not to play nice — but for a knife fight.

While developing a knack for withering, one-line put-downs, Badenoch instead launched into a methodical skewering of her right-wing rivals.

She had arrived with her scalpel sharpened.



“Character, conduct, and standards matter,” she told the assembled faithful.

“I don’t want to live in a country run by people who threaten journalists, call veterans traitors and debate whether my mixed-race children are English.”

Over no fewer than 400 words, Badnoch sought to cut Reform open and show voters what their insides are made of.

Think we’re the nasty party? Take a look at the other guys.

Worried about Tory sleaze? Hold my beer while I tell you about this dodgy donations scandal.

It felt like the moment a Rubicon had been crossed and any flickering embers of a possible tie-up extinguished for good.



How could Badenoch possibly entertain cutting a deal with people she claims question the Englishness of her kids?

That Tory members whooped her attacks on Reform with as much gusto as they did her attacks on Labour show how the idea of a pact is far from straightforward.

Arsenal and Chelsea fans might both boo Spurs, but that doesn’t mean they mix well.



“They are not like us; we are not like them,” Badenoch told her party. “We are different.”

Team Kemi has spent the conference insisting that striking an agreement with Farage would turn off more wavering voters than it will win.

The endorsement of this strategy from her members will reinforce her belief that an all-out victory is the only option.

In truth, the Tory base would probably not let her jump into bed with Farage even had she wanted to.

Politics is a proud and tribal business.



But persuasive arguments for the Tories and Reform to cut a deal will continue to linger so long as the numbers make it make sense.

Last month’s mega-poll showed just how badly both parties would hurt each other by continuing to compete at the ballot box.

Those calling for a rapprochement will point to Andy Burnham’s radical Big State agenda as proof of the desperate need to unite against a common foe.

And despite both sides’ protestations, there is not THAT much difference between their policy platforms of lower taxes and stronger borders.

Badenoch was adamant that her plan was to woo back disenchanted Tories who flocked to Reform at the fag end of the last government.



“Reform voters, many of them are our people. We let them down and we want them to come back home.”

The question for Badenoch is whether the new electoral map has put a ceiling on her ambitions.

The clarion call of her big speech yesterday was that her revamped Tory party had “something for everyone”.



Yet it did seem to be a recalibration of the Conservative Party towards attracting voters from its traditional Middle England stomping ground rather than make a grab on the Red Wall.

The showstopper pledge to abolish inheritance tax on family homes will land especially well among affluent communities in the south.

Dare I say a fair few Lib Dems might have had their ears pricked on hearing her offer to scrap certain death duties.

But for those working class areas in the north where average house prices are much less likely to be snared by inheritance tax anyway?

Some are seeing this as the Badenoch strategy starting to take shape.



People very close to her privately admit to me that there will be areas of the Red Wall that will never be won back and are now straight shoot-outs between Labour and Reform.

They see Boris Johnson’s 2019 triumph as a freak event where a desire to deliver Brexit and stop Jeremy Corbyn saw Labour voters hold their noses and become the first generation in their family to ever back the Tories.

“They’re never coming back to us,” one shadow cabinet minister tells me.

Wales and Scotland look equally as bleak for the Tories right now.

Voters are less loyal and more mobile these days, but Farage has the advantage of simply “not being a Conservative” in some areas.

He also comes without baggage of 14 years in government and is one of the best orators and campaigners of his generation.



That is not to say Badenoch will suddenly become all soppy on issues like immigration, welfare and defence.

These are flagship issues that chime with a cross-section of society — including Conservative shire heartlands — and she delivered a robust account of herself on all three in her speech.

Likewise she tried to burnish her credentials for sound finances, stopping short of giving her members the total inheritance tax abolition they craved because there is no money left.

And surely this cuts to the rub of what Badenoch was trying to achieve yesterday: ploughing a third way between Labour and Reform and being the antidote to chaos.

While some Tories fear their vote being squeezed in a pincer movement on both their left and right flanks, Kemi spies an opportunity.



People might be terrified of more Labour tax hikes but don’t trust Reform on the economy.

Or they might think Burnham unwilling to fund defence but are a bit alarmed Farage doesn’t have much to say on the matter.

They might think the PM has no mandate to govern but aren’t sure Reform is the real deal either.

This is where Badenoch hopes to find a gap and turn her party’s fortunes around. It is why she will happily lock horns with Reform just as much as Labour.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It will take time to heal the wounds of the past, but she made a clear pitch yesterday that the Tories have “something for everybody”.



The question is whether everybody — or anybody — is ready to listen.

News.title: Plastic surgeon killed after being shot in the head inside Costa del Sol BBL clinic as gunmen fled and manhunt launched
News.content:
GUNFIRE HORROR Plastic surgeon killed after being shot in the head inside Costa del Sol BBL clinic as gunmen fled and manhunt launched







Next

A PLASTIC surgeon has reportedly been shot and killed on the Costa del Sol in the latest of a spate of suspected murders along the Spanish coast.

A 57-year-man died after being shot several times in the head this afternoon in Marbella, police said.



Local reports said the victim is a plastic surgeon who was gunned down inside his clinic in the east of the city.

The clinic specialises in BBLs, supercharged BBLs and boob jobs.



No arrests have yet been made, with a manhunt launched to track down the shooter still at large in the tourist town.

Investigators said a shooter had entered the clinic with several customers inside and opened fire.



He was reportedly dressed in black head-to-toe, fleeing on a motorbike driven by an accomplice.

The victim was pronounced dead at the scene.

His identity has not been confirmed by police.

The shooting took place at Cirumed clinic, founded by Dr. Alexander Aslani, who previously worked as a consultant plastic surgeon at the London Highgate Hospital.



He is known for pioneering the supercharged BBL, which uses implants as well as transferring a patient’s body fat to the buttock area.

He also offers tummy tucks, rib cage reshaping and a “Bikini makeover”, which combines breast augmentation, liposculpture and BBL into a “simple surgery”, according to the clinic’s website.

The National Police in Malaga said: “Around 6pm a shooting occurred in Marbella. The victim, a 57-year-old man, sustained several gunshot wounds to the head.

“The medical personnel who treated him were unable to stabilise him, and he died. The investigation is ongoing.”

A government spokesperson said: “We received the first alert around 5.40pm, saying a worker had been shot inside a clinic east of Marbella town centre.”



It comes as Marbella and the broader Costa del Sol has seen a number of shootings in recent months.

At the weekend, a gunman opened fire on a busy motorway near Estepona.

Vehicles scrambled to get away from the shooter, but no one was injured.

In August, a man was found dead lying in the street with gunshot wounds near Marbella’s seafront.

Last month a man – later unmasked as a notorious football ultra – was shot in the face at a packed restaurant.



Umit Yalcin, 47, was having dinner with three friends when a man suddenly approached the table and opened fire.

Masked attackers rushed the terrace of the Lounge Bar Plaza in Malaga, horrifying onlookers and diners.

Several shots were heard and witnesses said they saw a motor with three people inside speeding away from the scene.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Just days earlier a pregnant woman, grandmother and a child were killed at another Spanish holiday resort.

Two masked men on a motorbike opened fire at a family on the Costa de la Luz near the southern border with Portugal.

News.title: Kemi’s warrior-like speech was peppered with vote-catching ideas – now she must persuade the country Tories can deliver
News.content:
Next

IF anyone was still wondering whether Kemi Badenoch has the stomach for a fight, they were left in no doubt.

The Conservative leader didn’t just deliver a speech, she strapped on her armour and declared war.



In a rallying cry in Birmingham, she braced her troops for a fight “we have not seen in this country for more than half a century.”

She fired them up to stand up for what they believe in – traditional British values, not spending beyond our means and letting people keep more of what they earn.



Her warrior-like speech used the words “fight” and “battle” 21 times.

It was bursting with sound judgement, a masterclass in down-to-earth common sense.



While primarily aimed at galvanising MPs and activists, it also sent a message to the wider public by drawing the dividing lines for the next general election.

She spelled out the clear choice voters face: lower taxes, a smaller state and a push for economic growth under the Tories.

Or more tax, borrow and spend with Labour. It was, as she said, “the Right way or the wrong way.”

Common sense Conservatives or reckless Labour.



The blisteringly sharp address was peppered with vote-catching ideas.

Scrapping inheritance tax on the family home will be welcome by striving families who simply want to leave something behind for their kids.

Cutting national insurance for young workers will ease the tax burden on small businesses and rescue under-25s from the grim prospect of a life on benefits.

Building a £10billion “shield in the sky” to bolster Britain’s air defences is a clear statement of intent that she is serious about national security and rearming our threadbare armed forces.

All we got from Andy Burnham last week was a plan to reform the voting system and reopen the toxic Brexit debate by taking Britain back into the EU’s orbit.



Unlike the PM, Kemi confronted every one of the big issues facing the nation head on.

She laid bare her plans to tackle the prison crisis, violent crime, the bloated welfare bill, our weakened defence capability, illegal immigration and the flatlining economy.

By contrast, there wasn’t a word on any of these massive concerns in Burnham’s speech at the Labour conference last week.

It was littered with vacuous vibes and nostalgia. Or as the Tory leader so aptly put it: “He’s promising a better yesterday while I’m promising a better tomorrow.”

She also socked it to Reform and ruled out a “unite the right” deal with Nigel Farage’s insurgent party.



It remains to be seen whether it will be enough to win back disaffected voters.

But in her 70 minute address, she instilled belief back into the hearts of the Tory troops. Many had forgotten what they stand for.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Kemi’s speech reminded them they are the party of home-ownership, strong national security and economic competence.

Her critical challenge now is to persuade the country they can deliver it.

News.title: Coronation Street, Brookside & Casualty star Eric Potts, 61, admits making indecent images of children over a decade
News.content:
Next

CORONATION Street star Eric Potts is facing years in prison after pleading guilty to making indecent images of children, The Sun can reveal.

The 61-year-old, who played baker Diggory Compton on the cobbles, admitted six serious charges including stashing Category A images.



The actor, who also featured in Brookside and Casualty, was arrested earlier this year and charged with three counts of making indecent photographs of a child and three counts of distributing them.

He last week pleaded guilty to making 83 images over a decade between May 2015 and October of last year.



Seven of those are Category A, the most serious classification, which often displays penetrative sexual activity.

Another 16 images Potts hoarded were in Category B and 60 are Category C.



Prosecutors also said the married father-of-two shared five images on a single day on July 16, 2024.

All the offences took place in Bacup, Lancashire, where the star has lived for 20 years.

Potts appeared before Blackburn magistrates’ court, where he pleaded guilty to all charges in a 10-minute hearing.

Prosecutor Safia Hussain said: “Police officers attended the defendants home address and, seized a number of devices which included a PC, an HP Laptop and an iPhone.



“They were taken for examination by the digital forensic unit, and a number of indecent images were found on the devices.

“The defendant was therefore charged with making and distributing images of Catrgory A, B, and C.”

He will be sentenced at Burnley crown court next month.

Scottish-born Potts is best known for playing eccentric baker Diggory, father of Molly Compton, after four smaller parts on the soap.

He appeared as Diggory in 50 episodes in 2005 and 2006 before he was written out when his character’s business failed.



Speaking about the role in 2019, he said: “It was just a joy being part of such an iconic show.”

Raised in Irvine, Ayrshire, he switched from studying law at Glasgow University to train at the Bristol Old Vic Theatre School from 1984.

He landed a two-year run in the Channel 4 soap Brookside from 1998 as oddball Mr Moore, a character briefly suspected of being a serial killer.

Other TV credits include Heartbeat, The Royal, Last of the Summer Wine, and BBC Scotland sitcom Still Game.

In 2005 he also appeared in an episode of Doctor Who.



He later had roles in Emmerdale between 2012 and 2018, and a part in Hollywood film Oz the Great and Powerful in 2013.

Away from the screen, Potts built a career as a panto dame and writer.

In December 2011 he starred alongside Dame Edna Everage in Dick Whittington at the New Wimbledon Theatre in London.

A Lancashire Constabulary spokesman said: “On August 20 last year we received information that the user of a file sharing account had uploaded an indecent video of a child to the internet.

“Officers from the Internet Child Exploitation Team attended the address linked to the account and arrested Eric Potts on suspicion of possession and distribution of indecent images of children.



“He was subsequently bailed pending further enquiries.

“Following an examination of his devices more illegal imagery was found and Potts, 61, of Bacup, was further arrested.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“He was charged in September this year and appeared at Blackburn Magistrates’ Court on October 1 where he pleaded guilty.”

News.title: Brave Dad saves child from rollercoaster ‘blaze’ after kids get trapped inside tunnel filling with smoke
News.content:
'CRAZY SCREAMS' Brave Dad saves child from rollercoaster ‘blaze’ after kids get trapped inside tunnel filling with smoke







Next

A BRAVE dad was forced to step in and rescue children from a suspected roller coaster fire during a day out with his family.

Wayne Lennox, 49, took his boys, aged nine and 10, to Pleasurewood Hills near Lowestoft, Suffolk, which he had not visited since he was a child.



But, their fun Saturday out turned to terror after the egg-spress ride malfunctioned, leaving passengers trapped in a tunnel filled with smoke.

The film maker said: “We heard crazy screams, banging and things going on, but it didn’t quite register because you’re a fairground so screams are quite a regular thing.



“Then, someone started shouting: ‘The roller coaster’s stuck!’”.

Wayne, who has worked with artists like Ellie Goulding, leapt over the safety barrier to get a closer look.



Then, he said: “My two children came running out of the tunnel on foot, shouting, ‘the roller coaster’s on fire, there’s smoke everywhere!’.”

The brave dad pulled his kids to safety, but said: “When I turned around I saw this young boy, he must have been around about nine, ten himself, on the tracks.”

Wayne said he was forced to shout at the child to push himself back against the wall.

Then, he said: “All of a sudden the roller coaster was released and came streaming backwards at an insane, crazy, speed.



“But as it went shooting past the kid, I had to shout at him to pin himself against the wall, I’m screaming at him, ‘stay there, stay there, stay there’.

“Then the roller coaster flew past at a blurry speed, and then just came to a halt where it started.”

Once the passengers were back at the start of the ride, they made a terrifying revelation



Wayne said: “People were hanging out of the roller coaster.

“Everyone was crying, screaming, shouting, everyone’s shouting: ‘It’s on fire, it’s on fire!’.

“Then an adult said: ‘There’s still children in the tunnel’ and my heart dropped.”

The director, who is currently working on a scary film project, said: “I ran in there and it was like something out of a horror movie.

“There were children at the top of this tunnel, walking across the tracks and these scraggly bits of netting.



“And the whole tunnel was full of smoke, it smelled like burning rubber.”

Wayne says they have since been told by the park there was a wheel malfunction which caused the issue.

But, he said, he was horrified to learn the ride – which is suitable for children over one meter tall, was reopened the following day.

He said: “To think that they opened this ride up the following day was just beyond me.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“They are lucky there were no fatalities that day.”



The Sun has approached Pleasurewood Hills for comment.

News.title: Man City charges LIVE: Agent speaks out, punishment agreement, UEFA consider action
News.content:
Manchester City are still waiting to discover their punishment for being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules, though they have appealed the decision

Hello and welcome to Mirror Football's live blog on Wednesday, October 7, where we will bring you the latest after an independent commission found Manchester City guilty of breaking Premier League rules in a strongly-worded report released last week.

City were found to have inflated revenue by more than £830million over a nine-season period between 2009-10 and 2017-18. However, the Etihad club have since appealed against the decision and continue to deny any wrongdoing.

However, it is being reported that Premier League clubs believe City should be expelled from the top flight next season if their appeal against the financial charges fails. That’s according to Sky Sports, who are reporting that clubs in the top-flight believe a points deduction would not be sufficient if it resulted in City spending just one season outside the Premier League.

UEFA are also believed to be monitoring developments and will wait until the end of the Premier League's disciplinary process before deciding whether to take any potential action against City.

The Financial Times is reporting that HMRC probed City in 2018 over whether it used complex arrangements to underpay tax. The report claims a civil investigation into the club’s tax affairs followed the publication of leaked internal emails by Der Spiegel in 2018. The Financial Times says Man City and HMRC declined to comment.

And former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher believes City should face a multi-year punishment for their financial misdemeanours. There is still much discussion about potential outcomes, so stay right here for all of the latest...

News.title: Distracted mum killed farmer in crash as family are left with 'horrific' memory
News.content:
Distracted mum killed farmer in crash as family are left with 'horrific' memory

Mum-of-two Ami Dronsfield was driving to a hair appointment when she activated her phone for seven seconds, which meant she was unable to see Michael Armstrong's quad bike in time

View 2 Images Ami Dronsfield pictured outside court (Image: Newcastle Chronicle)

A single mum-of-two has been jailed for killing a farmer after she crashed into his quadbike while looking at her phone.

‌



‌



Ami Dronsfield was on her way to a hair appointment driving a VW Golf when she became distracted by her phone and crashed into Michael Armstrong's quad bike, causing catastrophic injuries, a court heard.

‌



Dronsfield, 36, of West Turnpike, in Glanton, Northumberland, was jailed for three years and two months after pleading guilty to causing death by dangerous driving.

‌



Newcastle Crown Court heard her phone had been active for seven seconds. She was driving south on the A697 at Whittingham and failed to spot Michael Armstrong's quad bike in time.

View 2 Images Ami Dronsfield has been jailed (Image: Northumbria Police)

Christa Pike asked two questions as soon as she woke up after botched execution READ MORE :

It was said she had not created, sent or received any messages or calls while her phone was active, but the phone had been unlocked and both WhatsApp and Snapchat had been active for a brief period, Chronicle Live reports.

‌



Judge Robert Adams said it would have been dark at the time and the light from the phone would have been distracting. The court was told that Dronsfield called 999 and appeared to be in shock after the crash. She was heard saying: "Oh my God, what if I've killed him." She tested negative for alcohol and drugs.

An investigation of her phone revealed it had been active on two occasions, both times for just seconds. At 4.59pm that day, the device was unlocked. WhatsApp was opened by pressing an icon and then closed before the phone was locked again.

The phone was illuminated again at 5.02pm, unlocked by pin code or facial recognition. Snapchat was activated briefly, for seconds, before the collision.

‌



The car's emergency brake was applied two seconds before the crash. During the time the device was active, no messages had been prepared, created, sent or received on any of the apps. And no calls had been made or received.

Judge Adams accepted it was "a very short period of distraction but with fatal consequences" and there was "no question that she failed to see the quad bike during that time".

The court heard a heartbreaking statement from Mr Armstrong's family, describing their devastation. Mrs Armstrong explained how her husband had left to see his elderly father that evening, saying "I'm off, I'll see you soon". Those were his last words to her.

‌



After hearing about the crash, Mrs Armstrong and her son made their way to the collision site and saw a scene that was "beyond horrific". Mrs Armstrong said "time will never erase that horrific scene" after she saw that "in the wreckage was my beautiful husband Michael". She had been with her husband for 28 years and described him as her best friend and soul mate.

At his bedside in hospital, the family "prayed for a miracle which deep down they knew wouldn't happen". They said their goodbyes to Mr Armstrong on his son's 21st birthday.

The court was told that Dronsfield, who was of previous good character and had worked for Northumberland County Council for 17 years, was deeply remorseful for the "devastating impact my actions have had" and wished she could turn back time.

Article continues below

She said in a letter: "I'm truly ashamed and sorry beyond words" and pointed out "how quickly one mistake can have such devastating consequences."

Dronsfield was given three years and two months in prison, of which she will serve 19 months in custody before being released on licence. She was also disqualified from driving for six years and seven months.

News.title: 'Nobody should be surprised that Reform has cleared itself of wrongdoing - the real result is yet to come'
News.content:
'Nobody should be surprised that Reform has cleared itself of wrongdoing - the real result is yet to come'

"The party can declare itself cleared, congratulate itself and move on if it likes - but this is still Reform marking Reform’s homework and awarding itself a pass"

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

Reform investigates Reform, and Reform finds Reform did nothing wrong. That should surprise nobody.

‌



‌



An internal inquiry carried out by the party secretary and a barrister linked to the party may have produced a 27-page report, but that does not make self-examination independent scrutiny. The report says no electoral laws were broken over allegations that figures discussed disguising foreign donations.

‌



Yet it also admits senior figures said things that were “wrong, careless” and, in one case, untrue. Two advisers stepped down after the undercover investigation.

‌



Scotland Yard is still looking at the allegations separately. And that is the bit Reform would rather people forget.

The party can declare itself cleared, congratulate itself and move on if it likes. But this is still Reform marking Reform’s homework and awarding itself a pass. The real test will come from outside the party.

Until the police investigation is concluded, Nigel Farage and his colleagues should spare us the victory lap. Reform may have cleared Reform. That does not make the questions or the investigation disappear.

‌



'A genuine breakthrough'

Victims should never be made to suffer twice - first from the crime, then from a justice system that leaves them waiting months or even years for their day in court.

That is why the new AI-powered Case Readiness Assistant could prove a genuine breakthrough. Spotting missing documents and problems before hearings begin could stop avoidable adjournments and help keep cases moving.

Britain’s courts are under huge pressure, and any delay adds to the anguish of victims, witnesses and families desperate for closure.

‌



Technology cannot replace judges, lawyers or proper justice. But if it can strip out needless bureaucracy and get trials started sooner, it should be used. Justice delayed is justice denied.

Victims have already waited far too long.

One walk remains

Brit Karl Bushby has taken the scenic way home - 30,000 miles, 29 countries and 28 years.

Article continues below

Now, after swimming the Channel, the adventurer is finally back on British soil. His epic journey proves what determination - and no bus fare - can achieve.

One last walk remains, and then comes the best destination of all: home.

News.title: Reform councillor 'whipping up racism' with video of protestors hurling abuse at migrants on RNLI boat
News.content:
Reform councillor 'whipping up racism' with video of protestors hurling abuse at migrants on RNLI boat

Councillor George Madgwick, the leader of Reform UK in Hampshire, was accused of "disgraceful behaviour" after he posted videos of protestors screaming "f***ing traitors" and "f*** off home" at RNLI boats carrying migrants

View 4 Images Coun George Madgwick posted the video showing the RNLI bringing migrants ashore at Gosport, Hamps (Image: x)

A Reform councillor has been accused of "whipping up racism" after posting footage of protestors hurling foul-mouthed abuse at migrants on RNLI boats.

‌



‌



Cllr George Madgwick, the leader of Reform UK in Hampshire, published a string of photos and videos as 149 migrants were picked up on Sunday in a mid-Channel rescue operation. The RNLI, alongside a French vessel, brought them ashore at Gosport, Hamps.

‌



Flares were set off and there were scuffles with police during a stand-off involving about 150 anti-migrant demonstrators. In one clip posted on X, billed as "exclusive" by Cllr Madgwick, individuals hurled expletive-laden abuse towards the RNLI boats as they arrive at the marina.

‌



View 4 Images Coun George Madgwick faced a backlash after posting expletive-laden footage on social media as migrants arrived Gosport, Hamps (Image: Jonathan Buckmasterr)

Murdered Leah Croucher's parents demand fresh law that may have stopped killer sex predator READ MORE :

Sophie Lancaster killer to walk free despite denying he took part in attack on her READ MORE :

Chants including "f***ing traitors", "f*** off home", "send them home" and "I hope you f***ing sink" can be heard as the crews pulled into the harbour. Despite the language, Cllr Madgwick wrote: "I can not believe the British Government have allowed a boat of illegal migrants to dock in the Home of the Royal Navy here in Portsmouth Harbour, Gosport.

"This makes me feel physically sick. They wonder why local people are angry. This is why. Not far right thugs. Normal local families and people horrified at what they are witnessing. When will this end?"

‌



But last night a Stand Up to Racism spokesperson said: “An elected Reform councillor is whipping up racism towards the most vulnerable people. Gosport and areas along the South Coast have seen known fascists masking up and terrorising communities.

View 4 Images Police made 12 arrests as anti-migrant protestors attempted to blockaded Gosport Marina on Sunday evening (Image: Lab Mo/SOPA Images/Shutterstock)

"Far-right Reform UK are egging them on. It’s disgraceful behaviour that is only going to fuel the fire of a fascist movement on our streets." Twelve protesters were arrested during the confrontation on Sunday evening after the boats are believed to have set off from close to Utah Beach, east Cherbourg, at 6am.

‌



It is the third boat in a month to arrive in Britain after setting off from Normandy. Boats typically depart from Calais. About 300 people gathered in Gosport to protest against the migrants' arrival. Many launched flares, with footage showing protesters enveloped in smoke.

Protesters attempted to set up barriers to stop the migrants leaving, but several coaches left the site escorted by police. The migrant dinghy is believed to have followed the route of two other dinghies that launched from Normandy last month.

View 4 Images Stand Up to Racism said behaviour at the protests "is only going to fuel the fire of a fascist movement on our streets" (Image: x)

‌



The arrival of the first vessel, carrying 114 people, prompted protests when those on board were brought ashore in Portsmouth on September 6.

A spokesman for the RNLI confirmed "two RNLI lifeboats were tasked by HM Coastguard on the central south coast of England". A Government spokesperson said: “The Border Security Command works around the clock to protect our border. We have established contingency plans to make sure we can securely disembark, check and process all small boat arrivals.

“Migrants will be transported to short term holding facilities in Kent where they will be processed as normal and undergo stringent health, security and biometric checks.” Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary said it had deployed officers to Gosport to “support our partners in the event of an emergency at sea”.

‌



It follows similar scenes last month when protesters gathered in the area expecting migrants to arrive on a dinghy, but they were ultimately taken to Dover by sea. Meanwhile, two men died and two women were injured in an attempt to cross the English Channel in a small boat.

French authorities said the men, one in his 30s and one in his 40s, died after leaving the coast at Berck overnight on Sunday. The women were taken to hospital after suffering burns over a large part of their bodies, the authorities said.

A spokesman for the Pas-de-Calais prefecture said: “An investigation has been opened by the Boulogne-sur-Mer public prosecutor’s office to determine the circumstances surrounding the deaths. François-Xavier Lauch, Prefect of Pas-de-Calais, thanks all the services involved, particularly the firefighters, for their intervention and commitment during this operation."

Article continues below

The Mirror approached Cllr Madgwick and Reform for comment.

News.title: UK's top 10 scams to look out for as online shopping fraud surges 164%
News.content:
UK's top 10 scams to look out for as online shopping fraud surges 164%

Purchase scams are on the rise, as new data reveals they are the fastest-growing scam in the UK - here are the top 10 scams you should look out for

View 3 Images Scammers are conning Brits out of thousands (Image: Getty Images)

New figures from a free scam-checking service suggest 'purchase scams' are the UK’s fastest-growing con. These scams usually involve someone paying upfront for goods or services that either don’t exist or never turn up. Over the past 12 months, checks in this category have jumped by 164%.

‌



‌



The service has also seen rises in other types of fraud. Checks for impersonation scams are up 31%, while fake security alerts — pop-ups, emails or texts designed to convince you your device is infected — have increased by 62% in the past six months.

‌



Fake messages claiming to be from delivery companies are also up 29%. Checks linked to bogus online casinos have risen by 59%, and marketplace scams on sites such as Facebook Marketplace and Etsy are up 76%.

‌



View 3 Images Purchasing scams are on the rise (Image: Getty Images)

The findings come after a poll of 2,000 UK adults, commissioned by The Co-operative Bank, found two-thirds are worried about being scammed.

Nearly two-thirds (63%) said scams are getting more sophisticated as criminals use more technology. More than half believe scams are becoming more common (57%) and harder to spot (55%). Meanwhile, 84% said they are concerned artificial intelligence is making scams look more convincing.

‌



To help customers check suspicious activity, The Co-operative Bank has teamed up with scam-checking service, Ask Silver, to launch its own scam-checker where users can upload a text message, image or website and receive guidance on whether it could be a scam.

Vishal Majithia, head of economic crime at the bank, said: "The scams we're seeing today often hide behind perfectly ordinary moments, from shopping online and tracking a parcel to receiving a message that appears to be from an organisation you trust.

"Fraudsters follow where people spend their time and money and quickly adapt their tactics to popular platforms, services and new technology.

‌



"That means anyone can be targeted, so knowing what to look out for and taking a moment to check something before you act can make all the difference."

According to the Ask Silver data, which has also revealed the top 10 trending scams in the past 12 months, the nation has seen a surge in fraudsters impersonating both everyday organisations and government agencies - an increase of 59% and 53%, respectively.

‌



There were over four million recorded online scams in 2025, according to the Office for National Statistics – with over three million adults experiencing a loss as a result.

Those who have ever been scammed have lost an average of £2850, with 60% stating that most digital scams they have encountered were disguised as everyday admin.

Elderly people are usually believed to be the most susceptible to digital scams. But, data from ONS shows those aged 25 to 44 were the most likely to fall victim to this – particularly phishing scams which involve messages from fraudsters posing as legitimate organisations to extract personal information, or money, from the victim.

‌



View 3 Images Young adults are most susceptible to digital scams (Image: Getty Images)

Alex Somervell, CEO and co-founder of Ask Silver, said: "In this digital age where scams are increasingly sophisticated, and fraudsters are highly experienced, we have to empower individuals with tools that keep them safe and allow them to communicate, shop and live with peace of mind.

"This is a deeply personal mission for me as my dad lost almost his entire life savings to scammers, and it had a devastating impact on our family, and trying to help prevent that experience for others inspires us at Ask Silver.

Article continues below

"As AI-enhanced scams accelerate the potential impact of fraud, we are using our AI-powered scam checker to fight back.

"Supporting customers at the point where individuals are parting with their hard-earned cash is where we can make a real difference, and we're delighted to be partnering with The Co-operative Bank in this way because with every scam we stop, it's another person we can keep safe."
