Sports.title: The Coldplay Kiss-Cam meets football! Female fan separates herself from 'boyfriend' in excruciating moment when cameras turned to them at Lionel Messi's Argentina farewell
Sports.content:
A female football fan was seen separating herself from her boyfriend after the couple were caught on camera during Lionel Messi's Argentina farewell.

The couple were among over 80,000 spectators present at the Estadio Monumental as Argentina paid tribute to the legendary star in a friendly against Benin.

Cameras picked out the couple during the pre-match build-up, with footage shared on social media showing the female fan realising they were being shown on the big screens.

The fan was then seen awkwardly removing her boyfriend's hand from her shoulder.

She then began adjusting her hair while glancing in his direction and exchanging words.

Football fans were quick to begin speculating about the moment on social media, with some joking it was 'Argentina's Coldplay moment'.

A female football fan was seen separating herself from her boyfriend after the couple were caught on camera during Lionel Messi's Argentina farewell

Fans joked on social media that it was Argentina's 'Coldplay moment', referencing the infamous kiss-cam which caught a a CEO and his co-worker embracing last year

Others gave a more sympathetic view of the clip, suggesting the female fan had merely wanted to adjust their hair

The comments referenced the infamous kiss-cam at a Coldplay gig last year that caught a CEO and his co-worker embracing.

'Coldplay Kiss Cam moment at Lionel Messi farewell,' one fan joked.

'It feels like she deliberately put some distance between herself and the camera once she noticed it,' another wrote.

'I feel that pain bro,' a third added.

Others, however, offered a more sympathetic view of the clip with one fan saying: 'Am I being naive to theorize that she might have just wanted his arm off her so she could fix her hair?'

The match itself proved an emotional occasion as Messi said farewell to Argentina's national team.

The 39-year-old capped his 208th and final appearance for his country with a goal and two assists as Argentina waved goodbye to its hero with a 3-0 win.

Following the game, tributes to Messi continued with an emotional musical performance before Messi took the microphone himself.

Lionel Messi played his final match for Argentina in an emotional affair in Buenos Aires

Fireworks were launched into the night sky above the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires

At the national anthem, Messi's sons - Thiago, Mateo and Ciro - joined their father

Messi scored his final goal for Argentina from the penalty spot as they earned a 3-0 win over Benin

'My dad is the first person I think about tonight,' he began, remembering his father, Jorge, who died aged 68 back in August.

'I can only thank you all. It has been a huge pride to defend this shirt for over 20 years. We never stopped fighting, never stopped giving everything. Playing for Argentina is the most beautiful thing.'

Messi's speech left supporters and players such as Enzo Fernandez struggling to contain their emotions.

'I want to thank all of my teammates. You made all of my dreams come true... I was surrounded by warriors. I'm going to miss this,' he continued.

'This may be the saddest day of my career, leaving the national team. I don't want to leave this place. I don't want to leave the field... I love all of you, and I will miss all of you. I am proud to be Argentinian.'

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola will RETURN to Man City for next week's Champions League clash against PSG - with legendary former boss to pay visit to the Etihad for the first time since summer exit after backing club over guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola will make an extraordinary first return to Manchester City next week in the wake of the bombshell verdict that has rocked the Premier League.

The former manager is set to attend Wednesday’s Champions League tie against Paris Saint-Germain, seen as a show of solidarity towards the club after they were found guilty of all but one of their charges for breaking financial rules.

Guardiola will be joined at the Etihad Stadium by the City board, including chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak, for the club’s first home European match since his summer departure.

Sources close to Guardiola had suggested on Wednesday afternoon that the 55-year-old was unsure whether the trip would be viable before a firm decision was later taken to travel over.

The Catalan’s right-hand man, Manel Estiarte, does consultancy work for City Football Group and is also expected to be in attendance.

City have lodged an appeal against the findings that they artificially inflated commercial revenues by £830million through ‘sham’ contracts with a range of Abu Dhabi-based companies.

Pep Guardiola will return to Man City for their PSG clash in a show of solidarity

Guardiola leapt to City’s defence a day after the three-person independent commission’s verdict was made public – with potential sanctions ranging from stripping the club of titles, points deductions, fines or expulsion from the top flight.

‘I want every single Manchester City fan across the world to know I am here; more than ever,’ he said in a statement.

‘I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran (Soriano), the players, staff, Enzo (Maresca) and you, our unique supporters.

‘Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all.’

That he has moved to revisit the Etihad so soon after departing is seen as a significant step. Guardiola is close with Maresca, who was his assistant during the Treble campaign, and is a City ambassador.

Maresca’s squad are back in full training on Thursday before meeting Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday in what will prove an emotionally charged day on Merseyside.

Sports.title: Birmingham City's American Revolution 2.0: How Blues fine-tuned grand plans to reach Premier League promised land - from new stadium delay to shunning Wrexham rivalry and what they learned from transfer mistakes
Sports.content:
They may not be in the Premier League yet but Birmingham City's US owners Knighthead are already working on the kind of building project usually attempted by Manchester United or Real Madrid.

Thanks to NFL great Tom Brady's investment and publicity, Birmingham are now one of the best-known English teams on the other side of the Atlantic. And an ambitious new 62,000-seat stadium plan could put them even more prominently on the map.

The reality, though, is that Blues are still in the early phase of their grand plans. After finishing 10th last season in their first season back in the second tier, they are 10th again to begin this campaign after a fearsome opening sequence of fixtures. Investment is no guarantee of escape from the Championship – just ask Wrexham – and there is still a way to go to get back to the top flight after 16 seasons away.

It won’t be any easier this weekend either, as Blues travel to Midlands rivals West Bromwich Albion, currently fifth.

Here, Daily Mail Sport looks at how close Birmingham are to realising Knighthead’s dreams – both on and off the pitch.

The ambitious plans Tom Wagner (left) and Tom Brady (right) have for Birmingham City are still in their early phase

This season has seen a tough start on the fixture list and Blues sit 10th after eight matches

Stadium delays

‘My timeframe is lunacy but we’ll look to get this completed in five years,’ said chairman Tom Wagner after he was asked when Birmingham might be playing in their new stadium.

Wagner made that assessment in April 2024 and the deadline has already been pushed back by two years to 2031. ‘Ambitious’ is perhaps a kinder word than lunacy but as more time passes without a spade in the ground, Blues fans will start to wonder.

In May, head of infrastructure Nick Smith indicated the club would submit plans to Birmingham City Council in May 2027 but they have now revised that target to the end of next year. The projected opening date is unchanged.

Building a new stadium alone is a hugely complex project and by committing to the £2-3billion ‘Sports Quarter’ vision, Birmingham have a great deal on their plate. Originally, Blues wanted the Sports Quarter to house both the training ground and a stadium for the women’s team, but that has been adjusted too. Now the club are looking for a new venue for those, ideally one location but with separate entrances and exits.

Did Wagner inadvertently set a trap for himself and the club by discussing 2029? That never looked realistic and now the further Blues push the deadline into the 2030s, the more fans become sceptical.

It is worth looking at Tottenham here. Football folk across the world admire Spurs’ state-of-the-art stadium yet few recall the length of the process. When Spurs confirmed plans to build the new ground, they had recently sacked manager Juande Ramos and appointed Harry Redknapp. That was October 2008. Spurs’ first competitive match there was not until 2019. Patience will be required here though Birmingham are confident they will realise their plans in a much shorter time than the 11 years it took Spurs.

Birmingham say the decision to relocate the training ground and women’s team stadium unlocks revenue-generating potential within the 135-acre site, with accountants Deloitte managing the land acquisition programme.

Knighthead had already proposed retail, commercial and residential buildings within the Sports Quarter and say they now have the chance to expand on that. If that works, the possible pay-off is enormous. The scheme remains hugely exciting. Until supporters can see bricks and mortar, though, they will be nervous.

Renderings of the 'Powerhouse' stadium plan. The club hope it will be ready by 2031

Blues want a 62,000-seat capacity for the new stadium, with the striking towers around it a nod to the city's industrial past

Where next?

In February, the club announced that Wagner had suffered a stroke. The 57-year-old continues to focus on his recovery and continues to engage with Knighthead and the club, while Knighthead’s leadership remain closely involved. Wagner recently returned to St Andrew’s for Blues’ 2-2 draw with Wolves, where he received an extremely warm welcome from fans.

Meanwhile, Blues’ search for a director of football continues. Daily Mail Sport can reveal that at this stage, they are looking at external candidates and John Murtough, the former Manchester United transfer chief, was high on the list. Murtough is now director of global development at Atalanta and has a compensation clause in his contract with the Serie A club.

Blues have not had a permanent director of football since Craig Gardner left in June with head of recruitment Joe Carnall taking a prominent role. Carnall has impressed many since stepping up and looks a strong candidate should Blues change tack.

Brady’s health guru Alex Guerrero continues to plan conditioning and recovery strategies from his US base, though he is rarely at the club’s training ground in rural Warwickshire. Intriguingly, many of the logos and messages from TBRx – Brady’s performance and fitness company – have disappeared from the walls of the Elite Performance and Innovation Centre.

There has also been a feeling within Blues that they have leaned too much into the rivalry with Wrexham, who also have high-profile American owners. Chris Davies’ side won 2-1 there in August and there was not the fanfare that might have greeted previous victories during the clubs’ US eras.

There has been a feeling within Blues that they have leaned too much into the rivalry with Wrexham, another ambitious Championship club with deep-pocketed US owners

Former Manchester United football director John Murtough (right) is on Blues' list of potential directors of football

This season’s targets?

Blues would never say it publicly but perhaps everyone at the club has taken a deep breath. ‘Don’t mess it up’ is one of Knighthead’s mantras when negotiating a key deal and there were times in summer 2025 where they failed to practise what they preach.

Having marched into the Championship by winning League One with 111 points, Knighthead expected to do the same in the second tier. They were confident that by 2026-27, Blues would be in the Premier League. Davies was one of the few to highlight the difficulty of winning consecutive promotions.

Blues made more sensible transfers in summer 2026 – no more huge wages for ageing players like Kyogo Furuhashi, who has been shipped out to LA Galaxy after one league goal in 28 games – and have switched to a more pragmatic style of play, with greater emphasis on set-pieces. In Colombian midfielder Jhon Solis, they have a gem who should make them a healthy profit after making his loan deal permanent.

A year ago, the club wanted to move at breakneck speed. Knighthead today seem a little older and wiser. It appears they have a better understanding of the Championship. With eighth place good enough for a play-off spot, Blues' sights are still high. Yet if they do not make it this year, they will surely be even better equipped to do so in 2027.

Sports.title: Former Newcastle director Amanda Staveley calls on Premier League rivals to 'build bridges' with Man City - as club prepare for appeal after seismic verdict over 'sham' sponsorship deals
Sports.content:
Amanda Staveley urged the Premier League to exercise caution before imposing a significant sanction on Manchester City for their financial rule breaches.

Staveley, who brokered Abu Dhabi’s £200million acquisition of City in 2008, hinted the parties should reach a settlement rather than a punishment City would inevitably contest.

City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules after a seven-year legal process which brought 115 charges.

City maintain their innocence and have appealed the ruling but could face relegation if unsuccessful. Their sanction will be decided by an independent commission where nothing is off the table.

But Staveley, who most recently was a director at Newcastle United, wants City and the Premier League to focus on ‘building bridges’ to avoid a doomsday scenario.

Speaking at sports industry conference Leaders Week London at Stamford Bridge, Staveley said: ‘You’ve got so much pressure on football. I think we should just focus on the future, getting it right and trying to build bridges with our neighbours.

Amanda Staveley wants Manchester City and the Premier League to focus on ‘building bridges’

Manchester City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules during a period of prolonged success between 2009 and 2018

‘I think it will get resolved. The Premier League had a difficult thing, an opportunity (to bring the case).

‘You've got to put yourself in their position. You've got 20 clubs. Half of them are shouting at you to do one thing, the other 10 clubs are shouting at you to do another.

‘As an executive, you're always pulled, you're always being threatened to be sued by one club.

‘Clubs are meant to be co-owners of one league. So, to navigate all of that is really tough.

‘With how important the Premier League is, we have such an exciting league.

‘European football is potentially the most watched sport in the world and we should really nurture this asset.

‘We should nurture our fans and do everything we can to resolve the issues that exist today.’

Sports.title: Jon Rahm leaves LIV Golf over 'unacceptable' terms as bankrupt breakaway tour's future suffers major blow
Sports.content:
Jon Rahm has quit LIV Golf after deeming the terms for the 2.0 version 'unacceptable'.

LIV Golf has been torn apart after the withdrawal of Saudi funding, leading to questions over the future of its stars.

The organisation has reportedly informed the majority of its staff that their jobs had been terminated in August amid the increasing uncertainty shrouding the embattled tour's future.

Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) announced it would stop funding beyond the 2026 season.

But the league, after filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, has secured a possible $300million (£227million) in financing from BC Partners Credit.

But Rahm won't be involved after his lawyer, John Beck, said Rahm 'independently reviewed the terms of LIV 2.0 and determined those terms are unacceptable as to him'.

Jon Rahm will leave LIV Golf after the terms for the 2.0 version were deemed 'unacceptable'

It is said that Rahm and LIV are now in talks over 'a consensual separation agreement between Mr Rahm and LIV'.

According to BBC Sport, players are not required to join LIV 2.0, even if they have agreed multi-year contracts.

There is an extension for the league to discuss terms with its players, which must be concluded by October 25.

Rahm has won three straight seasons in the league.

'The funding commitment announced by PIF earlier this year will reach its conclusion,' a LIV spokesman told Golf Digest. 'As a result, we are scaling back operations as we transition to the next chapter of LIV Golf and work toward making LIV 2.0 a reality.

'This week, we informed many of our colleagues that their employment under LIV 1.0 will end in the first week of September. We are grateful to our employees for their hard work and dedication in building LIV Golf, and we remain committed to supporting those affected through this transition.'

The rebel golf circuit, which launched in 2022 with the financial backing of the PIF of Saudi Arabia, paid nine-figure bonuses to lure top players like Brooks Koepka, Dustin Johnson, Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm away from the PGA Tour, offering $20million prize funds.

But it all began to fall apart earlier this year when PIF said it would no longer fund it after the 2026 season. One event in New Orleans already was scrapped.

Sports.title: Man City legend David Silva comes out of retirement aged 40 to join Hong Kong side Sha Tin
Sports.content:
Man City legend David Silva comes out of retirement aged 40 to join Hong Kong side Sha Tin

Manchester City legend David Silva has come out of retirement to sign for Sha Tin in Hong Kong.

The 40-year-old called it a day on his playing career back in 2023 when he tore his anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) while playing for Real Sociedad.

He is most famed for spending ten years at Manchester City between 2010 and 2020, where he won 11 major honours; four Premier League titles, two FA Cups and five League Cups. Much of that time period, though, is now under scrutiny.

He also has a statue outside the Etihad Stadium, and won the 2010 World Cup with Spain, as well as Euro 2008 and Euro 2012.

'I'm so excited to go to Hong Kong and enjoy the local culture, the food in Sha Tin and, of course, football in Hong Kong,' he said in an Instagram video announcing the move.

The club, meanwhile, said: 'David Silva will be in Hong Kong soon to settle in, link up with squad training, and build up to peak match fitness before making his pitch debut.'

View this post on Instagram

Manchester City legend David Silva (pictured) has come out of retirement to play for Hong Kong side Sha Tin

Silva announced his retirement from football at 37 three years ago after damaging his ACL in pre-season training.

The Real Sociedad midfielder posted a message on social media with the caption 'Thank you very much football' to confirm the end of his career.

‘Today is a sad day for me,' Silva wrote. ‘Today it is time to say goodbye to what I have dedicated my whole life to.

‘Today it is time to say goodbye to my colleagues, who are like a family to me. I will miss you very much.’

Manchester City paid tribute to their former midfielder, who played 436 matches for the club, stating that he will be remembered as 'one of the greatest players in City’s history'.

Sports.title: Former Premier League star Cheikhou Kouyate reveals he played his entire career with a 'secret' heart problem as he announces his retirement aged 36: 'I never even told my family'
Sports.content:
Former Premier League star Cheikhou Kouyate reveals he played his entire career with a 'secret' heart problem as he announces his retirement aged 36: 'I never even told my family'

Ex-Crystal Palace and West Ham midfielder Cheikhou Kouyate has revealed he played his entire career with a secret heart problem.

The 36-year-old lifted the lid on his medical issue after announcing his retirement from an impressive career in the English top flight and internationally with Senegal.

Kouyate confessed to having played for years with a health issue looming over him and even hid the diagnosis from the national team and his own family.

He says he signed insurance forms at various clubs so they would not be responsible if anything serious happened to him on the pitch.

Kouyate told Senegalese channel Walf TV: 'I suffered from this heart problem since birth. I played with it.

'In England, it was monitored every six months. I had medical check-ups at West Ham, Crystal Palace, and Nottingham Forest. Every time I had the tests, the problem reappeared.

Cheikhou Kouyate, previously pictured in hospital for an unrelated injury, has now admitted he played his entire career with a heart problem

The former Crystal Palace, West Ham and Nottingham Forest star even kept the problem a secret from his own family and has now retired from playing

'The doctors always pointed out the problem to me, but I took responsibility myself. I signed the insurance papers stating that anything that might happen to me would be my responsibility.

'Anderlecht called me [in the summer] to play there and also to start training as a coach. But after the medical examination, the doctor asked me to stop playing football.'

He went on: 'The problem is at high altitude. If I play in the heat, it hurts terribly, during and after matches.

'It feels like a side stitch, for about five minutes, and then it goes away. When it happens, after the match, I get painful cramps. After 24 hours, it stops.

'I never said anything. I didn’t want to be forced to stop early. I never told my family, not even the national team doctors. They didn’t know about my problem.'

There have been numerous tragic, fatal cardiac arrests on the pitch down the years, including Marc-Vivien Foe, Antonio Puerta and former Newcastle midfielder Cheikh Tiote.

And Kouyate, who played almost 300 games in the Premier League as a defensive midfielder, will count himself extremely fortunate not to have suffered any serious medical issues relating to his condition.

Kouyate left Nottingham Forest for Amedspor in Turkey last year but only played eight games for the club before calling it a day.

Sports.title: Southampton's spying manager Tonda Eckert is handed FA let-off with a six-week suspended ban over Spygate scandal which saw them thrown out of the play-offs for the Premier League
Sports.content:
Southampton manager Tonda Eckert has escaped a ban following the FA's investigation into Spygate. The Saints supremo has been handed a six-week expulsion from all football however, the penalty is suspended until the end of next season. Southampton were thrown out of last season's Championship play-offs after Daily Mail Sport's incredible revelation that they had spied on opponents Middlesbrough at a training session. The EFL then booted the club out of the play-offs, costing them a place in the Premier League worth a potential £200m, with a panel docking them a further four points. The FA then launched its own probe, triggering concerns that Eckert could be hit with a lengthy ban. However, he has instead been given a six-week suspension from all football which is suspended until the end of next season and handed a £28,000 fine and reprimands. 'Southampton Football Club welcomes the outcome of the FA hearing into the events at the end of last season,' a Southampton statement read. 'We hope this now brings a conclusion to a regrettable period of our history and measures have been put in place to ensure that such errors in judgement never happen again at our club. 'We want to take this opportunity to thank the supporters for their unconditional backing throughout this process. Our fan base is unmatched, and we are excited to move forward together towards a bright future.' Southampton manager Tonda Eckert has been given a six-week suspended ban over the Spygate scandal Will Salt was spotted at Middlesbrough's training ground before their Championship play-off Eckert was sanctioned for three breaches relating to spying on the training sessions of Boro, Oxford United and Ipswich Town in 2025 and 2026. Should Eckert repeat the offence, the suspension will be triggered. Boro went on to lose the play-off final to Hull City, who were promoted. The FA said that Eckert was the only witness their panel, which included two KCs, heard from and added that he was ‘exceptionally impressive’. Explaining the Oxford incident, Eckert said that their opponents had sacked Gary Rowett as head coach and appointed Craig Short as interim and that he wanted to see if they were going to play with a back four or a back five so sent someone to watch them train. In the Ipswich incident, he agreed to receive CCTV footage of them training at National League Eastleigh, ahead of their fixture with his Saints. With regards to Boro, Eckert told the panel that in a preparation meeting he asked whether it would be possible to find out if Hayden Hackney had resumed training. ‘One of the assistants informed me that Middlesborough FC’s [sic] training ground is located on a golf course which is accessible to the public,’ he added. ‘I said that we should send someone there to see if Hayden Hackney was training. Nobody expressed any reservations or objections to this proposal. 'The exchange took a matter of minutes and then we continued with the meeting. To confirm I did not ask for any videos to be taken of Middlesborough FC’s [sic] training sessions and I did not identify any particular individual to travel to Middlesborough [sic] to identify if Hayden Hackney was training. I do, however, accept that I was wrong to ask for any kind of observations.’ An intern was sent to the venue, who was subsequently spotted by Boro – who complained to the EFL – but not before Eckert had been ‘provided a breakdown of the videos… including the predicted line up. ‘I had already finished preparing for the match,’ he said, ‘but I watched the videos’. The panel praised Eckert, 33, for his ‘genuine contrition’. He had argued that during his time in Germany and Italy, spying on training sessions of opponents was ‘commonplace’, that he was unaware it was against the rules in England and said that allegations he had bullied younger members of staff into spying were ‘extremely upsetting’, adding that he would have never have forced anyone to do anything to which they had a moral objection, let alone a breach of the rules. The panel found there was no ‘systemic or organised course of action’ with regards to spying, and found ‘considerable mitigation’ with regards to Eckert who had shown ‘deep and meaningful’ remorse and ‘learned lessons’. TIMELINE: THE SPY-GATE SAGA May 7 — Daily Mail Sport reveals the spying allegation Daily Mail Sport reported that a Southampton first-team analyst had allegedly been caught hiding in bushes near Middlesbrough's training ground while recording a session ahead of their Championship play-off semi-final. The incident became known as 'Spygate 2.0'. May 8 — Southampton are charged by the EFL The EFL charged Southampton with breaching regulations requiring clubs to act in 'the utmost good faith' and prohibiting them from observing an opponent's training within 72 hours of a match. The report identified the suspected spy as a junior intern and said he had allegedly deleted footage before leaving the site. May 10 — Southampton manager refuses to discuss the affair Manager Tonda Eckert walked out of a tense post-match press conference after refusing to answer questions about the spying allegations, while Middlesbrough's manager publicly criticised Southampton. May 13 — Evidence emerges of the suspected operation Daily Mail Sport published an image apparently showing the Southampton analyst hiding behind a tree and filming Middlesbrough's training. The report also raised questions about a possible paper trail linking the operation to the club. May 14–15 — EFL signals Southampton could be removed from the play-offs The EFL confirmed that Southampton could be expelled from the play-offs, with a disciplinary hearing scheduled just days before the final. Middlesbrough then called publicly for Southampton to be removed from the competition, describing expulsion as the 'only appropriate response'. May 19 — Southampton are expelled from the play-off final An independent disciplinary commission expelled Southampton from the Championship play-offs and imposed a four-point deduction for the following season. Southampton admitted spying on Middlesbrough and two other opponents — Oxford United and Ipswich Town — while Middlesbrough were reinstated to face Hull City in the final. May 20–21 — Southampton lose their appeal and player anger surfaces Southampton's appeal against expulsion was rejected, confirming that Middlesbrough would take their place in the Wembley final. Southampton players publicly expressed their anger and disappointment, while the potential loss of promotion bonuses prompted reports that some could consider legal action against the club. June 1–2 — Leaked messages intensify scrutiny of the club A leaked WhatsApp exchange appeared to show an intern being praised after a spying mission, with the message: 'You legend. Manager loved it!'. The revelations raised fresh questions about pressure placed on junior staff and Eckert's knowledge of the operations. July 22 — The FA charges Tonda Eckert The FA charged Eckert with three breaches of its misconduct rules relating to spying on opposition training. Daily Mail Sport reported that he was expected to cooperate with the investigation and could face a lengthy ban if found guilty. September 21 — Southampton seek leniency ahead of the FA hearing Southampton asked the FA to take into account the punishment already imposed by the EFL — expulsion from the play-offs and a four-point deduction — as Eckert's disciplinary hearing approached. The club acknowledged that staff had been sent to observe Oxford, Ipswich and Middlesbrough training sessions. October 7 - Eckert is handed a suspended six-week ban by the FA Southampton owner Dragan Solak added: 'I'm pleased that the independent panel has come to a decision and that we have an outcome. We have already suffered enough, and we appreciate the panel's recognition of that. 'We are confident the manager has learned from this matter, and a suspended sentence allows him to continue in his role. I firmly believe that Tonda is one of Europe's most exciting young coaches, and with this distraction removed, I am confident he can lead the team to a successful season. 'I'd like to thank our fans for standing by us and showing the team so much support during a time when we have needed them more than ever. 'The FA process has been a positive experience. Tonda has been given the opportunity to be open and honest with the panel, and the panel has been able to see that he is simply a good person who made poor decisions. 'The same cannot be said for the EFL process, and the way they have subsequently treated us is not something we will forget. However, now is the time to look forward to what I believe will be a great future for our club.' Before the verdict, Southampton had already lined up former Wolves and Middlesbrough boss Rob Edwards to potentially step in if Eckert's ban was lengthy. Eckert had pleaded for sympathetic handling, telling the BBC this week that the club have already had a 'big, big punishment' while Saints chief executive Phil Parsons said: 'What we hope as a club is they (the FA panel) actually recognise where we are at the moment, and what we've already been through, because I think it has to be taken into account. 'I really feel like we've taken enough. We've been hurt. I think it's one of the largest sanctions ever when it comes to football, or even sporting, history.'

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury fight start time confirmed
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury fight start time confirmed

The Principality Stadium will host the biggest fight in British boxing history, with the bout being billed as taking place on Friday, December 11

View 2 Images Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua (Image: Getty Images for Netflix)

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are set for a 1am ring walk in their heavyweight boxing clash in Cardiff.

‌



‌



The Principality Stadium will host the biggest fight in British boxing history, with the bout being billed as taking place on Friday, December 11. However, the expected schedule for the showdown has now been revealed, which will see the main event take place in the early hours of Saturday morning UK time.

‌



An application to Cardiff Council confirmed the ring walk is planned to start at around 1am, after a short live music performance, and the stadium will remain open until 3.30am. Those timings would suit peak viewing time in the United States, with Saudi Arabia’s boxing supremo Turki Alalshikh, his American business partner Dana White and broadcasters Netflix having originally pushed for New York’s Madison Square Garden as the venue.

‌



Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua tickets prices revealed for mega-fight READ MORE :

Tyson Fury to make Donald Trump offer for Anthony Joshua fight READ MORE :

Despite Cardiff being announced as the venue last month, required changes to its premises licence to allow the early-hours fight to go ahead have yet to be secured. In a bid to obtain the necessary permissions, Millennium Stadium plc has applied to the council to extend timings at the venue “on a very limited one-off occasion”.

The application seeks to extend permitted hours for boxing and wrestling entertainment from an existing cut-off of 1am to 3am on December 12. A council spokesperson said: “This is to facilitate the proposed Anthony Joshua v Tyson Fury bout, with the ring walk commencing at 0100.”

‌



The licence variation seeks an extension for live music on the same date, to facilitate a short live performance immediately before the ring walk. It also proposes an extension for recorded music, late-night refreshment and supply of alcohol until 3am, with the stadium closing time being moved to 3.30am.

The applicants added that the roof will be shut throughout the event and enhanced security and stewarding arrangements will be in place. An application to vary a premises licence must be advertised, including by displaying a notice at or on the premises, for 28 consecutive days.

View 2 Images Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua face off (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

Members of the public and other authorities may make an objection to the Principality Stadium application, or a comment in support, until November 3. If no relevant representations are received, the council must grant the application. If objections are made then a council hearing will be held to consider them.

This may result in modifications to the conditions of the licence, or the application may be refused altogether. After the fight was announced last month, Cardiff Council leader Chris Weaver said: “The contest at Principality Stadium has the potential to bring significant economic benefits to the city and attract visitors from across the UK and beyond.

“Major events provide a welcome boost for local businesses, support jobs and showcase Cardiff to a global audience. “There are still some arrangements to be finalised with the organisers, including any required changes to Principality Stadium’s premises licence, but we are looking forward to welcoming fans to the city for what promises to be an unforgettable night of boxing.”

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel fires clear warning to Cole Palmer after Chelsea star misses England camp
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel has sent a warning to the likes of Cole Palmer and Co: the England train is leaving without you.

Chelsea star Palmer pulled out of the England squad for the Nations League campaign, while Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo, Declan Rice and Tino Livramento also withdrew. They now face a fight to get back into Tuchel’s plans because the England boss says the “train is rolling” and is moving on without them.

Tuchel made it very clear that he will keep faith with the players who were part of this four-game camp and will reward their loyalty and commitment. That will come as a stark warning for Palmer in particular as Tuchel has already said the Chelsea star misses “way too many opportunities for England.”

England have also found a way to win and play with style without Palmer, Rashford and Phil Foden as they are as good as qualified for the knock-out stages of the Nations League next March.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

When asked if they face a battle to get back in, Tuchel said: “It’s always like this. This is how it has to be. Everyone should be eager to come, desperate to come because the train is rolling and the train is rolling and full credit to the players who bought into that.

“It can only work like this. We can only put our full energy into the camp and the players who are in camp makes the camp special. This will never change.”

‌



Tuchel also admitted that he “does not know” whether Foden and Palmer would work in England’s high octane style of football which saw them beat Czech Republic twice and also smash seven past Croatia. He added: “I don’t know, is the honest answer. They are not here. This team took another step and it’s always about the guys who are here.”

View 5 Images Thomas Tuchel has taken a firm stance with his players (Image: Eddie Keogh - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

That message was clear enough and Tuchel is certain to keep that in mind ahead of naming his squad for next month’s final two Nations League games with Croatia and Spain.

If England beat Croatia then it will set up a final game decider in Spain on November 15 as to who finishes top of the group to get home advantage.

‌



The Nations League quarter-final draw is on November 20 in Nyon while the Euro 2028 qualifying draw is in Belfast on December 6.

Palmer was left out of Tuchel's squad for the World Cup in the summer and hasn't played for his country since a friendly against Japan in March. He has earned 14 caps so far, scoring twice, including in England's Euros final defeat by Spain in 2024.

View 5 Images Marcus Rashford also withdrew from England duty (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Rashford was a key part of Tuchel's plans at the World Cup and boasts 19 goals in 78 caps, but has seen Anthony Gordon establish himself as the first-choice on the left wing over the past few weeks.

‌



His United team-mate Mainoo was an unused member of England's squad at the World Cup. The 21-year-old will have taken note of Alex Scott's impressive performances after the Bournemouth midfielder was handed a debut by Tuchel.

Meanwhile, Tuchel says England have “unlocked” a new way of playing with extra style, flair and all-out attack. They beat the Czech Republic twice and smashed seven past Croatia.

England lost to Spain but have finished the camp with Tuchel believing they are in a better place now in their first round of games since the World Cup.

That ended in disappointment after the semi-final defeat to Argentina and question marks about England’s DNA and becoming too defensive. But Tuchel says many of his questions have been answered by the players and their attacking approach.

‌



View 5 Images England have been in fine goalscoring form recently (Image: Eddie Keogh - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

He said: “It was on a very high level. Football on a high level, football that suits us, attacking football, a lot of high ball wins and we took some calculated risks in the ‘man-on-man’ approach in the opponents’ half.

“We did it in all four games and we had four good performances, if unfortunately not four wins. We didn’t beat Spain but it was always about the reaction and that was on a high level. It’s shown me how we react in the next camps after a tournament. I have never done a big tournament or a big camp after a tournament.

“It was new for me and brilliant to see how everyone bought into the idea of the next steps and the details needed to adjust to maybe unlock the next level. I love this group of players because the attitude and commitment is of the highest level.”

‌



Tuchel believes the new style comes from “slight adjustments” in training and the chance to build on their “strong foundations” but he insists they did not want to completely reinvent themselves.

View 5 Images Alex Scott impressed for England (Image: Michael Regan - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

Instead, England have clearly used Jude Bellingham further forward alongside Harry Kane, the two wingers almost make it a front four and the two midfielders at the base of the team are very important.

Scott - injured for the second Czech Republic game - has made a big impression as Tuchel called him “really excellent” with the same praise going to Lewis Hall who made England more balanced from left-back.

‌



That midfield duo could be key with the right partnership. One to hold, one to drive forward and Tuchel said Scott was “super strong” and on a “completely new level.” His partnership with Elliot Anderson in Croatia was a benchmark for the future.

Sports.title: How 'exceptionally impressive' Tonda Eckert avoided serious FA punishment for Spygate
Sports.content:
Tonda Eckert must have breathed a huge sigh of relief when he discovered the outcome of the FA's investigation into his role in the Spygate scandal.

The FA announced on Wednesday that the Southampton manager had been fined £28,000 and given a suspended six-week ban from football. It means the 33-year-old manager will continue on the touchline as normal for Sunday's South Coast Derby against Portsmouth.

Eckert will avoid any further sanction, provided he does isn't found to be “requesting, authorising, taking or using information" from a rival team's training session before the end of the 2027/28 season.

The mood at Southampton was jubilant and shown by the club's Twitter account sharing a video of Eckert celebrating in front of fans after a win at St Mary's Stadium. Having feared a potentially season-altering punishment, Saints are left feeling vindicated for backing Eckert.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The independent commission's verdict also draws a huge contrast between the two punishments, after the EFL ejected Saints from last season's play-off final and imposed a four-point deduction for spying on three opponents' training sessions.

So how did the FA arrive at such a punishment? Mirror Football has read the independent regulatory commission's written reasons and tells you all you need to know.

'Exceptionally impressive witness'

The FA's charge against Eckert of bringing the game into disrepute came after the EFL's harsh punishment against the club. It was just the 33-year-old German being judged in this case, and he made a very good impression of the commission.

‌



Eckert was the only person that the FA heard from directly. He was interviewed on July 2 and appears to have helped his case a great deal, in stark contrast to the previous EFL disciplinary commission, who were left "unimpressed" by him.

View 4 Images Tonda Eckert helped his case by being interviewed (Image: Matt Watson/Southampton FC via Getty Images)

The commission notes that Eckert was an "exceptionally impressive witness" and that he had shown "a remarkable degree of introspection and reflection" on his wrongdoing, having admitted the charges against him.

It was noted that he had "reflected very deeply and seriously on what had happened" and had gone to "quite extraordinary lengths not simply to learn the rules but also to understand why the rules are as they are". That is linked to Eckert's mitigation that he wasn't aware of the FA's rules against spying on rivals' training sessions, which is commonplace in Germany and Italy, where he previously worked.

‌



There was particular mention of the hurt Eckert had felt due to the perception that he had bullied a junior member of staff into doing the spying against his will. "Our clear impression was that his level of contrition was as deep and meaningful as could reasonably be expected of any individual," the commission notes.

No deterrent allowed

View 4 Images The FA's case against Jurgen Klopp in 2022 was referred to (Image: Nigel French/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

Many people had called for Eckert to be made an example of. They wanted the Saints boss to receive a very harsh punishment, so as to draw a line in the sand and stamp out any other offending.

But the commission's report makes clear that it isn't allowed to impose harsher sanctions on that basis. It refers to the FA's case against Jurgen Klopp in 2022, when the FA appealed against the commission's punishment for the then Liverpool manager.

‌



Klopp was fined £30,000 for berating officials and being sent off against Manchester City, prompting the FA to seek further punishment. He was subsequently handed a one-match ban. Back then there had also been calls for a deterrent punishment, but the same outcome arose.

No real precedent

The commission notes previous cases, such as the EFL fining Leeds £200,000 for Marcelo Bielsa spying in 2019 and the Canadian women's team spying at the 2024 Olympic Games, but says "we were not referred to any precedent which may be relevant on sanction".

Eckert was guilty of "a very serious offence" but is given credit for admitting the charges and showing contrition for his mistakes, which were sending a member of staff to watch Oxford and Middlesbrough training sessions and accepting CCTV footage of Ipswich training at nearby Eastleigh before a match.

View 4 Images Marcelo Bielsa previously spied on opponents while Leeds manager (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA, Getty Images)

‌



Avoiding double jeopardy

The FA sought a three-month ban from football for Eckert, but that was deemed too severe by the commission because it would likely result in the German losing his job and it would unfairly impact upon the club's fans. The commission felt a touchline ban would not go far enough, because it is usually handed out as punishment for an in-game offence.

The commission notes: "We do not consider that the perceived pressure undoubtedly felt by junior members of staff can be laid at Mr Eckert’s door and although there are three rule breaches, we do not consider there was a systematic or organised course of conduct."

Eckert's "genuine contrition", "exemplary" cooperation and "unprompted multiple apologies" helped his case immeasurably. His desire to make sure nothing similar happens again and that his staff feel comfortable raising concerns also worked in his favour.

The fact that the EFL had already ejected Saints from the play-off final and imposed a four-point penalty for the 2026/27 season also weighed heavily: "unquestionably [it would] be the equivalent of a further sanction being imposed on them if their head coach was unavailable for a period of six weeks in the Championship season".

‌



"We consider that this is a clear and compelling reason to suspend that part of the sanction which comprises the ban from all football and football related activity."

Sports.title: Man Utd, Arsenal, Liverpool and Tottenham told of Man City guilty verdict early
Sports.content:
Man Utd, Arsenal, Liverpool and Tottenham told of Man City guilty verdict early

Manchester City were found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges brought against them by the Premier League for financial breaches

View 2 Images Man City were found guilty of 114 charges (Image: Molly Darlington - WSL/WSL Football via Getty Images)

Several Premier League clubs were reportedly already aware of Manchester City’s guilty verdict before it was officially announced. Manchester United, Liverpool, Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur were apparently informed of the verdict before it was made public.

‌



‌



The Premier League confirmed last week that City had been found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges brought against the club for financial breaches.

‌



City maintain their innocence and submitted an appeal last week before the Friday deadline, where they insist they have “a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence” that clears them of any wrongdoing.

‌



The wait now goes on for the outcome of the appeal, which will be overseen by an independent three-person panel, with a decision expected before the end of the year.

‌



The Telegraph have reported that four Premier League clubs were informed of the verdict before the rest of the top flight were sent an email on September 25.

Liverpool, Manchester United, Arsenal and Tottenham all put into motion potential legal action back in 2024, which could see the clubs entitled to compensation in the event that the verdict against City remains guilty after the appeal.

It now remains to be seen what any compensation could result in, with the exact outcome of the case against City also uncertain.

‌



A list of punishments have been mentioned that could be given to City in the event their appeal is unsuccessful, including fines, transfer bans, points deductions, titles being stripped and expulsion from the Premier League.

City are still maintaining their innocence and issued a statement last week confirming they had submitted the appeal in response to the verdict.

View 2 Images Manchester City submitted their appeal last week (Image: Getty Images)

‌



“Manchester City Football Club can confirm that at 7pm on Thursday 1st October 2026 the Club lodged its comprehensive Appeal against the opinion of the Premier League Commission, in relation to the Premier League disciplinary matter,” the statement from City read.

“The Club’s firm position is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe.

“The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.

Article continues below

“We will continue to respect due process and are necessarily restricted in what we can say further until all proceedings are complete.”

Sports.title: Coolmore partners pay £4.2 million for colt who is 'spitting image of Frankel'
Sports.content:
Coolmore partners pay £4.2 million for colt who is 'spitting image of Frankel'

The yearling son of the great Frankel fetched the second highest sum paid at the Tattersalls October Yearling Sale, book one, when he went through the ring in Newmarket

View 3 Images Lot 237: described as the 'spitting image of Frankel' (Image: Tattersalls)

The Coolmore partners paid £4.2 million to buy a colt described as the 'spitting image of Frankel' on Wednesday.

‌



‌



After day one of the Tattersalls October Yearling Sale, book one, belonged to Sheikh Mohammed, who spent £15.6 million on ten new recruits for his Godolphin stable, day two belonged to his rivals.

‌



The ruler of Dubai had gone to £4.8m to secure a colt by Night Of Thunder on Tuesday, then 24 hours later MV Magnier, with White Birch Farm, made a statement purchase for his operation with the winning bid a colt by the late Sir Henry Cecil's legendary galloper.

‌



Horse suffers fatal injury after head-on collision with outrider after making winning debut READ MORE :

Consigned by Newsells Park Stud, the colt became the third progeny out of the mare Shambolic in five years to make seven figures. Her first foal, Ylang Ylang - also snapped up by Coolmore - went on to triumph in the Fillies' Mile after being purchased for £1.5m, while her half-brother Act Of Kindness was bought by Godolphin for £3.8m in 2024.

Graham Smith-Bernal, owner of Newsells Park, told Tattersalls: "When you have your stud manager, who's been there for 20 years, describe this horse as the finest horse he's ever produced, and you have Juddmonte, who's visited him a couple of times, saying he is the spitting image of Frankel...

‌



View 3 Images (Image: Tattersalls)

"For me, it was his temperament that was so special. Right from when he was weaned, he was a horse more interested in interacting with humans rather than other horses. You'd click your fingers, he'd come walking over from 400 yards away. You could see he wanted to know what you're all about. He vetted very well, he moves very well and he is just so special.

"He looks like Frankel, and if he's 10 per cent of what Frankel was I think the new owner will have done quite well. I wish them all the best. Of course, they [Coolmore] have already done well with the family through Ylang Ylang. In my book, anyway, this colt is couple of notches up from her. We wish them all the very best."

Article continues below

View 3 Images Graham Smith-Bernal: owner of Newsells Park Stud (Image: Laura Green)

Magnier said: "He's a lovely horse and in fairness to Newsells they do a great job. They've bred a lot of good horses, including his sister, who we bought here a few years ago. She was a very good filly, she's in-foal to Justify.

"Aidan (O'Brien) and dad (John Magnier) were here the other day, and they both liked him a lot. All the lads were happy to get him."

Sports.title: Women's Cycling has been transformed by TV backing claims Olympic champion
Sports.content:
Women's Cycling has been transformed by TV backing claims Olympic champion

Dani Rowe believes support from TV channels has made an important difference in growing the sport

View Image Dani Rowe believes TV support has helped transform women's cycling

Women's cycling is the perfect example of how serious investment by a broadcaster can transform a sport, in the view of Olympic champion Dani Rowe.

‌



‌



Amid recent criticism that BBC Sport is diminishing the visibility of Olympic sports to place a greater focus on Premier League football, the growth of women’s cycling has been welcome news for those whose sporting consumption is not solely restricted to the round ball.

‌



This weekend, Demi Vollering followed up her Tour de France Femmes win by being crowned world champion on the road in Montréal but only after an almighty battle in Canada. And with both events drawing huge crowds, both on the ground and on television – with TNT Sports covering the race in the UK – it was the latest example of how quickly women’s cycling is growing.

‌



Rowe, who won team pursuit gold for Team GB at London 2012, alongside Dame Laura Kenny and Joanna Rowsell, enjoyed success of her own on the road, including a Commonwealth bronze medal in the road race in 2018.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

But in her new role as a broadcaster with TNT, she explained that the sport has been transformed since she retired the same year, and cites it as proof that initial investment can make all the difference.

‌



“I think I can see both sides of the argument because I really understand that it's an industry and, the money in the sport is determined by bums on seats and eyes on the TV,” said Rowe, speaking at the Cycle Exchange in Kingston, the destination for buying, selling or exchanging premium used bikes.

“But I also understand how influential the growth of a sport is with the coverage, and that has been so obvious within women's cycling. It's unrecognisable from where it was when I stopped racing, and that's purely down to the coverage that we've got now.

“For other sports, I wouldn't be able to tell you exactly what TNT is showing compared to the BBC. But of course it's going to have a detrimental effect on the sport because ultimately it's a snowball effect, right? If it's not on the TV, it's not going to have the investment, so the sport's not going to grow, not going to have the professionalism.”

‌



The transformation in women’s cycling has been dramatic, with the Tour de France Femmes having only come into existence in 2022 – previously there was a one or two-day race known as La Course.

Huge investment has followed, allowing an increasingly large professional peloton, and while Rowe would have loved for it to happen sooner so she could have competed in front of such crowds, she is thrilled to see how far the sport has come.

She added: “Look at it now. You know, we've got £10,000 contracts. The strength in depth of the peloton now is massive. We're having races that weren't on the calendar. Like the fact that there's now a Tour de France for women and the viewing figures that they've got for it as well. It's just further proof that this racing is worth being shown.

Article continues below

“This has been a long time coming, yeah. There was always this potential. And it just took someone to say let’s go. It is brilliant. And it's nice. I'm still very much within the sport to be able to enjoy that too and see the changes.

“It just meant I could never earn as much money, but that's life, isn't it? That's the way it is. And I'm really glad that these women now have got these opportunities to showcase how good they are because they're absolutely elite.”
