Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora Claims More Toughness Than Jaron Ennis
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora feels he has more dog in him than Jaron Ennis. He plans to use relentless pressure alongside nonstop punching to neutralize what makes Boots lethal at 154 pounds.

Fundora wants a unification clash right after his October 17 defense against Ermal Hadribeaj. Ennis sits near the top of his target list, with Fundora already visualizing his battle plan.

“Pain, man. We bring the pain. I know I could beat him,” Fundora said to Sean Zittel. “Whether it is our awkward style that everybody loves to say or the fact that we throw a lot of punches, but we definitely have, I think we have more dog in us.”

When Zittel noted that Ennis proved his grit before, Fundora didn’t budge.

“That is fine, man. That is fine. Well, you showed it for like a round. I have been showing it my whole career.”

Fundora clearly believes he can drag Ennis into the trenches. Firing continuous punches could push Boots past his comfort zone, especially if Fundora unloads immediately after Ennis finishes flurrying.

That strategy cuts both ways. Stepping inside opens clean lanes for Ennis to time nasty counters. Fundora might gladly trade leather, but absorbing heavy shots eventually drains anyone trying to march forward.

The real test comes down to controlling the pace. Boots doesn’t need to sit in the pocket just to prove his chin. If he slips off the center line, he can crack Fundora before the big man ever finds his rhythm.

Fundora’s attitude injects genuine heat into this potential matchup. He wants to test the challenger on pure grit, finding out what happens when Boots faces someone who never stops pressing forward.

Nothing is signed yet. Fundora has to take care of business against Hadribeaj first, but he’s already put Boots on notice if unification happens.

Sports.title: Janibek Alimkhanuly and Jacob Bank Agree Title Fight
Sports.content:
Janibek Alimkhanuly found his path to a 168-pound crown after Hamzah Sheeraz vacated the belt instead of facing him. The Kazakh southpaw will battle Denmark’s Jacob Bank for the vacant WBO super middleweight championship after both camps reached an agreement.

WBO president Gustavo Olivieri confirmed the deal on X Wednesday. An official date along with a host location will arrive soon, as both camps formally notified the sanctioning organization that terms are locked in without needing a purse bid.

Olivieri stated that the WBO received formal written notification from Team Zhanibek Alimkhanuly plus Team Jacob Bank that both sides settled terms to contest the vacant crown, with further details coming in due course.

Sheeraz’s exit shuffled the deck for Janibek, yet the prize remains intact. Rather than hunting down the British titlist, the former unified middleweight kingpin squares off with a fresh, hungry challenger aiming for his first world championship. The sanctioning body initially ordered talks between top contender Janibek and the third-ranked Bank as soon as the belt opened up.

Bank comes into the fight sporting an unblemished record featuring 20 victories, 11 coming inside the distance. The Danish contender stayed busy with three wins already in 2026, creating genuine momentum heading into the biggest night of his career. Taking on an elite southpaw who ruled the 160-pound division demands everything he has.

Stepping up to super middleweight brings real curiosity for Janibek. Dominating middleweight proved his pedigree, but he must prove his firepower carries into a heavier weight category. Bank brings size, hunger, plus momentum to make life rough for the favorite.

Claiming this vacant belt crowns Janibek as a two-division champion. He kept his title shot alive after Sheeraz walked away, so taking care of Bank seals the mission.

If Janibek collects the WBO belt, he instantly becomes one of the highest-risk, lowest-reward targets in the entire division. He may have to rely on sanctioning body mandatories or take on the top contenders from Europe to get anyone to sign on the dotted line.

Sports.title: Andy Cruz Gets More Time for IBF Title Talks
Sports.content:
Andy Cruz’s team and Artur Subkhankulov’s have reportedly been negotiating until October 20 to reach an agreement for the vacant IBF lightweight title. Cruz has another opportunity to become champion, although winning the belt would leave his defeat to Raymond Muratalla unresolved.

“The teams of Cuba’s Andy Cruz and Russia’s Artur Subkhankulov have been granted an extension until October 20 to reach a deal for their vacant IBF lightweight world title bout,” journalist Carlos Linares reported on X.

The IBF initially gave the sides until October 7 to negotiate. Muratalla vacated the championship to move up in weight, opening the route for No. 1 contender Subkhankulov and No. 2 Cruz to fight for it. A date and venue have yet to be announced.

Cruz lost a majority decision to Muratalla in January and had wanted a rematch. Instead, he now has the opportunity to collect the championship without facing the fighter who beat him. That would be a useful recovery for his career, but the belt alone wouldn’t establish that he had surpassed Muratalla.

For Cruz, the immediate priority is securing the fight and making the most of another title opening. Waiting for Muratalla to return to lightweight would offer no guarantee of a rematch. Becoming champion would give Cruz something to bring into negotiations for other significant fights.

Subkhankulov has his own opportunity to change how he is viewed. The unbeaten Russian is 12-0 with six knockouts, while Cruz is 7-1 with four. Subkhankulov’s ranking has put him within reach of a championship, but Cruz represents a considerable increase in opposition.

Cruz’s Olympic gold medal and extensive amateur success give him experience against talented opponents. His loss to Muratalla nevertheless showed that those credentials don’t guarantee professional title victories.

The extension gives both teams additional negotiating time. It doesn’t guarantee an agreement, and Cruz still needs to beat Subkhankulov before discussing what a championship could bring. For now, his second title chance remains a fight to be finalized.

Sports.title: Derek Chisora Makes Excuses for Moses Itauma’s Defeat
Sports.content:
Derek Chisora claims outside pressure forced Moses Itauma into hunting for another knockout against Filip Hrgovic. That take lets Itauma off way too easily. The real issue sits with his engine during a grueling contest.

“Everybody said he was going to win the fight before he walked in the ring. So, there was so much pressure on him for him to win with a knockout,” Chisora said during an interview at the IBA press conference in Istanbul.

Chisora argued Itauma didn’t run out of gas, claiming his body shut down instead. Call it whatever you want, but Itauma hit an absolute wall once Hrgovic took his best shots. Getting stopped in round nine revealed flaws earlier blowout wins managed to hide.

Chasing a highlight reel finish explains part of the early rush, sure. Still, elite fighters must handle that noise. When an opponent absorbs punishment without budging, a top heavyweight can’t simply run out of fuel.

Take a hard look at Itauma’s path before this bout. Fast wins over aging veterans looked great on paper, but they never prepared him for a battle-tested opponent who punches back. Blasting someone out in two rounds requires entirely different stamina than fighting deep into the night.

His amateur background brings similar concerns. Trophies in the junior ranks never proved he could survive twelve rounds against a rugged pro. Matchmakers needed to build that ring time gradually, yet quick stoppages kept masking the unknown.

His thick muscular build raises legitimate questions about stamina management. That build doesn’t automatically cap him at six rounds, but problems clearly surfaced once Hrgovic dragged him past familiar territory.

Chisora can back his guy without spinning the loss into something harmless. If Itauma burned his gas tank chasing an early finish, his corner must fix that habit. If his cardio can’t handle that pace, training camp requires serious adjustments.

Dressing up exhaustion as some mysterious shutdown won’t help Itauma next time he meets someone who can take a shot.

Sports.title: Denzel Bentley Claims Strong Case to Bypass Yoenli Hernandez
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley believes he has a good case for the WBO to let him defend against Shane Mosley Jr. instead of mandatory challenger Yoenli Hernandez. If his appeal is rejected, he could give up the belt and go ahead with his planned Zuffa Boxing debut against Mosley Jr.

“I think because it went to purse bids it’s making it a bit difficult at this point. I think we do have a good case,” Bentley told Sky Sports.

Bentley believes he should get nine months as WBO champion before having to face his mandatory. He says his team disputed the order before the purse bid because they were already planning a voluntary defense. The WBO has yet to decide his appeal.

He is scheduled to fight Mosley on November 7 at London’s Copper Box Arena, on the Zuffa Boxing 12 card headlined by Chris Billam-Smith against Chev Clarke.

Hernandez’s promoter, Warriors Boxing, won the purse bid with a $200,000 offer. Queensberry attended without bidding, giving Warriors the right to stage Bentley’s mandatory defense.

Bentley has signed a multi-fight deal with Zuffa, and the Mosley Jr. fight is already arranged. If keeping his WBO belt means facing Hernandez next, he could give it up and pursue Zuffa’s own title instead.

Mosley Jr’s stoppage win over Serhii Bohachuk makes him a credible challenger, but he still looks the more winnable opponent for Bentley. Hernandez brings greater danger with his power. Bentley could lose his belt to the Cuban and take a beating that leaves him struggling to rebuild his career.

Mosley could beat Bentley as well, but he relies more on his boxing and looks less likely to batter him the way Hernandez might. Giving up the WBO title would allow Bentley to start his Zuffa deal against an opponent he has a better chance of beating.

Bentley has made no official move to surrender his belt. Keeping the hardware remains his primary goal, yet Hernandez earned his mandatory position through the proper channels. Signing with a new promoter clarifies Bentley’s motives, but it gives the challenger zero reason to step aside.

Sports.title: Callum Smith Signs Contract for Dmitry Bivol Fight
Sports.content:
Callum Smith has signed the documents for a title fight against Dmitry Bivol, according to RCC Boxing, with December 12 as the planned date in Yekaterinburg, Russia. The promoter’s announcement moves the matchup forward, although the date should still be treated as provisional.

RCC Boxing CEO German Titov told the organization’s press service that negotiations with Smith’s team had concluded, according to RBC Sport.

“Today we completed lengthy negotiations with Callum Smith’s team,” Titov said, translated from Russian.

Titov added that the necessary documents had been signed and RCC would organize the championship bout in Yekaterinburg. His wording on December 12 was “the planned date,” leaving room for further confirmation before fans make travel arrangements.

Smith is Bivol’s WBO mandatory challenger and holds the organization’s interim light heavyweight title. The British fighter’s route gives Bivol another title obligation to handle while a third meeting with Artur Beterbiev remains an attractive option.

The contract announcement is progress, but it comes from the company organizing the event. It supports reporting that RCC says Smith has signed. It does not justify turning a planned December date into an unconditional promise that the fight will happen that night.

For Smith, the opportunity would bring another attempt to win a full world title at light heavyweight after his defeat to Beterbiev. Bivol presents a different challenge: Smith would have to find ways to land his heavier punches against an opponent whose movement and combinations can leave challengers chasing rounds.

Smith cannot afford to spend long stretches following Bivol without throwing. Letting the champion dictate the distance would make it difficult to bring his power into the fight, particularly if Bivol establishes an early lead.

Bivol would also be putting another bout between himself and the Beterbiev trilogy. Smith’s mandatory position explains the matchup, but beating him would still leave the question of when Bivol and Beterbiev meet again.

The next step is firmer confirmation of the event details. RCC has announced signed documents; December 12 remains its stated target.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Uses Dana White to Build American Profile
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn admits his exchanges with Dana White are raising his profile in America. That gives him a reason to keep provoking the UFC boss during the Fury–Joshua promotion, but getting noticed is only the first step. Hearn still needs to give those American viewers a reason to follow his boxing shows.

“Don’t forget, my profile in America is nowhere near where it is in the UK, and that’s starting to change a lot because of the battle with Dana,” Hearn told Ariel Helwani. “Every time he speaks, he’s talking about me. It’s been really good for me and fun. Obviously, even more fun when you’re winning, but it’s a battle, isn’t it? It’s only the first of many in this process.”

Hearn’s admission helps explain the repeated comments about White’s role in Fury–Joshua. An irritated response puts the Matchroom promoter in front of White’s audience again. Hearn can benefit from that exposure regardless of whether the viewers agree with him.

The harder work comes afterward. American fans recognizing Hearn doesn’t necessarily mean they will watch his cards or buy tickets. His UK events being available through DAZN gives them access, but he needs fighters and matchups that make them want to tune in.

Joshua’s popularity in Britain cannot be treated as a guarantee of the same response in America. Fury–Joshua may draw attention as an individual event, but Hearn needs attractions that can support an ongoing U.S. schedule.

A promoter with P.T. Barnum’s instinct for exploiting publicity would move quickly to give that new audience something to buy. Alternating between American and British shows would let Hearn build interest while maintaining his established business at home.

That would require accepting smaller American ticket sales as part of the investment. Expecting British-sized crowds immediately could discourage the very shows needed to develop an audience. Repeat appearances, sensible venues, and more American fighters would give fans a chance to form an attachment.

Signing those fighters is only part of the job. Keeping them long enough to build their following is equally important.

Hearn calls the exchanges with White a win. The attention may be useful, but its commercial value remains unproven. If he doesn’t follow it with U.S. events people want to attend, his increased profile could fade when White stops responding.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Pushes Floyd Mayweather for Professional Fight
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia has set his sights on Floyd Mayweather for a fully sanctioned professional bout, insisting the retired legend reached out to him first. Ryan shut down any talk of an exhibition, making it clear he only wants a clash if Mayweather puts his 50-0 record on the line.

The Ring’s post on X detailing the challenge blew up instantly. Fans are definitely curious, though convincing Mayweather to risk his pristine ledger just before his 50th birthday is a massive hurdle.

“Okay Floyd let’s see how much you love that ‘0,’” Ryan posted on X. “And no I wouldn’t do an exhibition I want his 0 on the fucking line. How much does he actually think he got left. I’m ready Floyd, remember you made this call. I’m just returning the favor. Offer is on the table. Accept or not, if not I move foward as I have been.”

Ryan’s public callout does not mean Floyd agreed to step into a real ring. Nothing is signed, and no date exists.

Mayweather turns 50 this February. He has not fought professionally since beating Conor McGregor in 2017, and his last appearances against elite pugilists were his 2015 victories over Manny Pacquiao and Andre Berto.

Stepping into a real fight against a prime competitor after nearly a decade away is an entirely different reality. Mayweather still possesses unmatched ring IQ, yet reflex speed fades with time. Garcia’s explosive hand speed and blistering left hook could punish sluggish reactions if Floyd struggles to keep his legs under him as the rounds tick by. A decision win for Ryan seems likely, with a late stoppage well within reach if Mayweather cannot dodge incoming combinations.

Recent reports detailing Floyd’s financial headaches suggest a monster check would tempt him. Protecting that flawless record remains his primary concern. An exhibition gives him a lucrative payday with zero official consequences, but Garcia refuses to entertain that route.

Ryan also risks major blowback for targeting a man nearing 50. Floyd’s legendary status guarantees huge box office numbers, yet defeating an aged icon proves very little against the current elite at welterweight. Going after this spectacle suggests Ryan is chasing pure dollar signs, even if it hands him the historic bragging right of tarnishing Mayweather’s undefeated legacy.

Ghana News.title: Premature to call for Sports Minister’s removal while CID probe is ongoing – Ernest Norgbey
Ghana News.content:
Chairman of Parliament’s Youth and Sports Committee, Ernest Norgbey, says it would be premature to call for the removal of Sports Minister Kofi Adams while investigations into alleged irregularities surrounding Ghana’s World Cup travel arrangements are ongoing.

Speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story, Mr Norgbey said he would only support calls for the minister to step aside if the committee’s investigations establish that his continued stay in office could interfere with the process.

“I would only agree on that when the minister has, as promised, provided all the documents to us, all the information that we requested from him, and we realise that no, his continuous stay in office will interfere in the investigation. But as we speak now, it will be premature for me to pronounce that judgment. Not at all,” he said.

His comments follow calls by the Minority in Parliament for President John Mahama to remove Mr Adams from office, following allegations surrounding the arrangements for officials and other individuals who travelled for the 2026 World Cup.

The Minority has also questioned the handling of visa and travel arrangements, including allegations that some individuals paid significantly more than the amounts contemplated in the original arrangements.

However, Mr Norgbey said the allegations must first be established through investigations before conclusions are drawn.

He noted that the National Sports Authority (NSA) boss, Yaw Ampofo-Ankrah, was asked to step aside after being invited by the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) to provide evidence.

“The difference here is that the NSA boss was invited by the CID. You don’t know the briefing the President got from the CID. So the NSA boss gave evidence to the CID.”

According to Mr Norgbey, he is not aware that Mr Adams has been invited by the CID for questioning.

“I’m not sure the minister has been called before the CID, any investigative authority, to give evidence or otherwise, as we speak now.”

He therefore maintained that it would be premature to demand the minister’s removal at this stage, stressing that the investigative process should be allowed to establish the facts.

Mr Norgbey also disclosed that the Youth and Sports Committee is still awaiting additional information from the minister and various agencies involved in the preparations for the World Cup before it can conclude its own report.

Ghana News.title: NPP mourns Samuel Arthur Odoi-Sykes
Ghana News.content:
The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has expressed deep sorrow over the death of Ambassador Samuel Arthur Odoi-Sykes, describing him as one of the founding pillars of the party and a distinguished statesman.

In a statement dated October 7, 2026, and signed by National Chairman John Boadu, the party said Mr Odoi-Sykes devoted several decades to public service, democratic governance and constitutional democracy.

Mr Odoi-Sykes served as Member of Parliament for Ashiedu Keteke, now Odododiodioo, during Ghana’s Third Republic and later became Minority Leader of Parliament.

The NPP said he distinguished himself through parliamentary leadership and advocacy for democratic ideals.

As a founding father of the NPP, Ambassador Odoi-Sykes played what the party described as a pivotal role in establishing its institutional and ideological foundations.

He served as National Chairman of the party from 1998 to 2001, a period the NPP said was instrumental in uniting and strengthening the party ahead of its historic electoral victory in 2000.

According to the party, that victory resulted in the first democratic transfer of power between political parties under the Fourth Republic.

Following the NPP’s electoral victory, Mr Odoi-Sykes served as Ghana’s High Commissioner to Canada from 2001 to 2006, where he represented the country and contributed to strengthening Ghana’s diplomatic relations.

The NPP said he also served on several national and party committees throughout his lifetime, providing counsel, strategic leadership and institutional experience.

The party described his integrity, humility, intellect and commitment to Ghana’s democratic development as qualities that would continue to inspire future generations.

“His passing marks the end of an illustrious chapter in Ghana's political history,” the statement said, adding that the nation had lost a distinguished public servant while the NPP had lost “one of its most respected elder statesmen and steadfast architects.”

The party extended its condolences to his wife, children, the Odoi-Sykes family, friends and associates.

It said Ambassador Odoi-Sykes had “paid his dues” through a life of service to God, country and the party, and that his legacy of principled leadership, patriotism and selfless service would remain part of Ghana’s democratic history.

Ghana News.title: Stay out of World Cup visa probe to avoid interfering with CID investigations – Ernest Norgbey to politicians
Ghana News.content:
Chairman of Parliament’s Youth and Sports Committee, Ernest Norgbey, has urged politicians to stay out of the ongoing investigation into alleged irregularities surrounding Ghana’s World Cup travel arrangements.

His comments follow concerns over the payment of approximately $623,000 in visa facilitation fees in connection with Ghana's arrangements for supporters and officials travelling to the tournament.

The Minority in Parliament has called for the immediate dismissal and prosecution of the Minister for Sports and Recreation, Kofi Eddie Adams, and the Chief Executive of the Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA) over their alleged involvement in the 2026 FIFA World Cup visa scandal.

The call comes days after President John Mahama suspended the Director General of the National Sports Authority (NSA), Yaw Ampofo Ankrah, over his alleged involvement in an investigation into a $623,000 visa facilitation fee.

According to Mr Norgbey, the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) should be allowed to conduct its work without political pressure or commentary that could potentially interfere with the process.

Speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story, Mr Norgbey said although politicians could engage in political debate, investigative agencies must be allowed to establish the facts.

“We can do our politics; we are politicians, we can do our politics. I’m not sure the security agencies, the investigative agencies, will also do politics with it.” "...if that is not handled well, it will also be treated as one of the politics that we play in this country, which I am worried about. If an individual has committed a crime, visa recipient, etc., and the investigative authorities are handling the matter, politicians should be taken away out of this matter. Otherwise we'll handle it in the political way, and to what end? That is my worry at this point in time." He said he was worried that the allegations being debated publicly could ultimately undermine the credibility of the investigation.

“That is why I am so worried that this matter is being discussed at this point, at this level, in the public domain, because if care is not taken, at the end of the day it will go a long way to interfere with what the CID is doing.”

Mr Norgbey stressed that the allegations against officials, including Sports Minister Kofi Adams, could not be treated as established facts until investigations were completed.

He also noted that President John Mahama had already directed the National Sports Authority (NSA) boss, Yaw Ampofo-Ankrah, to step aside to allow investigations into the matter.

According to him, the circumstances surrounding the NSA boss’s decision to step aside differ from those involving the Sports Minister, who he says has not, to his knowledge, been invited by the CID for questioning.

Ghana News.title: Bono East Minister inspects ‘Big Push’ roads; contractor on Tankor-Fiema-Busunya road ahead of schedule
Ghana News.content:
The Bono East Regional Minister, Francis Owusu Antwi, has embarked on a tour of major road construction projects being undertaken under the government's Big Push policy in the Nkoranza North District.

The Minister, who was accompanied by a team of regional officials from the Regional Coordinating Council (RCC), including the regional highways and feeder roads engineers, inspected ongoing works on key stretches of road in the district on Tuesday.

Speaking after the inspection, Mr Owusu Antwi said he was visibly impressed with the pace of work, particularly on the 14-kilometre Tankor-Fiema-Busunya road, where the contractor has completed over 50 per cent of the work — far ahead of the expected 29 per cent.

He commended the contractor for staying on site with adequate machinery and workforce, stressing that the speed of work was vital to delivering the project on time.

"This is the Big Push in action. The contractors are on site, the machines are here, and the workforce is ready. Speed is vital because the people of this district deserve better roads," he said.

The Minister also highlighted the socio-economic importance of the road network to residents, particularly in terms of health, job creation and access to markets.

He noted that with the famous Buaben Fiema Monkey Sanctuary located in the area, the completion of the road network would significantly boost the tourism potential of the district and the Bono East Region at large.

"When this road network is completed, it will boost the tourism potential of this district and the region as a whole. It is about connecting our people to opportunity," he added.

The District Chief Executive for Nkoranza North, Effah Patrick, said the 74-kilometre road construction in the area under the Big Push policy would help connect communities and create easy access for agricultural produce to various markets across the country.

"This 74km road will connect our communities. It creates easy access for our farmers to transport their produce to the various markets in the country. It is a game-changer for us," he said.

He was, however, thankful to the President for the support.

The Regional Feeder Roads Manager, Stephen Quainoo, who also spoke during the tour, commended the contractor handling the Tankor-Fiema-Busunya road for being way ahead of schedule.

He disclosed that while only 29 per cent of the work was expected to have been completed at this stage, the contractor had already surpassed the 50 per cent mark.

"The contractor is currently way ahead of schedule. We have over 50 per cent of the work done compared to an expected 29 per cent. I am hopeful that the contractor will complete the work ahead of schedule," Mr Quainoo said.

For the people of Nkoranza North, the ongoing road projects under the Big Push policy represent more than just infrastructure — they symbolise improved access to healthcare, enhanced economic opportunities and a brighter future for the district.

The Regional Minister is expected to continue his tour in the coming days to inspect other ongoing projects across the Bono East Region.

Ghana News.title: Scrutiny is not disloyalty – Chief of Staff defends serious journalism at 30th GJA Awards launch
Ghana News.content:
​The Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) officially launched the milestone 30th GJA Media Awards and inaugurated its nine-member Awards Committee at the Kempinski Hotel Gold Coast City, Accra.

The launch event, held on October 7, brought together high-ranking government officials, members of the diplomatic community, media executives, and stakeholders to set the stage for the upcoming awards ceremony scheduled for November 7, 2026.

​The newly inaugurated Awards Committee, chaired by National Media Commission (NMC) Commissioner and former Daily Graphic Editor Kobby Asmah, will oversee a rigorous, transparent, and credible assessment process until October 28, 2026.

​Delivering a keynote address as the Special Guest of Honour, Chief of Staff Julius Debrah declared that the government cannot effectively serve the public if it only receives applause, saying that rigorous oversight and critical reporting are vital for national development.

"We may disagree with a headline or a conclusion, but disagreement is not hostility, and scrutiny is not disloyalty," Mr Debrah stated, stressing that state-media relations must rest on mutual accountability and shared responsibilities.

While urging public officials to provide timely information and respect press freedom, Mr Debrah also challenged journalists to maintain high ethical standards.

He stressed the need for reporters to thoroughly verify facts, separate opinion from news, and protect personal reputations from becoming collateral damage in the race to publish first.

Addressing the digital evolution of the industry, the Chief of Staff noted that modern technology has transformed mobile phones into powerful newsrooms and broadcast tools, creating jobs and amplifying once-ignored voices.

He called on the GJA to lead training and mentorship efforts, bridging traditional reporting with digital content creation to advance innovation and ethics side by side.

"Ghana will need a media that can move at the speed of technology without abandoning the discipline of truth," Hon. Debrah concluded, urging reporters to continue holding public officeholders accountable with courage, conscience, and fairness.

As the GJA looks toward its landmark celebration on November 7, 2026, the message from the capital is clear: while technology reshapes the newsroom, the timeless pursuit of truth, courage, and accountability remains the ultimate standard for Ghanaian journalism.

Ghana News.title: Abuse case: Nana Akua’s husband Harold unable to appear in court after hospital admission – Police
Ghana News.content:
Harold Norman, who is at the centre of domestic abuse allegations involving his wife Rosemond Akua Adobea, popularly known as Nana Akua, was unable to appear before court on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, because he had been admitted to hospital.

According to the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) of the Ghana Police Service, Mr Norman was scheduled to be put before court today.

However, his lawyer informed the Police that his client had been admitted to hospital and was therefore unable to appear as scheduled.

The Police said investigators from the Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit (DOVVSU) subsequently visited the hospital to verify the claim.

They are also monitoring the situation to ensure that Mr Norman is arraigned immediately upon his discharge from the hospital.

Mr Norman was arrested on August 27, 2026, following a petition filed by Rosemond Akua Adobea on August 20, alleging that her husband had subjected her to physical, emotional and economic abuse.

The Police said he was later granted police enquiry bail with two sureties on August 29 while investigations continued.

The case had previously been handled by DOVVSU at the Lakeside and Ministries Police Stations in July 2026, according to the CID.

The Police have assured that investigations into the allegations will be conducted professionally and fairly.

Ghana News.title: Mahmud Kabore picks NDC Ashanti Regional Communication Officer nomination forms
Ghana News.content:
Mahmud Kabore has picked up nomination forms to contest the position of Ashanti Regional Communication Officer of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC).

Kabore said he intends to strengthen the party’s communication structures and equip communicators with timely and accurate information if elected.

Speaking to the Kumasi Mail after picking up his forms, Mahmud Kabore said his political involvement began at the grassroots level and had taken him through the branch, constituency, regional and national communication structures of the party.

He recalled serving as acting branch secretary following the death of the substantive branch secretary at Asuboasu L/A Primary School in the Sekyere Afram Plains area.

“I have passed through the grassroots of the party to the constituency level and worked for the party as a regional and national communication member,” he said.

Kabore said his experience working under various communication directors had given him an understanding of the challenges facing political communication.

“The time has come for me to take full responsibility for the Party’s Ashanti Regional Communications Team and bring to bear the wealth of experience, knowledge and lessons I have gathered over the years, from the national front to the constituency level. Working with all stakeholders, we shall build on the solid foundation laid by the Lawyer Sammy Gyamfi-led administration at the national level and the Lawyer Abass Nurudeen-led administration in the Ashanti Region. Together, we shall unite our communicators, strengthen our structures, amplify the Party’s message and make the Ashanti Region a stronger communications force for victory in 2028 and beyond,” he said.

Mahmud Kabore said he would build on the work of previous communication teams rather than discard their achievements.

“In Ashanti Region, I am coming to build upon what they have achieved for the party,” he said.

Key priorities

Kabore said his priorities would include improving coordination among the regional, constituency and branch communication structures and ensuring that communicators receive timely and reliable information.

Mahmud Kabore said communicators must be able to explain government policies and programmes clearly and respond to public concerns using verified information.

He also identified training as a priority, particularly in policy communication and the use of social media.

Kabore said he would seek to address negative perceptions of the NDC in the Ashanti Region through what he described as strategic communication.

He also highlighted the welfare of party communicators, saying their work should be supported with the necessary resources, information and organisational structures.

The contest forms part of the NDC’s internal processes ahead of preparations for the 2028 general elections.

Kabore is seeking the opportunity to lead the party’s communication team in the Ashanti Region.

Ghana News.title: KNUST Career Services pioneer Selina Doe Angmor named among 2026 40 Under 40 honourees
Ghana News.content:
Mrs Selina Doe Angmor, pioneer and first Director of the KNUST Career Services Centre, has been recognised among the 2026 40 Under 40 honourees in the Human Resources category.

She received the recognition at a ceremony held at the Kempinski Hotel in Accra on September 12, 2026.

The award recognises her work in human resources, higher education, workforce development and career services, particularly her contribution to connecting students and graduates with opportunities in the world of work.

Mrs Angmor played a key role in establishing the KNUST Career Services Centre, where she helped shape its vision, systems and programmes and strengthen its engagement with students, employers and industry.

Under her leadership, the Centre developed into a career development hub providing students and graduates with career guidance, employability support and opportunities to connect with employers.

Her work extends beyond KNUST.

She currently serves as Project Lead for the European Union Pact for Skills Programme at KNUST, supervised by the United Nations Capital Development Fund (UNCDF), where she leads initiatives focused on career services, employer engagement, digital skills and employability development.

Her professional experience also spans the oil and gas, energy, banking, hospitality and media sectors, with expertise in talent acquisition, learning and development, performance management and organisational capacity building.

Mrs Angmor has also been involved in the Model United Nations community for more than 14 years, participating in programmes and international conferences linked to the United Nations Headquarters in New York and Geneva.

Her journey in Model United Nations has taken her from participating as a young delegate to training others preparing for similar international experiences.

The recognition adds to a career focused on developing people, strengthening links between education and industry, and creating opportunities for young professionals.

Mrs Angmor’s recognition in the Human Resources category highlights her contribution to career development and workforce preparation, particularly through her pioneering work at KNUST.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
