World.title: 2027: Duke vows to reduce petrol price to ₦300 per litre if elected president
World.content:
Former Cross River State governor and Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) presidential candidate, Donald Duke, has promised to reduce the price of petrol to about ₦300 per litre if elected president in 2027.

Mr Duke said he would not achieve the price reduction by returning to the opaque subsidy regime of the past, but by changing how petroleum products for domestic consumption are priced.

He said Nigeria should price petrol based on the actual cost of producing and refining its crude rather than subjecting domestic consumers to international market prices.

The former governor made the remarks on Wednesday during an interview on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief, where he criticised President Bola Tinubu’s economic policies and outlined his own approach to the petroleum sector.

‘Subsidy regime is a scam’

Mr Duke dismissed the traditional subsidy arrangement as unsustainable. He argued that Nigeria, as an oil-producing country, should use part of its crude production to meet domestic energy needs at a lower cost.

“The subsidy regime thing, this whole scam, I’m going to price petroleum products for local consumption at production cost, not at the international market because that’s so far rigid,” he said.

He said the cost of producing and refining crude for domestic consumption was substantially lower than the international benchmark used to determine the price Nigerians pay.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“I’m giving you a production cost of $45, right? The international price. That’s $45, including processing and refining; otherwise, it is about $30, and it’s sold back to your own people at $100 and more,” he said.

Mr Duke said the present pricing structure was particularly burdensome for low-income Nigerians, whose earnings are increasingly consumed by transportation and energy costs.

“You don’t want them to breathe, and your people are known to be the poorest in the world; they can’t afford it,” he said.

“The basic minimum wage is N70,000; will your salary go in just filling a tank of fuel or some fuel? So, we have got to look at it.”

How Duke says ₦300 petrol would work

Asked how much Nigerians should expect to pay for petrol under his administration, Mr Duke said his target would be about N300 per litre.

“I will try and bring it to about N300. It sounds so outlandish, but I have given you the arithmetic,” he said.

He proposed setting aside a portion of Nigeria’s crude oil production specifically for domestic consumption, while exporting the remainder.

“Allocate 600,000 barrels; if that is what is consumed daily, allocate that to yourself; the other one million you can sell,” he said.

His proposal seeks to insulate the domestic market from the full impact of international crude oil prices by treating some of Nigeria’s crude as a strategic domestic resource rather than pricing it entirely against its export value.

Mr Duke also said he would not inherit Mr Tinubu’s economic policies if elected, insisting that his priority would be productivity.

“I won’t inherit his policies; you know, for me, productivity is everything, as I said, within a safe and orderly environment,” he said.

Duke links insecurity to economic hardship

The PRP candidate also connected Nigeria’s worsening insecurity to economic pressures, arguing that the country’s population had grown substantially. At the same time, the real value of government spending had failed to keep pace.

“What you are seeing is the symptoms of a collapsed economy,” he said, adding that economic pressure was contributing to banditry, kidnapping and other crimes.

Mr Duke said Nigeria’s economic challenge could not be addressed merely by increasing nominal budget figures without improving their purchasing power and the economy’s productive capacity.

He called for a debate among the presidential candidates ahead of the 2027 election, saying Nigerians should be able to compare the candidates’ economic ideas directly.

“I desire to get the conversation driven to where, in particular, it is instrumental to our thinking. I would like us to have a debate, for instance, a very robust debate, and I’m going to be calling for this where all the candidates speak,” he said.

How other 2027 candidates differ on subsidy

The fuel-price proposal places Mr Duke among a growing number of 2027 presidential candidates making cheaper petrol a central campaign issue, although their approaches differ.

President Tinubu, who abolished the petrol subsidy after assuming office in May 2023, has rejected calls to restore it. In his recent Independence Day address, he described subsidies as “addictive” and said his administration would not reverse its economic reforms.

Former Vice President and African Democratic Congress presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has taken the opposite position. He has repeatedly said he would restore petrol subsidy if elected.

More recently, Atiku proposed a transparent production subsidy for petroleum products refined in Nigeria, with a fixed spending limit, legislative approval and independent audits.

Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, said the subsidy should be removed but criticised how the proceeds have been managed. He said the savings should have been redirected into productive sectors such as healthcare and other areas that directly benefit citizens.

Accord Party candidate Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim has proposed a starting petrol price of ₦605 per litre, saying it could eventually fall to between ₦200 and ₦300 if production costs and the exchange rate are brought under control. He has argued that the country needs a transparent cost structure rather than an opaque subsidy system.

Social Democratic Party candidate Adewole Adebayo has gone further, promising to reduce petrol, cooking gas and aviation fuel prices to ₦200 per litre within 12 months of taking office, partly through the revival of Nigeria’s refineries and development of modular refineries.

The competing proposals have brought the subsidy debate back to the centre of the 2027 presidential contest, with candidates divided between restoring some form of government intervention, maintaining subsidy removal while reducing production costs, or retaining the existing market-based framework.

Mr Duke’s central argument is that Nigerians should not have to pay an international-market price for a resource produced in their own country.

The feasibility of the proposal, including the actual cost of producing and refining the crude, the volume available for domestic consumption, and the fiscal implications of selling part of Nigeria’s crude below export-market value, is likely to become a major issue as the 2027 campaign progresses.

World.title: Oke presents letter of credence to Macron, assumes duty as Nigeria’s envoy to France
World.content:
Nigeria’s Ambassador to the French Republic, Ayodele Oke, has formally assumed his diplomatic duties following the presentation of his Letters of Credence to French President Emmanuel Macron.

Mr Oke presented his letter to the French President on Monday in a brief ceremony at the Élysée Palace, the official residence of the French presidency.

Mr Oke has now become Nigeria’s 17th ambassador to France. He is also the latest ambassador to present his letter of credence to his host country, formally marking the resumption of duties.

Letters of credence are formal diplomatic documents issued by a country’s head of state to confirm the appointment of an ambassador or permanent representative.

They officially introduce the envoy to the receiving authority, in this case, the French President, and certify that the individual is empowered to speak and act on behalf of their nation.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that President Bola Tinubu announced new ambassadors last year and approved their posting in March. This came two years after he recalled the previous ambassadors without giving a specific reason.

During the interregnum, Nigeria operated without top representatives abroad, relying only on former foreign minister Yusuf Tuggar and the Chargé d’affaires at its embassies.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

READ ALSO: Tinubu meets Macron for private dinner in Paris

Since the posting approval, several appointees have resumed duties.

In a statement issued after the ceremony, Mr Oke said his mandate would include strengthening bilateral relations in security, trade and investment, while ensuring that Nigeria’s interests, values and international reputation are advanced with “clarity and credibility.”

He also said his broader diplomatic responsibilities included securing advantages for Nigeria, protecting Nigerian citizens and promoting the country’s national image in France.

Mr Oke’s appointment places him at the centre of the evolving Nigeria-France relations. It comes at a time when the relationship between the countries is growing stronger.

The ambassador said it “underscored the compelling need to elevate and recalibrate the partnership between Nigeria and France.”

World.title: Health Review: Ebola alert, Lassa fever deaths, maternal health push, other developments that shaped September
World.content:
September brought significant developments across Nigeria’s health sector, from new maternal health interventions and healthcare financing to local production of essential health products.

Beyond Nigeria, concerns over Ebola and declining malaria financing also kept regional health security in focus.

PREMIUM TIMES reviews some of the major health developments that shaped the month.

Nigeria heightens alert over DRC Ebola outbreak

Nigeria strengthened surveillance measures following the continued spread of Ebola Virus Disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

As of 21 September, the DRC had recorded 7,773 confirmed cases and 3,759 deaths across 63 health zones in seven provinces. The NCDC said travellers arriving from countries with active or relevant Ebola transmission may be required to complete a Health Declaration Form.

Read full article →

Lassa fever deaths rise to 259

Nigeria recorded 1,086 confirmed Lassa fever cases and 259 deaths across 24 states and 118 Local Government Areas, with the case fatality rate rising to 23.9 per cent.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The NCDC identified late presentation, high treatment costs, poor health-seeking behaviour and inadequate awareness in high-burden communities among the challenges contributing to the high death rate.

Read full article →

FG launches incentives for maternal, newborn healthcare

The federal government launched new incentives to increase use of maternal and newborn health services under the Maternal and Neonatal Mortality Reduction Innovation Initiative (MAMII).

The intervention seeks to address barriers that prevent women and newborns from accessing timely, quality healthcare, including antenatal care, skilled delivery, and postnatal services.

Read full article →

Nigeria begins local production of insecticide-treated nets

Nigeria has begun local production of dual-active-ingredient insecticide-treated mosquito nets as part of efforts to strengthen malaria prevention and reduce dependence on imported health products.

At full capacity, the new manufacturing facility is expected to produce about 10 million nets annually and create more than 600 jobs.

Read full article →

Kaduna intervention strengthens response to postpartum bleeding

A maternal health intervention in Kaduna State is strengthening the capacity of primary healthcare workers to detect and manage postpartum haemorrhage, one of Nigeria’s leading causes of maternal deaths.

Under the Task Shifting Task Sharing project, 77 Community Health Extension Workers across 77 primary healthcare facilities in nine LGAs were trained in maternal and newborn healthcare, including the E-MOTIVE approach for managing excessive bleeding after childbirth. Programme records show that supported PHCs managed 192 postpartum haemorrhage cases between October 2025 and June 2026.

Read full article →

Nigeria targets 70 per cent local production of essential health products

The federal government announced a target to produce at least 70 per cent of Nigeria’s essential healthcare products locally by 2030 as part of efforts to strengthen medicine security and reduce dependence on imports.

The government said it had secured about $2 billion in financing commitments, while 87 local manufacturers benefited from zero tariffs on pharmaceutical machinery and production inputs.

Read full article →

Diphtheria outbreak persists in Plateau

Plateau State recorded 469 suspected diphtheria cases and 31 deaths, with cases reported across 10 of the state’s 17 local government areas.

The state government said 160,000 children had been vaccinated as authorities intensified immunisation, surveillance and public awareness efforts to contain the outbreak.

Read full article →

Malaria funding cuts threaten Africa’s progress

African health leaders warned that a 30 per cent reduction in malaria financing could lead to an additional 146 million cases and nearly 400,000 deaths on the continent by 2030.

The warning renewed calls for stronger domestic financing as African countries account for the overwhelming majority of the global malaria burden.

Read full article →

World.title: FIFA Ranking: Super Eagles plunge to 30th, drop to Africa’s sixth
World.content:
The Super Eagles have suffered a significant setback in the latest FIFA Men’s World Ranking, dropping four places to 30th in the world following a disappointing September international window.

Nigeria, who occupied 26th position in the previous ranking, were punished for their mixed results in the opening matches of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign.

The three-time African champions began the qualifying series with a 2-1 victory over Madagascar in Uyo but were brought crashing back to earth days later after Guinea-Bissau handed them a heavy 3-0 defeat.

The contrasting results have now seen Nigeria lose four places globally, while their position on the African continent has also taken a major hit.

The Super Eagles have dropped from third to sixth in Africa, with Morocco retaining their position as the continent’s highest-ranked team.

Nigeria behind five African nations

Morocco lead the African rankings, followed by Senegal, Egypt, Algeria and Côte d’Ivoire, with Nigeria now completing the continental top six.

The latest standings underline how quickly the hierarchy can shift after competitive fixtures, particularly as the 2027 AFCON qualifiers carry greater ranking weight than friendly matches.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Nigeria’s slide also reflects the damaging effect of the defeat in Bissau, where the Super Eagles conceded three goals without reply after their narrow victory over Madagascar.

The result left Eric Chelle’s side with three points from their opening two qualifying matches and reminded them of the importance of consistency during the qualification campaign.

Spain remain among the world’s elite

At the summit of the global ranking, Spain remain firmly among the leading football nations, with the reigning world champions occupying the No. 1 position.

Argentina are second, followed by France and England, while Portugal and Brazil complete the next two positions.

Morocco’s continued rise is particularly significant from an African perspective, with the Atlas Lions in seventh place globally and comfortably ahead of every other African nation.

The Netherlands and Belgium are eighth and ninth, respectively, while Mexico complete the world’s top 10.

The latest top 10 is: Spain, Argentina, France, England, Portugal, Brazil, Morocco, Belgium, Netherlands, and Mexico.

Top football nations outside the top 10

Several other major footballing nations remain within striking distance of the world’s elite.

Colombia sit 11th, followed by Switzerland in 12th and Germany drop to 13th, while Mexico’s position inside the top 10 keeps North America represented among the leading nations.

Senegal are the second-highest African nation at 18th globally, while Erling Haaland’s Norway occupy 19th and Uruguay drop to 20th.

Other notable nations include USA, Denmark, Italy, Iran, Austria and Ecuador, all of whom remain within the world’s top 30.

Nigeria’s neighbours in the latest ranking include Algeria, Egypt, and Côte d’Ivoire, all above the Super Eagles, highlighting the increasingly competitive African football landscape.

Africa’s top 10

Morocco now lead the continental top 10, with Nigeria slipping to sixth after disappointing qualifying results.

The order goes thus: Morocco, Senegal, Egypt, Algeria, Côte d’Ivoire, Nigeria, DR Congo, Cameroon, Mali, and South Africa.

For the Super Eagles, the latest ranking marks another setback after a promising period under Chelle.

Nigeria will now need stronger results in their next competitive fixtures to halt the slide and begin climbing both the FIFA world ranking and the African standings once again.

World.title: Police confirms death of Edo University lecturer after sex in hotel
World.content:
Ambrose Alli University

By Ozioruva Aliu

The police in Edo State have confirmed the death of a lecturer of the Ambrose Alli University, Ekpoma identified as Dr. Matthew Uwaigbe who was said to have died after an amorous affair with a sex worker in a hotel.

The incident reportedly occurred on Sunday, October 5, 2026, at a hotel in the Mosco area of Ekpoma, within Esan West Local Government Area.

According to information gathered about the incident, Uwuigbe had checked into the hotel with the woman, identified as Angela Defa Jacob.

At some point after their sexual encounter, the lecturer reportedly asked Jacob to step out and get water for him.

She left the room and returned a short while later.

But instead of finding him waiting for her, she reportedly discovered Uwuigbe lying motionless on the bed.

The situation was subsequently reported to the police at about 8 p.m. that same Sunday.

Police spokesperson Eno Ikoedem confirmed that the deceased had lodged at the hotel and had engaged the services of the 21-year-old woman before his sudden death.

She said Jacob had been sent out to purchase water and found Uwuigbe dead when she returned.

For Ambrose Alli University, the institution confirmed that Uwuigbe was a member of its staff.

The university’s Public Relations Officer, Otunba Mike Ade Aladenika, stressed that the incident did not happen on university grounds.

He said the circumstances surrounding the lecturer’s activities were a matter of his private life, adding that the woman involved was not a student of the university.

Vanguard News

World.title: Uzodimma commends security agencies for quick release of corps members
World.content:
Gov Uzodimma

Imo State Governor, Senator Hope Uzodimma, has applauded security agencies for their quick intervention in securing the release of 20 corps members kidnapped along the Onitsha-Owerri Road a few days ago.

He said he was particularly pleased with the security agencies for their collaboration and patriotism in ensuring that the corps members were rescued unharmed.

In a statement he personally signed, Governor Uzodimma also expressed satisfaction with the collaborative efforts of both the Oyo and Imo State Governments towards the quick release of all 20 captives.

He said that since the issue involved the security of lives, the government was cautious about releasing too much information to the public, hence the discreet manner in which it was handled.

The Governor said he was particularly grateful to the security agencies for the discreet and collaborative manner in which they tackled the challenge.

He also praised the parents for their patience during the trying period and urged Nigerians to always have faith in the Federal Government to overcome the current security challenges in the country.

Vanguard News

World.title: NES#32: FG to assess what’s working in Nigeria’s economy
World.content:
By Gabriel Ewepu

The Federal Government, Wednesday, through the Federal Ministry of Federal Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning, said the the 32nd edition of the Nigerian Economic Summit tagged NES#32 will be used to examine what is working in the economy.

This was stated by the Minister of State for National Budget and Economic Planning, Dr. Doris Uzoka-Anite in a speech delivered at the World Press Conference on the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit organised by the Nigerian Economic Summit Group, NESG, in Abuja, from the 26th-27th October, 2026 with theme ‘Growth that Works: Delivering Jobs, Productivity and Shared Prosperity’.

Uzoka-Anite while acknowledging the impact of the previous editions of the Summit said the recommendations by the NESG have been implemented while others are on the way.

She also urged the media to project the Summit as it has been doing in past editions, which had really informed the government, stakeholders and Nigerians.

She said the media is not just for publicity but are the arrowheads of the Summit, and added that all aspects of the Summit need to be critically reported for further actions.

She said: “The Nigerian Economic Summit provides a unique opportunity to examine what is working within our economy, identify the gaps that remain and develop practical and implementable recommendations for accelerating economic transformation.

“The summit brings together the country’s leading policymakers, business leaders, economists, academics, development partners, labor representatives, civil society organizations and other stakeholders to deliberate on the challenges confronting our economy and, more importantly, the opportunities before us.

“The ultimate objective is to move Nigeria from potential to prosperity by ensuring that economic policies and reforms translate into tangible improvements in the lives and livelihoods of Nigerians.”

Meanwhile, she said the Summit will also be organised around five key priorities: Work Nigeria – creating more and better jobs for our people; Produce Nigeria – increasing productivity, promoting industrialisation, and strengthening value addition; Invest

Nigeria – attracting investment while developing our human capital through education, healthcare, and social development; Scale Nigeria – unlocking the potential of our states and sub-national governments to drive inclusive and sustainable growth; and Secure Nigeria – strengthening national security and building the resilience needed to withstand economic and other shocks.

Earlier, the Chairman, Central Working Organizing Committee,



NES#32, Dr Aisha Umar, in a remark, said for over three decades, the Nigerian Economic Summit has brought together stakeholders under roof to confront Nigeria’s defining economic questions.

According to Umar, “NES#32 asks one profound question: how do we ensure growth translates into productive enterprises, decent jobs and rising incomes — not just stronger GDP numbers?”

However, she acknowledged that, “Nigeria’s reforms over the past three years — subsidy removal, exchange-rate unification, fiscal restructuring and bank recapitalisation — have begun to restore macroeconomic discipline, improve external buffers and revive investor confidence. These are real achievements. But stabilisation is necessary; it is not sufficient.

“The question before Nigeria has therefore shifted from restoring stability to converting it into transformation. The next phase must strengthen the transmission from reform to investment, investment to productivity, productivity to jobs, and jobs to shared prosperity. That is the growth that works.”

She also added that, “This is urgent: Nigeria still faces high production costs, infrastructure deficits, low productivity and insecurity, with over 90 per cent of employment informal. The task is not to grow faster, but to grow differently — raising productivity and creating jobs at scale.

“A fragmenting global economy brings both risk and opportunity. Nigeria’s large market, resources, youthful population and position within AfCFTA give it real advantages — but only if we can produce efficiently and attract productive capital.”

Meanwhile, according to the Chief Executive Officer, CEO, NESG, Dr Tayo Aduloju, 10 governors would participate during the Summit including local governments and the judiciary.

He also spoke on the impact of the NES on policies after 33 years of active and fruitful engagements with policy makers in both public and private sectors of the economy, which had led to reforms in the telecom industry, pensions, tax, and among others.

World.title: ‘All my respect’ – Ronaldo celebrates Messi after Argentina retirement
World.content:
Portugal legend Cristiano Ronaldo has paid tribute to Lionel Messi following the Argentine captain’s final appearance for the national team.

Messi ended his international career on Tuesday night after helping Argentina secure a 3-0 friendly victory over Benin at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires.

The 39-year-old scored one of Argentina’s goals and provided two assists as he bowed out after more than two decades of

representing his country.

Messi, regarded as one of football’s greatest-ever players, described the occasion as “the saddest day of my career” as he brought an emotional chapter of his career to a close.

Ronaldo, who shared one of football’s most celebrated rivalries with Messi for more than 15 years, reacted to the Argentine’s farewell post on Instagram on Wednesday.

The Al-Nassr forward wrote: “Leo, so many years defending your country and a story that will live on forever. You have all my respect for everything you’ve achieved with Argentina. A hug.”

The message highlights the respect that has developed between the two superstars despite their long-running rivalry, which defined an era of world football during their respective spells at Real Madrid and Barcelona.

Messi had announced his decision to retire from international football in late August, following Argentina’s defeat to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final.

The decision came after a physically and emotionally demanding tournament, which was also overshadowed by the illness and subsequent death of his father, Jorge Messi.

Messi leaves international football as Argentina’s record appearance holder, having made 208 appearances and scored 126 goals for the national team.

He also guided Argentina to the 2022 World Cup title and helped the country secure Copa América triumphs during his international career.

Ronaldo and Messi have continued to acknowledge each other’s achievements in recent years despite their historic rivalry.

Ronaldo also expressed his support for Messi following the death of the Argentine’s father earlier this year.

Both players are now in the later stages of their careers, with Messi continuing with Inter Miami in Major League Soccer and Ronaldo representing Saudi Pro League side Al-Nassr.

Vanguard News

World.title: 2027: Tinubu’s win gap over opponents will be unbelievable — Bwala
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, Daniel Bwala, has expressed confidence that the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential candidate will secure a much wider margin over his opponents in the 2027 presidential election.

Bwala made the assertion while speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today, in response to a question on what gave him confidence that Tinubu could win the 2027 election, despite arguments that the President’s 2023 victory was relatively narrow.

He said the odds had also been against Tinubu ahead of the 2023 election, arguing that developments at the time did not favour the President.

“The confidence I have is this: all of the statistics and results you read out which happened before President Bola Tinubu won the election at that time, there was nobody who did not know that the odds were not in his favour,” Bwala said.

“The governing party at that time, it was clear that they were not working for him. In the real sense of the word, there were policies that were reeled out just before the election that were quite damning to him.

“There were governors allegedly who were not excited about that because of some thinking here and there.”

According to Bwala, the odds were also against Tinubu during the presidential primary of the All Progressives Congress, APC.

“The odds were against him, even at the primary level. He could have been rigged out,” he said.

Bwala also pointed to the support Tinubu eventually secured from governors, particularly in the North-East.

“Do you know how many governors we recovered? A lot of the governors of the North-East,” he said.

He then made a categorical prediction about the margin he expects Tinubu to secure in 2027.

“Let me tell you and let me say it categorically, and I will be happy to come back, the gap that President Bola Tinubu will give each and every one of these candidates will be so much that you won’t believe it,” Bwala said.

He further cited the number of governors now supporting Tinubu, arguing that their positions give them significant influence over the political structures in their respective states.

“President Bola Tinubu has got how many governors on his side? How many governors have joined him? The governors are Chief Executive Officers of their respective states; they coordinate the structures of the state and won their election to be governors,” Bwala added.

World.title: 20 corps members: Police confirm rescue, vow to arrest suspects
World.content:
Photo Credit: Nigeria Police Force/X

By Emmanuel Iheaka

The police have confirmed the rescue of the 20 corps members abducted along the Owerri-Onitsha express way in Imo State last week Thursday

A statement endorsed by the Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, said the corps members were rescued at Amakohia Ubi, Owerri West Local Government Area of the state, following a coordinated operation with sister security agencies.

Iniedu stated that efforts were ongoing to apprehend those responsible for the abduction and bring them to justice.

He noted that the victims were currently receiving medical assessment and necessary care.

“The Nigeria Police Force, in collaboration with sister security agencies, rescued the 20 prospective NYSC corps members abducted in Imo State on 1st October 2026.

“The victims were rescued on 7th October 2026 at Amakohia Ubi Village, Imo State, following sustained search-and-rescue operations. They have since been taken for medical assessment and necessary care.

“Efforts are ongoing to apprehend those responsible for the abduction, as the Police and other security agencies sustain coordinated operations towards bringing all culpable persons to justice.

“The Nigeria Police Force appreciates members of the public for their cooperation and support and remains committed to the protection of lives and property, prompt response to security threats and continued collaboration with sister security agencies”, the statement read.

World.title: NAF crash: ‘You didn’t say you wouldn’t return from Abuja’ — Bako’s partner
World.content:
The partner of Flight Lieutenant I.S. Bako, one of the 25 people killed in Tuesday’s Nigerian Air Force aircraft crash in Igbokoda, Ondo State, has mourned the deceased officer in an emotional social media post.

Joanna Yakubu, in a TikTok post on Tuesday, recalled her last conversation with Bako, a co-pilot aboard the ill-fated aircraft.

Yakubu said Bako had told her he was travelling to Abuja but gave no indication that he would not return.

“It actually Abuja you told me you are going to and you didn’t mention you will not come back. You left me,” she wrote.

The NAF aircraft, with registration number NAF 931, was on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos when it crashed into the swamps of Igbokoda, in Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State.

According to the Nigerian Air Force, 25 people were on board, comprising five crew members and 20 passengers. No survivor was found.

The Director of Public Relations and Information, NAF, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, said search-and-rescue operations were immediately activated following the crash.

Ejodame said NAF 931 was conducting a routine mission from Benin to Lagos when the accident occurred, adding that rescue efforts were conducted in coordination with relevant authorities.

“No survivors have been found,” he said.

The Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, condoled with the families, colleagues and loved ones of the victims.

Aneke described the crash as “a deeply painful moment for the Nigerian Air Force and the nation” and assured the bereaved families of the full support of the Service.

Those killed

The deceased crew members were identified as Squadron Leader MI Aburime, flight captain; Squadron Leader AP Man-Ugwueje, co-pilot; Flight Lieutenant IS Bako, co-pilot; Warrant Officer Abubakar A, aircraft technician; and Corporal Uguru HC, aircraft technician.

The passengers were identified as Flight Lieutenant TL Lazarus, Flight Lieutenant M Akinloye, Flying Officer IM Adeshina, Master Warrant Officer Onwuka F, Master Warrant Officer Matini BA, Warrant Officer Nuhu FS, Flight Sergeant James RB, Flight Sergeant Mohammed AI, Sergeant Ani AE, Sergeant Izibenikien SI, Sergeant Alafuka C, Sergeant Mbadugha AN, Lance Corporal Ugwuba FC, Lance Corporal Eledan GE, Mrs Ezeh Nneka, Godstmine Tarabina, Joy Micheal, Sunday Micheal, Ukeme David and Gideon Omotola.

The NAF said Aneke had ordered a comprehensive investigation to determine the circumstances surrounding the crash.

World.title: Canada will not allow assisted suicide for those with only mental illness
World.content:
Canada

Canada will not allow medically assisted suicide for people whose only condition is mental illness, the justice minister said Wednesday, seeking to close debate on one of the country’s most controversial healthcare issues.

Canada legalized assisted dying for those at the end of life in 2016.

The right was extended to those suffering from serious and incurable illnesses in 2021, even if death was not “reasonably foreseeable.”

Initially, Canada was to allow assisted death regardless of condition by 2024, but that date was pushed back three years, with the government saying it wanted to make sure that the already overwhelmed mental health system was ready.

Without government action, people exclusively suffering from a mental illness would have had access to assisted suicide in March, when the exclusion was set to expire.

But Justice Minister Sean Fraser told reporters on Wednesday that Canada’s Liberal government plans to pass legislation that will prohibit assisted suicide for people whose only underlying medical condition is mental illness.

“Canada has made a decision not to move forward with the expansion (of assisted suicide),” Fraser said.

“While there is not a perfect consensus on this issue, we believe this is the correct approach.”

Fraser’s announcement follows recommendations from an advisory panel which in June urged the government not to expand assisted suicide rights.

That panel raised concern about the lack of mental health support in communities across the country, and the risk that suffering patients would choose death because they could not access care.

The committee also highlighted debate among mental health experts as to whether mental illness could ever be deemed incurable.

A majority of Canadians support the right to assisted suicide, but in recent months some medical professionals have called for a review of the policy, including how patients receive approval to end their lives.

World.title: Appeal Court Begins Hearing SERAP’s Appeal in N101m Defamation Judgment Debt Friday
World.content:
The Court of Appeal in Abuja has scheduled hearing for Friday in the appeal filed by the Incorporated Trustees of the Socio-economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) in relation to the May 5 judgment given against the group by a High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

Information about the planned hearing date is contained in a notice sent on Wednesday by the appellate court’s Registry to parties in the appeal marked: CA/ABJ/CV/1114/2026.

Justice Halilu Yusuf of the High Court of the FCT had, in the May 5 judgment, awarded N101million in damages and cost against SERAP and its Deputy Director, Kolawole Oluwadare upon holding that they defamed two officials of the Department of State Services (DSS) through a false publication it made on September 10, 2024.

The judgment was on the suit marked: CV/4547/2024 filed by the DSS officials – Sarah John and Gabriel Ogundele – who accused SERAP and Oluwadare of making false claims in publications on the group’s website and social media platforms that the claimants invaded their Abuja office on September 9, 2024 and subjected them to harassment.

Justice Halilu Yusuf held among others that claimants led sufficient evidence that effectively established all the ingredients of defamation.

Justice Yusuf rejected that defence of justification raised by SERAP and Oluwadare on the grounds that they failed to provide evidence that their publications were not based on falsehood.

The judge noted that the words like invasion, forceful entry and harassment were used inaccurately, the defendants having admitted at trial that the DSS officials did not forcefully enter into SERAP’s premises and did not brandish any weapon

He held that the publications made by the defendants injured the reputation of the claimants in their professional capacity and standing in the society.

Justice Yusuf said: “Having been unable to establish invasion and harassment, the defence of justification fails. There is no doubt that the publication affected the claimants mentally and psychologically.”

The judge said, going forward, it was necessary for care and due diligence on the part of SERAP and its officials before releasing information to the public.

He added that in the exercise of their right to tweet and send information out, the defendants should be aware of the rights of others, particularly as it relates to government agencies and their officials.

The judge dismissed the objection raised by the defendants against the competence of the suit and held that the claimants possessed the requisite locus standi to file the suit over which the court has the jurisdiction to entertain.

He held that as against the defendants’ argument, the claimants must not be named in the publication complained about for defamation to be established.

Justice Yusuf noted that from when the claimants complained about the inaccuracy of the publications, the defendants failed to take any steps to pull down the injurious publication.

He proceeded to adjudge the publications as defamatory and awarded damages of N100million against the defendants in addition to N1m as cost of prosecuting the suit.

The judge also ordered the defendants to publish a public apology on SERAP’s website, X handle, two national daily newspapers and two television stations.

He held that the judgment sum shall attract 10 percent interest per annum from the date of the judgment until the sum is fully paid by the defendants.

World.title: Atiku Accuses Tinubu Govt of Abandoning Farmers, Importing Food
World.content:
Former Vice President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of presiding over a decline in agricultural export earnings while farmers face insecurity and manufacturers contend with high production costs.

Atiku made the accusation in a statement issued on Wednesday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council.

He said the agricultural trade figures showed that Nigeria’s agricultural trade moved from a ₦740.27 billion surplus in the first half of 2025 to a ₦56.13 billion deficit in the first half of 2026, representing a ₦796.40 billion reversal.

“Tinubu cannot call this reform when the people who grow our food and the businesses that should process it are being squeezed from both sides,” Atiku said.

According to him, agricultural exports fell by 33.3 per cent, while imports also declined.

“The excuse that Nigerians simply imported too much will not stand. Tinubu’s government must answer for the collapse in what Nigeria sold to the world. The country is losing export earnings, and the President owes farmers, workers and businesses more than another speech about prosperity,” he said.

Atiku questioned what the administration had done to improve security for farmers, reduce the cost of moving agricultural produce and make local processing and manufacturing more viable.

“What has his administration done to make it safer to farm, cheaper to move produce, easier to keep a processing plant running or more profitable to sell a finished Nigerian product? Farmers cannot cultivate promises. Manufacturers cannot power factories with speeches. Workers cannot feed their families on assurances that prosperity is coming,” he said.

The former vice president said Nigeria’s leading agricultural exports still include cashew nuts in shell and cocoa beans, arguing that greater domestic processing could enable the country to retain more value from its agricultural products.

“We grow the crop. Someone else does more of the processing, builds a business around it and earns the larger return. Then Tinubu speaks of jobs while Nigerian factories struggle to compete. He has made production expensive and called the resulting hardship reform,” Atiku said.

He added that the administration should take responsibility for the country’s agricultural trade performance.

“A trade deficit alone does not explain every problem on our farms. But after more than three years in office, the President owns the decisions that have left farmers exposed and producers burdened. He cannot claim credit for every favourable statistic and disown a ₦796.40 billion reversal when the figures turn against him.”

Atiku also defended his proposed production subsidy for petroleum products refined in Nigeria, saying it would support qualifying products from Nigerian refineries, including modular refineries, while imported products would not qualify.

He said the subsidy would be capped, budgeted and independently audited, with measures to determine whether savings reach consumers and businesses.

Atiku also criticised the Tinubu administration’s Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) initiative, describing it as an ineffective relief measure.

He said the cost of converting vehicles remained beyond the reach of many poor Nigerians, while conversion kits were difficult to access and buses presented as palliatives remained unavailable to many people who needed them.

“Local refining is about more than the price at the petrol pump. Aviation fuel affects fares. LPG affects the cost of cooking. Petroleum products and feedstocks affect industries and the people they employ. Nigerians need practical relief they can actually access—not schemes whose costs and shortages put the promised benefits out of reach. The value of our resources must reach Nigerians beyond the refinery gate,” he said.

Atiku said his administration, if elected, would restore a production subsidy from its first day in office.

“My administration will begin restoring a transparent production subsidy from Day One. We will back farmers and processors with the same determination. Grow it here. Process it here. Refine it here. Create the jobs here. Make life affordable here,” he said.

He further accused the Tinubu administration of failing to sufficiently translate Nigeria’s natural and agricultural resources into affordable products and employment opportunities.

“Tinubu’s record is becoming painfully clear: Nigeria supplies raw crops and crude oil while Nigerians pay dearly for finished goods. A government that cannot turn our resources into affordable products and decent jobs has failed the people it was elected to serve,” Atiku said.

World.title: Inter-faith Dialogue: The Powerful Validation of Uba Sani’s Peace And Inclusion Trajectory
World.content:
By Nasir Dambatta

On Monday, October 5th in Kaduna, something rare happened. A Sheikh, a Reverend, a Professor, Defence Minister and a Monarch – Ambassador Nuhu Bamalli, stood on the same podium at the Government House Banquet Hall and said the same thing: Kaduna’s peace is real, and inclusion is the reason.

In a state once defined by recurring ethno-religious tensions, that consensus matters more than any political endorsement. When the pulpit and the minaret agree, it is no longer politics. It is validation.

The occasion was the Special Interfaith Dialogue organised by the Kaduna State Bureau of Interfaith with a deliberate theme: “An Overview of the Impactful Three Years of Peaceful Co-Existence and Inclusivity in Kaduna State; Unveiling the Secret.” What was unveiled was not a strategy document. It was a lived experience shared by leaders who have spent decades watching Kaduna burn.

Governor Uba Sani himself provided the context. “When we came into office, we inherited a state that was highly toxic and divided. As a Governor, he devised a workable peace model. “Our model is very simple. It does not need any study. It is about justice. It is about bringing everyone to the table.” It is a model he said he swore to on May 29, 2023, when he took his oath on the Glorious Qur’an to govern fairly irrespective of ethnic or religious affiliation. The result, he noted, is that Kaduna has not recorded any ethno-religious crisis in three and a half years.

That claim found powerful validation from the Christian community. Rev. Caleb Ma’aji, Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria in Kaduna State, did not speak in abstract terms. He spoke about roads. Three specific roads he requested at the 2024 Christmas Carol — Nasarawa-UNTL-First Bank, PAN Drive-Television Garage-Sabon Tasha, and Romi-Karatudu — two have been completed, one is nearing completion. He spoke about pilgrimage. For years, Christian pilgrimage to Jordan and Jerusalem had stalled; last year, 50 Christians were sponsored. He spoke about representation, praising the choice of Jerry Adams, a Christian, as running mate as a clear departure from an old culture of exclusion.

From the Muslim community, the validation was equally direct. Both Sheikh Gumi, Prof. Khalid Aliyu, Secretary-General of Jama’atu Nasril Islam, described Governor Sani as a peacemaker, a progress that has since become the signature mark of the current administration in the State.

Perhaps the most striking statistics came from Sheikh Haliru Maraya, who contrasted the past with the present. In the previous years, he said, Kaduna recorded 4,876 lives lost, 7,694 kidnapped, 1,660 insecurity incidents, 534 schools closed and 500 hectares of farmland abandoned. Today, all 534 schools have been reopened, farmers have returned to the 500 hectares, and communities that once fled are rebuilding. These are a proof that inclusion has a human dividend.

Even the doubters have been converted. Bishop David Bakare, National Secretary of the Pentecostal Fellowship of Nigeria, was disarmingly honest: “I didn’t vote for Sani in 2023… I didn’t know you… I didn’t believe in anything that you were going to do,” he confessed, before declaring that performance has now earned his support.

That is why the dialogue resonated beyond the walls of Government House. It was not simply a gathering to celebrate peace. It was an opportunity to reflect on how peace was built, why it has endured and what must be done to sustain it. And perhaps that is the real secret that was unveiled. Not the triumph of one man and not the victory of one political party.

Here is what it is: the growing acceptance that peace thrives when citizens feel included, when justice is visible and when development reaches communities without regard to faith, ethnicity or geography.

For many of the influential voices gathered at the dialogue — Muslim clerics, Christian leaders, traditional rulers, security chiefs – notably Minister of Defence – Major-General Chris Gwabin Musa and community stakeholders — those principles are precisely what they see reflected in Governor Uba Sani’s approach.

Whether history ultimately judges that approach a lasting model will depend on the years ahead. But on October 5th, one message rang out clearly from an unusual coalition that the State has rarely seen on one stage: Kaduna’s peace gains are real, inclusion matters and both are worth protecting.

For a state once symbolising some of Nigeria’s deepest fault lines, that is no small validation.

World.title: Africa Must Have A Say in How Its Minerals Are Priced, Says WiM-Africa
World.content:
Folalumi Alaran in Abuja

Africa must strengthen its influence over the global pricing and value determination of its mineral resources by developing stronger market intelligence, processing capacity, mineral data and commercial systems, the Executive Director of Women in Mining Africa (WiM-Africa), Dr. Comfort Asokoro-Ogaji, has said.

Asokoro-Ogaji is expected to advance the position when she participates as a roundtable speaker at the Shanghai Metals Expo 2026 in China in November.

The roundtable, convened by Shanghai Metals Market (SMM), will focus on ‘Eastern Pricing 2.0: Integrating Futures, Physical Markets, Industry and Finance for the Next Stage of Global Metals Pricing.’

According to Asokoro-Ogaji, the changing global metals market presents Africa with an opportunity to reconsider its position in the systems through which minerals are traded, priced and ultimately converted into economic value.

“Africa cannot build pricing power simply by having minerals beneath its soil. We must put our African mineral ecosystem together — our producers, geological and market data, processing capacity, standards, laboratories, commodity exchanges, financial institutions and regional value chains — if we want to become more relevant in the markets where value is determined,” she said.

She said the continent’s mineral strategy should move beyond negotiating better terms for the export of raw materials to developing the capacity to process, aggregate, certify, finance and trade minerals within stronger African value chains.

The issue is becoming increasingly important as global competition intensifies for copper, lithium, cobalt, nickel, rare earths and other minerals considered critical to industrialisation, advanced manufacturing and the energy transition.

Asokoro-Ogaji said Africa’s challenge was not merely to determine whether pricing influence was shifting from established Western markets towards emerging Eastern markets, but to ensure that the continent becomes a meaningful participant in the evolving global pricing architecture.

She said stronger African participation would require reliable geological and market data, mineral testing and certification systems, traceability, access to finance, regional trading platforms, processing facilities and stronger links between African producers and international buyers.

She added that the issue was particularly important for women-led and smaller mining enterprises, which often face barriers to credible market information, mineral testing, product specifications, finance and direct access to international buyers.

According to her, without these systems, many African producers would remain confined to the mine-gate level of the value chain, while a larger share of the value generated from their minerals would continue to be captured elsewhere.

She called for deeper cooperation among African governments, mining companies, commodity exchanges, financial institutions, geological institutions, laboratories, processors, traders, research organisations, women-led enterprises and regional bodies to strengthen the continent’s mineral market infrastructure.

Asokoro-Ogaji’s participation in the Shanghai roundtable follows the expansion of strategic cooperation between WiM-Africa and Shanghai Metals Market, providing a platform for engagement on mining, metals, battery minerals, market connectivity, knowledge exchange, technology and industry development.

She said Africa’s long-term objective should be to participate across the entire mineral value chain, from geological data and extraction to processing, finance, trading and value creation.

“Africa has mineral power. The next challenge is building the market architecture capable of translating that endowment into greater economic and pricing influence,” she said.

World.title: Cordros Wealth Summit 2026 Redefines Prosperity With ‘Wealth Beyond Money’
World.content:
Cordros Capital Limited, a leading financial services group in Nigeria, has successfully hosted the Cordros Wealth Summit 2026 with the theme ‘Wealth Beyond Money.’

The landmark event, which was held recently in Lagos, convened industry titans, macroeconomic experts, policy drivers and investors to expand the traditional definition of prosperity, moving beyond liquid cash and fiat assets towards structural legacy, social capital, wellness, character and risk governance.

​Delivering the keynote address, Founder and Group Executive Chairman of Rainoil Limited, Dr. Gabriel Ogbechie, emphasized that financial currency is merely a tool, while enduring wealth resides in real assets, scalable enterprises, character and social capital.

​Highlighting the exponential growth of asset markets over time, Dr. Ogbechie noted: “When you invest in shares, people work for you.”

He pointed to the stock market’s remarkable trajectory, expanding from N4.5 trillion to N5 trillion market capitalization in 2009 to its current N163.68 trillion valuation today, and cited the dramatic appreciation of real estate, where land in Ikoyi increased from N30,000 per square meter years ago to premium multi-million naira valuations today.

Going beyond balance sheets, Ogbechie urged attendees to invest deeply in non-financial pillars, emphasizing that social wealth is fundamentally defined by the value of one’s relationships, contact network, and mutual recognition.

He advised participants to actively nurture their connections in all endeavours while equally prioritizing character and personal integrity, posing a reflective question on whether one’s word truly holds as an unshakeable bond when subjected to a character check.

In addition to personal character, Ogbechie underscored the critical importance of health, well-being and philanthropy, advising attendees to take their physical fitness seriously through regular workouts and medical checkups while trusting God for the rest.

He further emphasized that true prosperity is tied to impact, asserting that no matter how much material wealth a person accumulates, failing to give back to the needy makes them inherently poor, and concluding that genuine wealth and good living are ultimately achieved through entrepreneurship and purposeful giving.

​Renowned economist and Chief Executive Officer of Financial Derivatives Company, Bismarck Rewane, delivered a comprehensive macroeconomic breakdown.

Drawing a distinction between the physical and social sciences, Rewane noted that social science outcomes take time to manifest, referencing global geopolitical tensions like the Middle East crisis.

​Addressing the Nigerian economy’s deep integration with global markets, Rewane highlighted shifting macroeconomic trends:

​Inflation & FX: Inflation dynamics are becoming more predictable, while exchange rate movements are becoming less destructive.

Addressing macroeconomic structures, Rewane noted that fiscal deficits and public debt, projected between 40.6% and 43.5% by 2030, are steadily transitioning into manageable pathways.

To further stimulate real economic growth, he strongly advocated lowering benchmark interest rates, emphasizing that high rates in the twenties restrict expansion and urging policy makers to align rates with inflation to strike a sustainable economic equilibrium.

​Reflecting on the group’s expansion, Group Managing Director of Cordros Capital Limited, Wale Agbeyangi, thanked the keynote speakers, panelists and guests for shaping an insightful forum.

He shared the evolution of Cordros Capital from a boutique stockbroking firm established in 2007 into a full-fledged financial services ecosystem.

​Over nearly two decades, Cordros expanded into Investment Banking (2010), Asset Management (2013), Trustees, Insurance Brokerage and Registrars, building a comprehensive platform covering wealth creation, accumulation, protection and intergenerational transfer.

​Speaking on industry shifts, Managing Director of Cordros Asset Management Limited, Gbolahan Aina, emphasized the changing nature of wealth and the democratization of investing.

Highlighting projections that global wealth will expand significantly with $30 trillion shifting into addressable market pools by 2030, Aina reiterated that wealth building is not reserved solely for Ultra-High-Net-Worth Individuals (UHNWIs).

Through structured mutual funds, equities, and alternative asset classes, retail investors can hedge against inflation and compound wealth long term.

Moderated by broadcast journalist Olive Emodi, a distinguished panel explored asset allocation, risk, and succession, during which CEO of Falcon Corporation Limited, Audrey Joe-Ezigbo, underscored the crucial role of fatherhood in empowering the girl child and building international-standard corporate governance.

She advocated unwavering confidence and systemic rigor in enterprise, noting that: “Shrinking does not help anybody shine.”

​Founder and CEO of Bestman Games Limited, ​Ambassador Nimi Akinkugbe, demystified wealth creation, noting that those who succeed analyze risk carefully before taking courageous action.

She warned: “If you transfer wealth without transferring capability, it amounts to catastrophe.” She added that if heirs lack interest in running a business, they can participate responsibly as shareholders.

CEO of Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX), Jude Chiemeka, highlighted the vast spectrum of diversification choices across equity, fixed income, and derivative products on the exchange, reminding investors to continuously evaluate risk profiles across their investment journey.

World.title: XEJet Launches Direct Abuja — Gusau Flight Services
World.content:
Kasim Sumaina in Abuja

XEJet Limited, a premium airline, has launched its inaugural flight service to Gusau. The new route establishes a direct air link between Abuja and Zamfara State.

The new service, which connects Abuja directly with Gusau, the capital city and economic heart of Zamfara State, further expands the airline’s local network and its connectivity across Nigeria. Flights are scheduled to operate twice weekly using the Embraer ERJ-145MP aircraft.

The inaugural flight departed the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja at 2:00pm on Monday, 5th October, 2026 and arrived safely at Gusau International Airport, where a brief reception was held to mark the historic occasion.

Ahead of departure, the General Manager of XEJet Express, Hamzat Bukar, welcomed Zamfara State officials, dignitaries and other guests aboard the inaugural flight.

Bukar, said that the new route supports tourism, trade, and cultural exchange between Zamfara State and the rest of Nigeria, while strengthening the airline’s connections with key local markets.

He revealed that the service will make travel more accessible and convenient for business travelers, government officials, and families alike. “We are committed to supporting the growth of the region and delivering the safe, reliable service our passengers expect.

“This launch forms part of XEJet’s continued expansion across Africa, and we look forward to announcing even more milestones in the near future,” he added.

Receiving the inaugural flight at the Gusau International Airport, the airport’s Managing Director, Kabir Yahaya Gusau, expressed his delight over the successful launch and safe arrival of the aircraft.

He said, “Today marks the first time Gusau International Airport has welcomed passengers, and I am delighted to say everything went smoothly. I would like to sincerely thank the management of the airline for partnering with us and giving the people of Zamfara a smoother travel opportunity.”

World.title: NSCIA Backs State Policing, Mobilises Muslims for 2027 Elections
World.content:
Olawale Ajimotokan in Abuja

The Nigerian Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA) led by the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar has backed the legal amendment seeking the constitutional amendment that will decentralise the operation of Nigeria Police.

The council adopted that resolution in a communique issued Wednesday at the end of its General Assembly held in Abuja on October 1, 2026.

The communique was signed by its President-General, Abubakar and Secretary-General, Prof. Ishaq Oloyede.

NSCIA called for an urgent and a comprehensive reform of Nigeria’s security architecture and reiterated that it would support state policing, provided the reform that requires approval of at least 24 houses of assembly before it can advance to the next stage of the constitutional process is anchored on professionalism, constitutional safeguards, impartiality, accountability, sustainable funding, respect for fundamental rights and effective coordination between federal and state security institutions.

NSCIA also urged all government agencies to respect the right of muslim female students, corps members, female personnel in the security agencies and staff in other work places to use hijab as their fundamental human right.

The Council tasked Muslims to obtain their National Identity Numbers (NINs) and Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and participate fully in the process of selecting Nigerian leaders at all levels in the 2027 elections

Also worthy of note, it faulted the authorities of the University of Ibadan, Obafemi Awolowo University and University of Lagos on their hostile dispositions to the Supreme Court judgement, which favoured the use of hijab in their International Schools.

NSCIA berated the tertiary institutions for their futile attempts to re-designate such schools as private (despite being established by public institutions) ostensibly to manipulate court judgements against the right of willing female students to use hijab in public schools.

It urged the aforementioned tertiary authorities to retrace their steps by being law-abiding and inclusive.

Although it acknowledged the efforts of the government to stimulate the economy, the NSCIA charged the federal government to expedite action on drastically reducing the cost of transportation and food to alleviate the hardship being faced by ordinary Nigerians.

The Council also adopted the 2026 report of the National Hajj Commission of Nigeria (NAHCON) and endorsed its recommendations to reposition the Hajj industry in Nigeria for excellence.

The meeting was attended by prominent Emirs, Obas, Chief Imams, Chiefs, Principal Officers of the Council, renowned Islamic scholars, leaders of major national Islamic organisations and delegates from all the states of the federation and the FCT.

World.title: NLC Declares Indefinite Strike in FCT Over Teachers’ Welfare
World.content:
Olawale Ajimotokan in Abuja

The Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Council, with effect from Wednesday declared a total and indefinite strike paralysing all public and private sector operations across the nation’s capital over unresolved welfare disputes of FCT teachers.

The NLC issued the directive following the expiration of a seven-day ultimatum issued to the FCT Administration on September 8, 2026, demanding the resolution of the stated issues

The NLC FCT Council Chairman Comrade Knabayi S. Adalo, described in a communique the FCTA’s official response to the ultimatum, as “ambiguous, dismissive, and totally unacceptable”.

The NLC appealed to parents, residents, and civil society organizations in the FCT to support the industrial action, warning that failure to act will lead to the total collapse of the territory’s education sector

At the centre of the dispute is the FCTA’s implementation of a “vacancy clause,” which conditions teacher promotions on available establishment vacancies.

The NLC reckoned that teachers are recruited specifically by the FCT Universal Basic Education Board (FCT UBEB) and the FCT Secondary Education Board (FCT SEB) to teach, making them distinct from core civil servants or pool staff.

The union noted that vacancy-based promotion schemes applied to pool officers lead to severe career stagnation and demoralization for educators.

In light of this dispute the Congress directed all public and private sector workers, including affiliate unions across schools, hospitals, offices, and government establishments, to stay away from work starting October 7 until all demands are met.

It has also instructed enforcement committees to mobilize and monitor compliance across the territory.

“Teachers are not core civil servants nor pool staff and cannot be subjected to vacancy-based promotion meant for pool officers.

“The FCTA’s attempt to sustain industrial harmony without addressing injustice is mere wishful thinking.

“There can be no peace without justice,” Adalo stated.

The Council’s key demands include: immediate abolition of the vacancy clause as a requirement for teacher promotions, inclusion of eligible 2025 candidates to write their promotion examinations alongside or before 2026 candidates; and reversal of redeployment and demotion letters issued to directors benefiting from the Harmonized Retirement Age for Teachers Act, 2022, alongside the dissolution and reinstatement of management teams at FCT SEB and FCT UBEB.

Chiefs might have to drop Petersen for Learner

World.title: Jacob Zuma hospitalised in KZN: Here’s what we know
World.content:
Former president Jacob Zuma has been hospitalised in KwaZulu-Natal, with the MK Party moving to allay concerns over his health. Image: Flickr

Former president Jacob Zuma has been hospitalised in KwaZulu-Natal, with the MK Party moving to allay concerns over his health.

Zuma was admitted to hospital after campaigning in the province this week.

The MK Party says the 84-year-old underwent a routine medical check-up and is well.



However, reports surrounding his admission differ.

JACOB ZUMA HOSPITALISED

Initial reports indicated that Zuma had taken ill while campaigning in Msinga on Tuesday before being admitted to hospital.

A report states that an eyewitness saw Zuma arrive at hospital by ambulance.



However, the MK Party has played down concerns over the former president’s condition.

Party spokesperson Sifiso Mahlangu said Zuma undergoes routine medical checks twice a year.

“The president is not unwell. He is very much well and alive; it was a regular check-up,” Mahlangu said.



The party also said Zuma was in good spirits and expected to return to the campaign trail .

MK PARTY SAYS ZUMA IS WELL

Mahlangu said he had spoken to Zuma and maintained there was no cause for alarm.

He said Zuma had undergone routine checks, including blood tests.



According to another report, a family associate said that Zuma had been feeling unwell, but that his condition was not serious.

The associate said the hospital visit coincided with his scheduled medical check-up.

Other reports indicated that Zuma had already been discharged and returned to his Nkandla home.



The MK Party has not disclosed further details about the former president’s health.

ZUMA ON THE CAMPAIGN TRAIL

Zuma remains the leader and public face of the MK Party as South Africa heads towards the local government elections.

He has been campaigning in KwaZulu-Natal ahead of the polls.



The former president served as South Africa’s head of state from 2009 until his resignation in February 2018.

He later backed the newly formed MK Party ahead of the 2024 general elections and subsequently became its leader.

Zuma’s latest hospital visit comes as the party steps up its campaign ahead of the local government elections.



The MK Party maintains that Zuma is well and plans to resume campaigning on Friday.

But the report has found that consumers are taking less risks with credit.

READ | Consumers urged to settle debt amid paused rate hike

Home loan ownership has fallen from 21% to 14% year on year with personal loans, overdrafts and vehicle finance also down.

Behavioural scientist Kele Boakgomo said South Africans are defending what they have.

World.title: IMF says indebted governments must tighten their belts
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The International Monetary Fund has called on governments to reign in their borrowing.

It comes amid growing debt issues around the world due to higher interest rates.

IMF managing director Kristalina Georgieva was speaking before IMF and World Bank annual meetings to be held in Bangkok next week.

READ | Reserve Bank hikes interest rates by 25 basis points

She said that debt levels are the highest they've been since the second world war and governments need to make tough political choices.

Yields on government bonds in the US - effectively the interest rate on the debt - have jumped in recent weeks.

It sparked concern that governments will have to give investors bigger paybacks to loan money.

Fears around France's debt position has dropped the Euro to a 17-month low in recent days.

World.title: Inter-Ministerial Committee meets after ConCourt ruling on asylum seekers
World.content:
JOHANNEBSURG - The Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) is expected to convene what it calls an urgent meeting following the Constitutional Court ruling on the processing of asylum applications.

Deputy government spokesperson, William Baloyi said the meeting held this Wednesday evening includes legal experts and key stakeholders to carefully consider the implications of the judgment and to identify a lawful, practical and sustainable way forward.

In July, the apex court ruled that parts of the Refugee Act were unconstitutional and invalid.

It found that any person seeking asylum cannot be denied access to the system for failing to provide the required documents or to report to a refugee reception office within the stipulated five-day window.

READ | Constitutional Court finds parts of Refugee Act unconstitutional

Baloyi said they are fully aware of the matter and are treating it with urgency.

“IMC on Migration is acutely aware of the uncertainty, concern, panic and confusion that have arisen following the recent Constitutional Court judgment concerning asylum seekers and the impugned provisions of the Refugees Act... “South Africans should be assured that government remains committed to maintaining the integrity of our migration system, upholding the rule of law and safeguarding national interest,” he added.

Earlier in the day, a protest was held outside Home Affairs’ Refugee Reception Centre in Durban.

Protesters demanded an end to asylum applications being processed at the facility.

They wanted the centre to stop accepting and processing asylum claims for foreign nationals.

World.title: Sibiya's bail hearing stalls
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The state's case against suspended Deputy National Commission Shadrack Sibiya has tightened with a wave of digital evidence.

The 16-year-old complainant's father, Mr M, who worked as Sibiya's bodyguard, has revealed that he has almost 300 recordings of the disgraced top cop.

He said he had been keeping evidence records of Sibiya’s criminal activities

The court heard that Mr M also preserved photo evidence, vehicle-camera footage and vehicle-tracking information.

Sibiya’s wife, Sizakele Dlamini, filed an affidavit in the Randburg Magistrate’s Court claiming Mr M threatened her and said he would release documents about Sibiya to the police.

Mr M claimed that he had been documenting Sibiya’s movements and possessed sensitive information regarding certain individuals’ disappearances, of which Sibiya was allegedly aware of.

Meanwhile, prosecutors have shut down Sibiya's claim of consensual sex with an 18-year-old because the teenager wasn't sober at the time.

The state has welcomed the defence's evidence placed on record.

The material includes WhatsApp messages and audio recordings that the state says implicate the top cop.

The case has been postponed to Tuesday, a day after Sibiya's expected SAPS disciplinary hearing.

For now, he remains in custody.

eNCA reporter Pule Letshwiti-Jones has more details in the video above.

World.title: OUTA opposes plan to slash fuel levy for RAF
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - OUTA has warned that reducing the Road Accident Fund (RAF) levy will do little to fix the fund’s deepening financial crisis.

According to OUTA CEO Wayne Duvenage, RAF is underfunded but he argued that its problems are largely rooted in years of mismanagement, rising costs and maladministration spanning over a decade.

Duvenage comments come as the Department of Transport announced the consideration of a new funding model for the troubled fund, including a possible reduction in the RAF levy.

But Duvenage opposes the plan.

“When it comes to paying an annual fee to feed a levy such as this, as opposed to small incremental amounts as you fill up each time, it's much easier to collect it in the fuel price than trying to get people to pay a thousand or two thousand rand at the end of the year when they come to license their car, which is another thousand rand. “So, we must find a solution to this problem, but the solution lies not necessarily in the revenue collection, it lies in the way the Road Accident Fund has been badly managed,” he said.

According to the RAF website, the main income it receives is a levy based on fuel sales known as the RAF Fuel Levy.

“The RAF fuel levy income is a charge levied on fuel throughout the country and the quantum of the RAF fuel levy per litre is determined by the National Treasury on an annual basis, whereas total fuel sales are influenced by a number of macro-economic factors," RAF said

There are two main variables that determine the income of RAF, this includes petrol and diesel sold per annum and the rate of the levy.

RAF explains how the levy can be viewed as a compulsory contribution to social security benefits which is used only for the specific purposes as provided for in legislation

World.title: Number Of The Day | 2% Down: Why The JSE Sell-Off Matters For The Rand And Fuel Prices | 07 October 2026
World.content:
Why A Falling JSE Can Reach Much Further Than Your Investment Portfolio

A bad day on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange can look like a story for traders and pension-fund managers. But when falling shares arrive alongside a weaker rand and rising oil prices, the consequences can travel quickly beyond the market and into ordinary household budgets.

That is what makes the current combination of pressures worth watching. The JSE fell more than 2% on Wednesday, with resource and financial shares among the sectors under strain. At the same time, the rand weakened as the US dollar strengthened, while global oil prices climbed. Reuters reported Brent crude above $102 a barrel during Wednesday's global market sell-off.

Those movements are connected.

When investors believe US interest rates may remain higher or rise further, dollar-denominated assets can become more attractive. That can strengthen the dollar and

put pressure on currencies such as the rand. For South Africa, a weaker currency matters because the country buys oil on international markets in dollars.

That means South Africans can be squeezed from two directions at once: the global price of oil can rise while each dollar also becomes more expensive in rand terms.

The fuel-price problem does not stop at the pump

This matters particularly now because motorists have already absorbed a substantial October fuel-price increase. South Africa's regulated fuel-price system reflects, among other factors, movements in international petroleum prices and the rand-dollar exchange rate. Reuters reported that petrol prices were set to rise by as much as 12% from 7 October, while wholesale diesel prices would increase by 10%.

Another sustained period of expensive oil and rand weakness would therefore matter well beyond motorists filling their tanks. Fuel is embedded in the cost of moving food, goods and people around the economy. Businesses facing higher transport and operating costs must decide whether to absorb those increases or pass some of them on to customers.

That is how a market story can become an inflation story.

The South African Reserve Bank is already paying close attention to that risk. Its October 2026 Monetary Policy Review says global inflation rose during the first half of the year as energy disruptions lifted transport and production costs. It expects South African inflation to remain above 5% until the second quarter of 2027 and warns that persistent fuel, administered-price and food shocks could become embedded in inflation expectations.

Interest rates make the chain even more important

The Reserve Bank raised its policy rate by 25 basis points in September to 7.25%, taking cumulative increases between April and October to 50 basis points. It has identified upside risks to inflation and specifically pointed to the renewed fuel-price shock.

That does not mean another petrol-price increase automatically produces another interest-rate hike. Monetary policy depends on a much wider set of economic conditions. But it explains why movements in oil, the rand and inflation expectations matter to anyone with debt.

Higher-for-longer interest rates affect home loans, vehicle finance, business borrowing and disposable income. What begins as volatility in currencies and commodities can eventually influence how much money households have left after servicing debt.

This is also why a 2% fall on the JSE should not be read simply as a scoreboard showing whether investors had a good or bad day. Markets are constantly repricing expectations about inflation, interest rates, currencies, company earnings and future economic conditions.

For South Africans, the more useful question is therefore not simply whether the JSE recovers tomorrow.

It is whether the uncomfortable combination underneath the sell-off — a strong dollar, a weaker rand, costly oil and persistent inflation pressure — begins to unwind, or settles in for longer.
