World.title: Man City should 'accept' punishment for rule breaches, says Lineker
World.content:
MANCHESTER - Gary Lineker has called on Manchester City to "accept whatever punishment" they are given for the good of the game after the club were found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules.

An independent commission said last week that City had arranged "sham" contracts with a number of their commercial partners to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs over a nine-season period, between 2009 and 2018.

The 10-time English champions, who continue to deny any wrongdoing, confirmed on Friday that they had appealed against the judgement.

No sanction has yet been decided upon but City could face substantial points deductions, a fine or even expulsion from the Premier League.

"Obviously, it looks really bad for Manchester City, and bad for the game, too," former England captain Lineker said on Wednesday at Leaders Week London 2026, held at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge stadium.

"When they talk about the 'Premier League conspiracy theories', you just think to yourself, 'Well, this is actually the last thing in the world that the Premier League would want'.

"So, I'd love to see Man City now just own it and just say, 'OK, we got it wrong but for the good of the game, we'll accept it and we'll accept whatever punishment comes our way and we'll carry on'.

"That would be a blessing and save their face a little bit at the moment, although it doesn't look likely."

Pressed as to whether City should be stripped of the three league titles they won during the period in question, 65-year-old Lineker said: "I wouldn't be surprised if it goes down that route. But who suffers from that? The players and the fans."

Kyle Walker, who spent eight years at City, winning multiple trophies before his departure in 2025, said that the players would always have the memories of their achievements, "whatever happens".

The Burnley right-back, speaking on Talksport, said: "It's something that we probably don't want to talk about because we want to be looked upon as winning (those) trophies and winning them the right way.

"It's very difficult because we've worked very hard for them, and not just us. I look at the fans that have travelled up and down the country, travelled abroad to Istanbul when we won the treble, and they deserve that night as well."

Article by AFP

World.title: Wajir patient isolated over suspected viral haemorrhagic fever
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The patient, a resident of Habaswein in Wajir South Sub-County, is currently admitted at Albadar Nursing Home. [File, Standard]

A 20-year-old man in Habaswein, Wajir County, has been isolated after presenting with symptoms consistent with a suspected viral haemorrhagic fever, following recent travel from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

The patient, a resident of Habaswein in Wajir South Sub-County, is currently admitted at Albadar Nursing Home, where he is being treated after developing fever, headache and cough. He was also found to have severe anaemia, with a haemoglobin level of 4g/dL.

According to a disease surveillance report filed at Habaswein Police Station, the patient told health officials that he had recently travelled to the DRC, where he worked as a “tan boy” on a cargo truck or trailer.

He reportedly developed fever and headache while still in the DRC on September 2, 2026, before traveling by trailer to Uganda, where he stayed for about five days and sought medical attention.

The report states that he was treated with antibiotics in Uganda before travelling by trailer to Malaba. From Malaba, he travelled by motorcycle to a relative's residence, where he stayed for approximately five days.

He later travelled by trailer to Nairobi and proceeded by bus to Isiolo, where he stayed for about 10 days before travelling to Habaswein by Probox vehicle. He arrived in the town around September 20.

Upon arrival, the patient sought treatment at Hilac Medical Clinic, where he was managed for pneumonia and septicaemia for about three days.

However, his condition did not improve and he was subsequently transferred to Albadar Nursing Home, where he remains admitted.

The report adds that the patient is receiving intravenous Augmentin and paracetamol and has been transfused with two units of whole blood.

“Despite the above interventions, the patient remains clinically unwell and sick-looking,” the report states.

Authorities have since placed the patient in isolation as investigations continue to establish the cause of his illness.

“Sample collection has been completed, and the specimen will be shipped to National Public Health Laboratories tonight,” the report states.

World.title: Complainant letters cannot be used to initiate judge's removal, court rules
World.content:
Chief Justice Martha Koome. [File]

A letter addressed to the Chief Justice seeking administrative intervention cannot form the basis for removing a judge, the Employment and Labour Relations Court (ELRC) has ruled.

Delivering a unanimous judgment in a case filed by Environment and Land Court Judge Anthony Ombwayo, a three-judge ELRC bench comprising Justices Jemimah Keli, Onesmus Makau, and Dr. Jacob Gikeri ruled that a letter written to the Chief Justice cannot simply be forwarded to the Judicial Service Commission (JSC) and treated as a petition for removal.

World.title: How KNEC plans to stop cheating in 2026 exams
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The Kenya National Examinations Council (KNEC) Chief Executive Officer Dr David Njengere. [File]

The Kenya National Examinations Council (KNEC) will use smart padlocks to secure all examination storage containers as more than 3.6 million candidates sit the 2026 national examinations and assessments.

KNEC Chief Executive Officer Dr David Njengere said the council would monitor the containers from its headquarters to prevent anyone from accessing examination papers before the scheduled times.

“Last year KNEC piloted the use of smart padlocks in 250 containers. This year all containers will be secured using the smart padlocks which will be monitored from the KNEC headquarters,” said Dr Njengere.

Under the system, officials will open containers at designated times. Officials will access Kenya Primary School Education Assessment (KPSEA) and Kenya Junior School Education Assessment (KJSEA) papers at 6 a.m., while centre managers will collect Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (KCSE) papers at 7 a.m. and 12:30 p.m.

However, Dr Njengere identified mobile phones as the biggest challenge in preventing examination malpractice.

“Mobile phones remain our biggest challenge in administration of KCSE examination,” observed Dr Njengere.

He warned that the council would not allow candidates or examination officials to have mobile phones at examination centres during examination sessions.

“Any contravention of this rule will constitute a malpractice as per the KNEC Act and the Rules and Regulations,” noted Dr Njengere.

The council will deploy 342,005 contracted professionals to administer and manage the examinations and assessments. They include centre managers, supervisors, invigilators, security officers and drivers.

For KCSE, KNEC will deploy 10,765 centre managers, 12,274 supervisors, 57,432 invigilators and 21,388 security officers. Each examination centre will have at least two police officers.

Centre managers will collect KCSE papers twice a day, and KNEC will place morning and afternoon papers in marked cartons to reduce mix-ups and unauthorised access.

KNEC has personalised question papers with candidates’ details, and examiners will receive anonymised scripts with those details removed.

The 2026 examination and assessment season will involve 3,634,846 candidates, a 6.13 per cent increase from the 3,424,836 registered in 2025.

KCSE rehearsals will take place on Friday, October 16. Examinations for papers with low candidature will run from Monday, October 19 to Friday, October 30, while papers with large candidature will run from Monday, November 2 to Friday, November 20.

KPSEA and KJSEA assessments will run from Monday, October 26 to Friday, October 30.

KNEC Chairperson Prof. Julius Nyabundi said the council was preparing for possible disruption from El Nino rains.

“As we start off the 2026 field administration season, one of the risks we contend with are the attempts to cheat in assessments and examination,” said Prof. Nyabundi.

He urged candidates, parents and examination officials to protect the integrity of the examinations, warning that malpractice could undermine public confidence in the education system.

“Cheating in examinations undermines public confidence in the credibility, fairness and quality of the entire education system,” noted Prof. Nyabundi.

KNEC will operate a 24-hour call centre with toll-free numbers for candidates, officials and members of the public to report incidents and seek assistance during the examination period.

The 2026 cycle will continue the implementation of Competency-Based Education assessments, including School-Based Assessments in primary, junior and senior school.

Grade 10 learners are undertaking their first School-Based Assessment, which will contribute 15 marks towards the Kenya Certificate of Basic Education.

World.title: Mbadi hits out at Sifuna, says opposition lacks economic agenda
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

National Treasury CS John Mbadi after opening new classrooms and administration blocks constructed by the M-Pesa Foundation at Ligongo Primary School in Suba South Constituency. [James Omoro, Standard]

The National Treasury CS John Mbadi has hit out at Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna, saying that criticising President William Ruto should not be an agenda for a presidential candidate.

Speaking when he opened new classrooms and administration blocks constructed by M-Pesa Foundation at Ligongo Primary School in Suba South Constituency, Mbadi said lack of economic agenda makes the opposition unsuitable to lead the country.

“I have heard of opposition leaders who want the presidency, but they do not have an agenda for the economic transformation of this country,” he said.

The CS claimed that none of the opposition leaders is suitable for the presidency.

“These opposition leaders cannot make any economic change in this country. They should not be elected,” he said.

He told Nyanza residents to shun the new wave of opposition led by Sifuna.

Mbadi claimed that opposition leaders lack political direction.

He said Sifuna had taken too long to unveil a political party that he will use to run for the presidency.

“Do not join the opposition bandwagon. We are just a few months away from the General Election, but Sifuna still doesn’t know a political party he will use to run for the presidency. They are still leaving in confusion,” Mbadi said.

He said Sifuna has not demonstrated how to improve this country’s economy.

“Former President Uhuru Kenyatta left the economy of this country in tatters. We have tried to improve it but we are not yet where we want it to be,” Mbadi said.

He urged Nyanza residents to support Ruto.

The CS said Ruto’s government had improved mega infrastructural projects across the country as part of economic transformation.

He cited the 74 km Mbita- Sindo- Sori road, Lake Victoria ring road and other infrastructure projects as some of the reasons residents should support Ruto.

“I urge you to support Ruto so that we can continue acquiring more development projects in this region,” Mbadi said.

World.title: Kericho Annex Prison under scrutiny over death of remand prisoner
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Brenda Chemutai, 19, who allegedly committed suicide inside the Kericho Annex Prison where she was awaiting trial for an offence of being in possession of bhang that was seized in a vehicle allegedly belonging to a senior police officer. [Courtesy]

Questions are mounting over security and accountability at Kericho Annex Prison following the death of a 19-year-old remand prisoner in a suspected case of suicide.

Her family is demanding answers about how she obtained a bedsheet and why they were not notified until nearly 10 hours after the incident.

Brenda Chemutai was reportedly found hanging from a double-decker bed at around 9 am when her fellow cellmates were having breakfast on Friday.

The cell had eight inmates, who had gone for breakfast, according to a police report.

However, her relatives state they were not informed until about 7 pm, after her body had already been taken from the prison and transferred to the Kericho County Hospital Mortuary.

The delay has raised serious concerns for the family, which calls for authorities to clarify what happened between the time Chemutai was discovered and when her next of kin were contacted.

Kericho East Directorate of Criminal Investigation (DCI) officer, Kennedy Apindi, said police have launched investigations following reports from prison officials that the incident was a suicide.

He mentioned that preliminary information indicated Chemutai allegedly used a bedsheet.

The family, however, insists that investigators determine when she was found, who discovered her, when the incident was reported to police, who authorised her body’s removal, and why her relatives were not notified immediately.

“We had spoken with Brenda. She was expected to be released around December, and by January we would all have been together at home,” said her sister, Phyllis Cherotich.

Cherotich added that the family had seen no signs indicating Chemutai intended to take her own life.

"Her death has shocked us deeply. She never mentioned any plans of this nature. We want to understand how this was possible given the level of security at the facility," she said.

The circumstances surrounding the alleged use of a bedsheet have also raised questions for the family.

Her uncle, Michael Rono, questioned how such an item came into Chemutai's possession while she was in a remand facility.

"I am deeply surprised. When one enters the prison, one is carefully searched. Where did the bedsheet come from? We ask the government to ensure justice is done," Rono said.

Chemutai had been in remand since 2024, with her relatives saying she was arrested while still a minor and had spent nearly two years awaiting the conclusion of her case.

She was being tried for the offence of possession of bhang in a vehicle allegedly belonging to a senior police officer.

Her death has consequently brought renewed scrutiny to not only what happened inside the prison but also the circumstances that led to her prolonged detention.

Youth activists from the Voice of Youth Organisation, led by Kelvin Kipchichir, have joined the family in demanding investigations into both the death and the case that resulted in Chemutai's detention.

Kipchichir claimed Chemutai was arrested alongside other suspects in a vehicle allegedly linked to an Officer Commanding Station serving in Kakamega.

According to the activists, police recovered 32 rolls of bhang from the vehicle, while some of the suspects allegedly fled, leaving Chemutai behind.

The claims have not been independently established.

Kipchichir questioned why Chemutai remained in custody for such a prolonged period and called for scrutiny of the circumstances surrounding the vehicle and its alleged connection to the police officer.

“We are concerned that an OCS in the National Police Service could allow a vehicle to be used by an individual with a known criminal record,” he said.

He called on the Ministry of Interior to establish who owned or controlled the vehicle and under what circumstances it was allegedly being used.

The activists said the vehicle was still at Kericho Police Station.

For the family, the tragedy has been compounded by personal loss. Chemutai's father died while she was in remand, while she leaves behind a young child.

Relatives said detectives had informed them that the person alleged to own the bhang had since been arrested and was being held in Kisumu.

But the immediate question for Chemutai's family is what happened during her final hours.

They want a clear account of the period between the reported discovery of her body at about 9 am and the notification of the family nearly 10 hours later.

They also want investigators to establish how the bedsheet allegedly used in the incident came into her possession and whether prison officers followed all required procedures after she was found.

The activists are calling for the inquiry to extend beyond the death of Chemutai to her arrest, the length of her detention and the handling of the case against her.

The family has demanded a transparent and independent investigation, saying it wants answers on how a teenager who entered the justice system while still a minor ended up dead in remand custody.

The family says it wants those questions answered before proceeding with burial arrangements.

World.title: Pregnant woman found dead by roadside in Kirinyaga with head, hip injuries
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The National Police Service (NPS) has launched investigations after the body of a pregnant woman was found by the roadside in the Itangi area of Mwea East Sub-County, Kirinyaga County.

The woman, identified as Catherine Njeru, was found early Friday morning along the Piai-Itangi Murram Road with visible injuries to her head and hip.

In a statement, NPS said the incident is being investigated as a suspected murder.

"The NPS condoles with the family, relatives, and friends of the deceased and commits to expeditious and conclusive investigations to ensure that any person or persons responsible for this barbaric crime are brought to justice," read the statement.

Police have urged residents of Itangi to remain calm and refrain from speculation as the investigation continues.

Anyone with information that could assist the investigation has been asked to report to the nearest police station or a law enforcement officer.

The matter is being investigated by Kirinyaga County Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) officers, local Sub-County police and Central Regional Police Command, led by the Regional Criminal Investigations Officer.

According to NPS, the Inspector General of the National Police Service has also been briefed on the incident and directed the Director of Criminal Investigations to expedite the probe and establish the facts surrounding the woman's death.

World.title: Ruto downplays rivalry over oil refinery in East Africa
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Former Nigeria President Olesugun Obasanjo, Ali Dangote, President William Ruto and Uganda President Yoweri Museveni during launch of the Lamu Refinery on September 30, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has played down suggestions of rivalry between Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania over competing refinery projects, saying East Africa’s growing demand for petroleum products can support several facilities across the region.

Speaking during a media interview at State House Mombasa, Ruto said Kenya had no objection to Uganda and Tanzania pursuing their own refinery projects, arguing that the different facilities could complement rather than compete with one another.

“There is no bad blood at all. There is no problem,” Ruto said.

His remarks came a day after he presided over the groundbreaking of the Lamu refinery project, which the government is positioning as a major component of a wider industrial complex on the Kenyan coast.

Ruto said he had discussed Uganda’s plans with President Yoweri Museveni and agreed that Kampala could proceed with a smaller refinery without threatening Kenya’s investment in Lamu.

He said Kenya would even be prepared to buy petroleum products from Uganda if they could reach the Kenyan market at competitive prices.

“If it is manufactured there in Uganda and the oil from that place is near Busia, and it can reach Busia at a lower price, we will buy oil from anywhere and bring it to Busia,” Ruto said.

The President argued that the size of the regional petroleum market meant there was room for more than one refinery.

“This one in Lamu cannot serve all of us; it will be necessary to expand,” he said, adding that East Africa had “enough opportunity” for multiple facilities.

Ruto also extended the same approach to Tanzania, saying Kenya could participate in a refinery project in Tanga if it is eventually developed.

“Even if the one in Tanga is built, we as Kenya will go and buy some shares there. There is no problem,” he said.

The comments point to a regional energy market in which petroleum products could move across borders depending on availability, transport costs and prices. Rather than treating refinery projects as competing national investments, Ruto said the facilities could strengthen economic cooperation within the East African Community.

The President said the Lamu refinery would also address some of the challenges Kenya faces from dependence on imported refined petroleum products.

“Lamu will give us an opportunity to have fuel without the fluctuations that we have now,” he said.

He linked the proposed refinery to the need to reduce Kenya’s exposure to international oil price shocks, disruptions caused by instability in oil-producing regions and costs associated with transporting petroleum products over long distances.

Ruto said local refining could reduce expenses related to insurance and transportation while providing Kenya with greater access to locally processed fuel.

However, he said the larger economic opportunity would extend beyond the refinery itself. The government plans to develop industries around the facility, including petrochemical, chemical and plastics manufacturing.

The refinery could also provide raw materials for industries producing fertiliser and bitumen, potentially reducing reliance on imports of some petroleum-based products.

The broader development is expected to create opportunities for employment, investment and trade while strengthening Lamu’s position as an industrial and logistics centre.

Ruto said Kenya’s policy would be guided by competitiveness, allowing businesses and consumers to obtain petroleum products from whichever regional facility can supply them efficiently and at favourable prices.

The President maintained that Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania therefore did not need to view their refinery plans through the lens of rivalry.

Instead, he said, multiple facilities could create a larger and more integrated petroleum market capable of serving the needs of East Africa.

World.title: Outrage as KDF officers detain human rights team along Malindi-Lamu highway
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Activists clashed with police at a Gamba roadblock after being stopped en route to Lamu. [Vocal Africa]

Six members of Muslims for Human Rights (MUHURI), including five staff and a board member, were detained by Kenya Defence Forces (KDF) officers along the Malindi-Lamu highway, prompting condemnation from human rights organisations.

The incident occurred on Monday as the team travelled from Lamu to Mombasa after a field mission. The officers reportedly intercepted them between Gamba and Minjila, detained them for about two hours, then released them.

The Kenya Human Rights Commission (KHRC) and MUHURI said the officers covered their faces and refused to identify themselves when the human rights team challenged them.

The five staff members were identified as Francis Auma, Abdulrahman Mwanga, Fredrick Okado, Lathan Yusuf and Mohamed Abdla, while the board member was identified as Khelef Khalifa.

In a joint statement, the two organisations said the officers' actions violated a High Court ruling by Justice Bahati Mwamuye requiring security personnel to wear clearly visible name tags or identifiable service numbers on their uniforms.

The ruling also prohibits security officers from wearing hoods, balaclavas or face masks to conceal their identities.

"We call on the KDF and other security agencies to comply with the court order. Officers who violate the directive should be held accountable and face legal consequences," the joint statement read in part.

The organisations also demanded immediate compliance with a recent court order lifting the dusk-to-dawn curfew that had been imposed for more than a decade along the Minjila-Lamu highway.

They argued that the curfew had created conditions for arbitrary stops, harassment and detention of travellers using the route, citing the detention of the MUHURI team as an example.

The organisations urged security agencies to respect court orders and protect the rights of travellers using the highway.

However, a senior Anti-Terror Police officer aware of the incident told The Standard that the officers from the Border Police Unit (BPU) manning such roadblocks and tactical borders conceal their faces to protect their identities.

"In high-risk areas prone to insurgent or terrorist retaliation, including Kanyoyo in Kitui heading to Garissa, Moyale and Lamu, anonymity is framed as a matter of personal and operational survival," she stated.

World.title: Who is Zack Polanski, the ‘eco-populist’ rattling the UK’s establishment?
World.content:
London — The leader of the UK’s Green Party, Zack Polanski, will on Thursday challenge the political establishment by taking on the ruling Labour Party in a special election for the seat held by former prime minister Keir Starmer.

Polanski, with his deep reserve of progressive policies and an active presence on TikTok cuts a markedly different figure to Starmer, who consistently alienated his Labour Party’s left-wing and developed a reputation as a stilted, ineffective communicator.

That contrast helped Polanski and the Greens gain traction as a popular left-wing alternative to the governing, center-left Labour Party, which has been bleeding voters in recent years over its stance on issues like welfare spending, trans rights and the war in Gaza. Polanski even said on more than one occasion that his party “is here to replace Labour.”

But that momentum has largely stalled since Starmer resigned as prime minister in the summer following enormous pressure from his party. He stepped down as a member of parliament (MP) last month, triggering the by-election.

In Starmer’s place, a more formidable opponent has emerged. Andy Burnham, the current prime minister, is widely seen as a better political operator and more capable of appealing to a broad spectrum of voters, including the progressives Polanski has been targeting.

Britain’s new Prime Minister Andy Burnham took office in July. Christopher Furlong/Getty Images

So the outcome of this by-election – in the central London constituency of Holborn and St. Pancras – represents more than just Polanski potentially becoming an MP.

It pits the Greens and Labour directly against each other for the first time since Burnham took office, acting as the first major electoral test for the new government as well as a barometer of the Greens’ ability to compete with a rejuvenated Labour.

If Polanski wins on Thursday, it will be a stern warning for the new prime minister and could be an early indicator that Britain’s left flank has irrevocably split. But if he loses and Labour candidate Sagal Abdi-Wali holds the party’s seat, it will serve as a sign that Burnham has managed to pull progressives back into the Labour Party and slow its electoral decline.

Differing stances over the war in Gaza and antisemitism are central to that split, and to this by-election. Many Muslim voters have said they will not vote Labour because they think the government has not acted strongly enough over Gaza.

This weekend, the Greens adopted a controversial motion classifying Zionism, which Jewish groups sometimes define as a right to Jewish self-determination, as a form of racism, calling it an “ethnonationalist political project.”

Polanski, who is Jewish and changed his name from David Paulden when he was 18 to honor that heritage, did not vote on the motion nor mention it in his speech to the conference. He describes himself as an “anti-Zionist.” Israel responded by banning Polanski from visiting the country.

On Wednesday, a fresh storm broke out in British media over a reported friendship between the Green Party member who proposed the motion and a man convicted in the United States on al Qaeda terrorism charges.

Any split in the left comes at a critical moment in British politics, with Labour (and the Greens) also focused on containing a rising right-wing wave, most clearly signaled by the rapid ascent of the hard-right populist party, Reform UK.

Who is Polanski?

A self-described “eco-populist,” Polanski, 43, was catapulted onto the national stage last fall when he secured a surprise victory in the Greens’ leadership election, beating two of the party’s four MPs to claim the top job. Before that, he was still a little-known local politician, representing the Greens in the London Assembly.

The broad brushstrokes of Polanski’s image go something like this: to his admirers, he is an antidote to the stiff technocratic tendencies of more mainstream politicians; a gifted communicator willing to adopt the bold left-wing policies Labour has largely shied away from.

To his detractors, he is vague and unable to pin down the details of his own policies.

More recently, his social media use sparked controversy after he criticized the police’s response to an antisemitic attack in north London and, in a separate incident, reposted a photo that some interpreted as threatening Nigel Farage, the leader of Reform UK.

Zack Polanski is running to become an MP for the central London constituency of Holborn and St Pancras. Toby Shepheard/AFP/Getty Images

Still, under his leadership, the party has commanded national attention, building on its best general election performance when it secured four parliamentary seats in 2024. By May, the Greens’ rise seemed astronomic – they briefly polled as high as Labour and the center-right Conservatives, the two parties which have dominated British politics for decades, and enjoyed historic gains in spring local elections.

While Polanski has tried to link the climate crisis to other issues, he has largely prioritized immediate everyday concerns, such as the cost of living and suggestions of public ownership of water and other utilities, alongside other progressive initiatives like championing a wealth tax and rent controls, while also adopting a pro-Palestinian stance.

Polanski has claimed credit for pushing Labour further to the left, most recently saying his party was responsible for influencing Labour’s shifting stance on the Middle East, including the government’s recently announced sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.

Actor turned politician

A former actor, Polanski’s strength lies in his communication. He hosts his own nightclub nights and holds weekly conversations with academics, activists and journalists on his podcast “Bold Politics” on ideas like an extreme wealth line (a proposed globally agreed limit for an individual’s net worth), re-nationalizing water companies and rejoining the European Union.

But he is prone to slip-ups too – in one disastrous interview shortly after becoming leader he seemed to confuse the national debt and deficit. Months later, he more carefully laid out his economic policy at a left-wing think tank event, though it remains “vague,” said Laura Serra, a political scientist at the London School of Economics.

“People don’t really know what they (the Greens) stand for, what they’re going to do,” she added.

While Polanski’s almost constant media presence has given him a far higher profile than previous Green leaders, analysts argue that the party’s increasing popularity has less to do with him and more to do with the shifting political climate in the UK.

A Green Party sign displayed outside a house. Carl Court/Getty Images

And at the same time, Green parties across Europe have become more influential, propelled by growing support among recent graduates and benefiting from “changing societal cleavages,” said James Dennison, a political scientist at the European University in Florence, who has studied the Greens for more than a decade. “The change is more rapid in the UK, and it’s exaggerated partially because of the electoral system, so it takes them longer to break through, and when they do, they go faster.”

Polanski self-consciously forms part of a wider populist trend too; he describes his approach to messaging as “substance with clickbait” and an alternative designed directly to confront the right-wing populism of Reform, and its Trump-supporting leader Nigel Farage.

“Populism is about the 99%, the vast majority… against the very, very wealthy… Trump and Farage come from the 1% and want to protect the interests of the elite,” Polanski told Bloomberg earlier this year.

This simultaneous rise of the Greens and Reform could fracture Britain’s political landscape, in which the first-past-the-post electoral system typically favors two or three major parties.

So, regardless of who wins on Thursday, the Greens even being competitive in a traditional Labour stronghold like this is indicative of how the smaller, more radical parties are increasingly challenging the mainstream.

World.title: What is pneumonic plague and how dangerous is it?
World.content:
A 28-year-old lab researcher at a Russian institute dedicated to studying plague and dangerous pathogens died of pneumonia of an “unknown” origin.

The Irkutsk Research Anti-Plague Institute operates in Siberia, where several other people are quarantined. Rospotrebnadzor, the Russian agency that oversees infectious disease, has downplayed the link between the researcher’s death and her work, but the case has prompted questions about the type of plague that causes pneumonia.

The US State Department and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said they are monitoring the situation closely. The World Health Organization said Monday it’s in contact with Russian health authorities to verify what happened, what testing is underway and any potential international public health implications.

“Based on unofficial information available, the public health risk to the general population appears to be low,” a WHO spokesperson said, adding that its risk assessment would be updated once more information was available.

What is pneumonic plague?

Pneumonic plague is a rare, deadly lung infection caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. Scientists consider pneumonic plague the most dangerous form of the infection.

There are other forms of plague stemming from Y. pestis that attack different parts of the body.

The most common form, bubonic plague, often develops after a flea bite or when the bacterium enters through a cut or break in the skin. The infection triggers swollen, painful lymph nodes and can progress to septicemic plague.

Septicemic plague infects the bloodstream, potentially leading to organ failure, it can also come directly from a flea bite.

Pharyngeal plague attacks the throat after someone eats infected meat.

The bacteria Yersinia pestis causes plague, including the most common, bubonic plague, which typically results from the bite of an infected flea. Pneumonic plague is the most serious form of the illness. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention/Getty Images

How is pneumonic plague transmitted?

Pneumonic plague is the only form of the bacterial infection that passes directly from person to person. Respiratory particles carry it when a person coughs or sneezes. Droplets from infected animals can also transmit it.

The last documented person-to-person transmission of pneumonic plague in the United States dates back to 1924, during an outbreak in Los Angeles.

What are pneumonic plague symptoms?

With pneumonic plague, particles lodge in the lungs and can trigger severe pneumonia, making breathing difficult. Symptoms can begin within 24 hours of infection.

Other symptoms include fever, chills, headache, body aches, dizziness, weakness, fatigue, nausea, vomiting and diarrhea.

Without treatment, it is nearly always deadly.

How is pneumonic plague treated?

Doctors can treat plague with at least 10 to 14 days of antibiotics. Most commonly they use ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, moxifloxacin, gentamicin, and streptomycin. Patients that get antibiotics within the first 24 hours of infection have the best chance of surviving.

Doctors may also support someone with supportive care and provide supplemental oxygen, fluids and encouragement to rest.

Is there a vaccine for plague?

Although plague vaccines have been in use since the 19th century, it wasn’t clear they offer protection from pneumonic plague.

The WHO doesn’t recommend vaccination, except for high-risk groups such as laboratory personnel who are constantly exposed to the risk of contamination.

Why does plague still happen today?

Although people may be most familiar with plague from reading the Bible or historical literature — or as a metaphor to describe broader pestilence and poverty, according to infectious disease expert Dr. Tyler Evans — it persists today.

Known as the “Black Death” in the 14th century, the infection killed more than 50 million people in Europe. While antibiotics have made it more manageable, it remains present on every continent except Oceania.

Since the 1990s, most human cases have occurred in Africa, according to the WHO.

The last US death from pneumonic plague occurred in Arizona in July 2025, according to the CDC . The young man worked with sick cats and is believed to have contracted the infection from the animals. No one else exposed to the cats reported getting sick.

Evans, who wrote “Pandemics, Poverty and Politics: Decoding the Social and Political Drivers of Pandemics from Plague to Covid-19,” says the risk for plague is “getting worse as the result of ecological changes and particularly with the US pulling back on our public health infrastructure and measures.”

Plague, at least, can be quick to diagnose, he said. And “the antibiotics, first and second line, are very effective for this.”

Soldiers monitored a hospital in India, on September 27, 1994, during an outbreak of pneumonic plague. The soldiers were posted after more than 50 people escaped quarantine. John Moore/AP/File

Globally, how concerned do people need to be about getting sick?

WHO has said the risk to the general population appears to be low.

People with pneumonic plague feel sick very quickly, which can slow potential spread, according to Dr. Rutul Dalal, an infectious disease physician at Penn State Health St. Joseph Medical Center.

“It’s very difficult for someone to even walk, do their daily activities, let alone travel,” Dalal said. People can develop symptoms as early as 24 hours after exposure.

There are no direct flights between Russia and the US, he said, so by the time an infected person would reach the US they would likely already be exhibiting symptoms.

“Of course, you have to be careful, and you should keep this at the back of your mind … The world is a little village now, as I say — connected to each other. But at this point in time, compared to what we have been seeing, like during the Covid pandemic, this is not of that magnitude as of now, and hopefully remains contained as it is.”

For people around patients with plague, WHO recommends avoiding direct contact with those who are sick and urges caution around infected body fluids.

Workers caring for patients with pneumonic plague must wear standard protective equipment and may also take preventive antibiotics.

In case of exposure, health officials will also monitor family members and other close contacts of an infected person and provide them with antibiotics before they become ill. They also recommend routine hand-washing with soap and water.

World.title: Facing Russian stonewalling, Trump admin ramps up pressure for info as it struggles to plan for potential plague fallout
World.content:
The Trump administration is struggling to get clear answers about the death of a Russian laboratory worker at an institute dedicated to studying the plague and has formally escalated its request for information from the country, amid days of stonewalling from Russian officials about the mysterious circumstances surrounding the episode.

The death of the technician at the Irkutsk Research Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia immediately raised alarms throughout the administration, prompting a race to compile intel and plot for a potential public health response, according to multiple sources familiar with the matter.

But Russia’s reluctance to share information about the incident has complicated those efforts, leaving officials uncertain what broader risks it could pose — and how exactly to defend the US against them.

The US escalated its request for information, issuing a formal diplomatic communication, called a démarche, a source familiar told CNN late Tuesday.

“We have officially requested additional information from the Russian government,” a State Department spokesperson said. “We are also in official communication with other countries around the world to share information.”

“It’s incumbent upon Russia to obviously share more information with the world,” Secretary of State Marco Rubio said earlier Tuesday. “Maybe it’s bigger than we thought. We don’t know, but I think it would be reckless at this moment, given the limited information we still have, to speculate.”

US officials were in touch with the Russian government as early as last Friday, a State Department official said, including contact between the department’s health experts and the Russian Foreign Ministry. And that outreach has continued, an administration official said, as Rubio expressed hope Tuesday that the limited information sharing “will change in the next few hours and days.”

President Donald Trump told reporters outside the White House Tuesday afternoon that he had “call scheduled” to speak with Russian leader Vladimir Putin about the issue “very soon.” He added US agencies would have more information to report “probably tomorrow.” However, the Kremlin on Wednesday said no call has been arranged between Putin and Trump to discuss the Russian plague scare.

The US has gotten limited cooperation so far. What little information has come out of Russia has faced deep skepticism, with officials unconvinced that the Kremlin is being fully forthcoming, according to people familiar with the situation.

Still, until the administration knows more through intelligence collection and diplomatic outreach, officials are not taking steps such as putting travel restrictions into place to prevent any potential spread, according to a US official. The US already advises against travel to Russia due to various factors, including the possibility of wrongful detention and the war with Ukraine.

Among the critical questions still outstanding: whether the 28-year-old lab worker who died last week contracted pneumonic plague — a severe but treatable infection — or another, unknown infectious disease. Staff at the Anti-Plague Institute study a range of other dangerous diseases, including cholera, anthrax and brucellosis, according to the institute’s website.

US officials have also sought details on whether the disease was modified in any way, a process called gain of function that could dramatically alter the way the US and other countries might respond.

Rubio and other Trump officials have publicly downplayed the immediate threat to Americans, emphasizing that the administration is closely monitoring the situation and that pneumonic plague is treatable with antibiotics.

But behind the scenes, there is deep unease within the administration over the continued lack of insight, the people familiar with the situation said. Compounding those concerns is the Russian government’s outsized response, including quarantining the hospital where the lab worker was treated, according to the mayor of the Shelekhovsky district. Nearly 200 people are under observation, a regional news outlet reported.

The entrance to the grounds of the anti-plague institute in the city of Irkutsk, Russia, on October 6, 2026. AFP/Getty Images

“We don’t know a lot right now about what actually happened,” said one US official. “But one thing most of us feel certain about: The Russians are going to act like the Chinese did with Covid. They won’t be forthcoming.”

Still, Trump on Monday characterized the situation as a “big problem” for Russia, suggesting that the US might need to provide some unspecified level of aid.

In a statement, a State Department spokesperson said that several federal agencies were “closely monitoring the fatal case of suspected pneumonic plague,” but that many of the details surrounding it remained unconfirmed. They reiterated that Americans have long been advised not to travel to Russia for any reason.

“We encourage Russian authorities to share accurate information quickly and openly,” the spokesperson said.

In the days since the lab worker’s death, the National Security Council and State Department officials have led the administration’s push to gather information, piece together what happened and evaluate the potential risks, officials and others familiar with the situation said. Federal health agencies, including the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response, have also been involved in the cross-government effort.

A source familiar with the outreach said Trump officials have also backchanneled with the World Health Organization — the international health body that Trump pulled funding from soon after taking office, but that the government has continued to communicate with in emergency situations.

WHO seeks greater clarity

WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said Tuesday that Russian health authorities reported that no case of plague had recently been registered in Irkutsk region, in response to a WHO request.

He said Russian health authorities told WHO that an epidemiological investigation was conducted, and contacts were identified, tested and put under medical observation. The Russian health authorities did not detect any high-threat pathogens among the contacts, Tedros said.

Tedros said the WHO is seeking clarification from Russian authorities regarding “media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause.” Asked on Wednesday about the WHO’s request, the Kremlin dismissed the media’s coverage of the situation and referred journalists to the public health watchdog.

Some Western media outlets have reported a second case linked to the episode, citing unspecified Russian media reports. CNN is not aware of any such reports and neither local media in Siberia nor local officials have confirmed a second infection.

“If they’re not transparent, if they’re not open to independent accountability, how is it possible to trust the Kremlin is telling us the full and accurate information?” said Lawrence Gostin, a global health law professor at Georgetown University who has worked closely with WHO. “Clearly, on its face, the lab was conducting extremely high-risk research and using shoddy biosafety measures.”

The Anti-Plague Institute’s relatively remote location in eastern Russia, combined with the pneumonic plague’s limited ability to quickly spread, has given health experts some comfort that any immediate threat can be contained.

Pneumonic plague is a bacterial infection, unlike the highly transmissible coronavirus strain that sparked the 2020 pandemic. And while the plague is fatal if untreated, there are now effective and widely available antibiotics to treat it.

While there is little indication that the incident will touch off another global health crisis, officials and outside experts said it has nevertheless reinforced how difficult it can be to monitor and prepare for potential biological threats.

The Health and Human Services Department may have the medical stockpile necessary to combat conventional pneumonic plague, those officials and experts said. But there’s little certainty whether it could do the same against a modified version — or how long it would take to develop a treatment if needed.

Jennifer Nuzzo, an epidemiology professor and director of the Pandemic Center at Brown University School of Public Health, said the episode also comes as health response capabilities both in the US and globally have been diminished by funding cuts and the strain of responding to other crises. WHO has proposed slashing its budget following a $600 million shortfall triggered by the US’ exit.

America’s ability to handle a new public health response, meanwhile, “is severely diminished” amid its efforts to combat measles outbreaks, she said.

“We are talking about a very depleted system. God forbid you layer another pathogen onto the already laborious and difficult work of going after measles,” said Nuzzo. “That would be a nightmare.”

This story has been updated with additional details.

World.title: Whistleblower says Trump demanded FBI probe into protesters over a TikTok he saw
World.content:
The FBI opened preliminary investigations targeting anti-Immigration and Customs Enforcement protesters in Southern California, a former FBI intelligence official alleged in a whistleblower complaint, adding that she believed the move violated the law and agency policy.

The investigations were opened in early 2025 in the early weeks of the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown following demands from President Donald Trump and other administration officials, according to the disclosure by Jill Fields, a former supervisory intelligence analyst in the FBI’s Los Angeles field office.

CNN reviewed the complaint, which was filed by lawyers representing Fields to members of the Senate Judiciary Committee.

A Justice Department spokesperson told CNN said the DOJ will continue to “vigorously uphold the First Amendment rights of all Americans and restore the rule of law.”

“The DOJ and FBI have a responsibility to investigate any potential violations of federal law, and conspiracies to impede federal law enforcement and assaults on federal officers are against the law,” the spokesperson said in a statement. “Violence is not protected by the First Amendment. Politically motivated attacks will not deter us from doing our job.”

A statement from the White House also suggested the investigation was focused on violent acts, which it said are not protected by the First Amendment.

“These allegations are FALSE. The First Amendment does not protect violent rioting, obstructing law enforcement, and assaulting law enforcement,” White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said in a statement. “Assaulting and obstructing law enforcement is a crime. This administration has been clear: anyone who assaults or obstructs law enforcement will be arrested and prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law.”

CNN has also reached out to the FBI for comment.

In at least one instance, the FBI began preliminary investigations of protesters after the president demanded an investigation of people he saw in a TikTok video depicting demonstrators against ICE and Customs and Border Protection in Alhambra, California. The protesters were using bullhorns to warn neighbors about the presence of immigration-enforcement officers, Fields’ disclosure said.

Following the February 2025 protest in Alhambra, an analyst who worked under Fields “informed her that the squad had been ordered to run pre‑assessment checks on the two to four anti‑ICE and CBP protesters in the video accused of impeding an immigration arrest, even though FBI policy prohibits opening investigations based solely on First Amendment‑protected activity, and the squad did not yet have evidence of a crime,” lawyers representing Fields said in a letter to senators.

The investigations came after FBI Director Kash Patel told top FBI leaders that the president “was angry about the incident, and he wanted those protesters investigated and arrested,” the letter said.

In a letter to Patel and Attorney General Todd Blanche, citing the whistleblower complaint, Democratic Sen. Alex Padilla questioned the Justice Department on how many investigations into protestors were currently active and whether Trump had directed other, similar investigations.

Fields’ whistleblower complaint disclosed two separate incidents in which she said White House officials demanded the FBI investigate and arrest anti-ICE protesters.

A separate incident weeks earlier sparked a similar focus on free speech, according to Fields, when then-Acting Deputy Attorney General Emil Bove demanded the FBI investigate a group of anti-ICE protestors outside a federal building in California.

In both cases, Fields noted that First Amendment protections prohibited such investigations and potential charges unless other action beyond speech had taken place.

When she raised the issue with one superior, Fields says she was told it had to happen.

The former analyst said she was stripped of her team and lost support from FBI leadership in her Los Angeles office, pushing her to ultimately resign from the bureau.

This story has been updated with additional information.

World.title: FM probes with EU security chief developments in Red Sea, Horn of Africa
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty received a phone call from Kaja Kallas, the EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy.

Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Ambassador Nader Zaki said on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, that the call addressed bilateral relations between Egypt and the European Union and ways to develop and strengthen them. The two officials also discussed a number of regional and international issues of common interest.

The spokesman explained that the two officials discussed the rapidly unfolding developments in the Red Sea region and the Horn of Africa, as well as ways to de-escalate tensions and prevent their further expansion.

They reaffirmed the need to respect the sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity of states, and to intensify regional and international efforts to contain crises and create the conditions conducive to restoring security and stability.

They also stressed the importance of continuing coordination with the European Union to support de-escalation efforts and reach sustainable settlements to regional crises.

The talks also addressed Egypt’s pivotal and constructive role in de-escalating tensions, promoting political and diplomatic solutions, and maintaining the ongoing and distinguished coordination between Egypt and the European Union to achieve this common objective.

World.title: Egypt’s foreign reserves rise to $57.35 bln in September: CBE
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly affirmed the State’s commitment to developing the non-banking financial sector in its various activities given its vital role in driving the national economy, attracting investment and expanding the participation of the domestic and foreign private sectors.

The prime minister also highlighted the sector’s role in providing citizens with safe investment avenues under the full supervision of the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA), particularly through the Egyptian Exchange (EGX) and licensed investment funds.Madbouly made the remarks during a meeting he held on Tuesday evening October 6, 2026, in the New Capital with Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) Chairman Islam Azam to follow up on developments in the non-banking financial sector and activities under the authority’s supervision.

The meeting also reviewed the latest measures being taken by the FRA, within its supervisory and regulatory mandate, to enhance the efficiency of the capital market, insurance and non-banking finance sectors, increase their contribution to the national economy and protect the rights of market participants.The prime minister further said protecting the rights of participants in the sector is a top state priority, as reflected in the regulatory framework governing its activities and the successive decisions issued by the FRA, in line with market developments and the growing number of beneficiaries of the sector’s various activities, including insurance and non-banking finance.

During the meeting, Azam reviewed the latest developments in the regulatory frameworks governing these activities, including recent decisions aimed at improving service quality, meeting citizens’ needs, enhancing supervisory performance and strengthening the ability of the FRA and companies operating in the sector to detect, address and curb negative practices at an early stage.All measures, he said, would contribute to resolving customers’ complaints more quickly, raising their awareness of their rights and protecting their assets.

Azam also highlighted recent FRA decisions and their objectives, including strengthening safeguards for responsible financing, reducing defaults and fraud, combating impersonation and addressing various forms of money laundering.The measures include requiring financing entities to use one-time passwords (OTPs) to strengthen customer identity verification, ensure that customers are aware of the procedures and have agreed to the terms and conditions, and confirm their consent when financing is disbursed and used.

They also include requiring real-time connectivity with the credit information company and obliging consumer finance companies to obtain credit assessments based on customers’ behavioral analysis, while providing the necessary technological infrastructure in preparation for linking their databases with the FRA’s database.Azam explained that the full integration currently being organized and implemented between the FRA and all companies under its supervision would enable the FRA to access real-time and daily data from various markets and facilitate advanced analysis using artificial intelligence technologies.

Some of the resulting analysis will be made available to the market to help companies make more efficient decisions and improve the quality of insurance and financing products in line with customers’ actual needs, he added.In this regard, the FRA chairman said that providing customers with all information related to insurance and financing products and other investment vehicles, while informing them of their rights and obligations, constitutes a fundamental pillar of non-banking financial activities.

Other key pillars include data protection and effective mechanisms for complaints and grievances, he said, noting that these measures help assess the actual impact of financial services on customers’ lives and economic activities.

Azam also pointed to a number of recently issued decisions and instructions aimed at preventing misleading information and confusion between different savings and investment products and vehicles, as well as prohibiting the use of marketing statements or practices that could give customers inaccurate information.He added that the FRA’s implementation of financial inclusion targets under Egypt Vision 2030 is based on the need to protect and empower the most vulnerable groups.

Accordingly, the Authority is seeking to strike a careful balance between two complementary objectives: promoting the growth of financial activities by expanding access to financing and fostering innovation and competition, and protecting market participants to ensure that the desired growth is achieved in a responsible and sustainable manner without exposing customers to risks or burdens beyond their capacity.The meeting also addressed the FRA’s efforts to enhance the efficiency of companies and broaden the scope of risk management beyond credit risk to include market and operational risks.

Azam noted that Basel III standards are set to be applied to the non-banking finance sector starting next January. He also referred to a recently issued decision establishing controls for underwriting and pricing credit and guarantee insurance policies, including clear standards and stringent controls for developing reinsurance and risk-management policies.

The meeting further reviewed developments presenting promising investment opportunities, as well as the latest and upcoming offerings on the Egyptian Exchange, particularly those involving state-owned companies targeted for listing under the State Ownership Policy Document.It also highlighted the FRA’s role in building the capacities of employees of these companies and training them on the practical requirements for moving from temporary to permanent listing, including corporate governance, disclosure and transparency requirements.Azam also referred to ongoing preparations to launch short selling, stressing the importance of making the mechanism available alongside margin trading to improve price discovery, boost trading activity and attract new categories of investors, particularly foreign and young investors.

He noted that this development complements the launch of the financial derivatives market last March and the recent regulation of hedge fund activities, representing an integrated path toward modernizing the capital market under rules that ensure transparency and sound governance while protecting the rights of all parties.It is worth noting that the number of newly registered investors on the Egyptian Exchange exceeded 171,000 by the end of the second quarter of the current year, while trading values surpassed LE 6.4 trillion, an increase of approximately 78.3 percent compared with the second quarter of last year.

Meanwhile, investment funds recorded a 14.7-percent increase in net asset value by the end of the second quarter of the current year, reaching LE 471 billion across 224 funds.The number of fund units rose to 44 billion, with individuals accounting for 75 percent of the total, indicating growing confidence in investment funds as one of the key investment instruments in Egypt in recent months.

World.title: President al-Sisi heads to Korea at start of Asian Tour
World.content:
President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi will travel to the Republic of Korea on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, as the first leg of his Asian tour that will also include Malaysia and Indonesia.

The tour will begin with a state visit to the Republic of Korea, where President Sisi will hold talks with President of the Republic of Korea Lee Jae Myung, according to Presidential Spokesperson Mohamed al-Shennawy.

During the visit, the president will also participate in a roundtable with the heads and representatives of major Korean companies.

The tour will also include a state visit to Malaysia and a visit to Indonesia, the spokesman added.

World.title: PM reviews preparations for Egyptian energy journey session at Egypt Forum 2026
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly stated that the Egyptian Energy Journey session at Egypt Forum 2026 reviews the energy sector’s progress since 2014 through a comprehensive presentation of achievements, supported by figures, indicators, projects, and investments in electricity, renewable energy, and future expansion plans, alongside challenges and response methods.

Madbouly made the remarks during a meeting held to review the session’s axes, in the presence of Electricity Minister Mahmoud Esmat, Finance Minister Ahmed Kouchouk, Petroleum Minister Karim Badawi, and other senior officials, as part of preparations for Egypt Forum 2026 ordered by President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi to be held from October 19 to 24 at the St. Regis Hotel in the New Administrative Capital.

The Prime Minister pointed out that the session will also review the petroleum and mineral wealth sector’s progress during the same period, including developments in exploration, production, major discoveries, and efforts regarding foreign partners’ dues, stressing the need for the session to answer citizens’ questions and present future project plans.

World.title: Liberian Court Orders Arrest of Former Vice President in Transnational Drug Case
World.content:
A Liberian court has ordered the arrest of former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor, ex-wife of convicted warlord and former President Charles Taylor, along with former security officials, police officers and several European nationals. The order follows a grand jury indictment on drug trafficking and money laundering charges, one of the highest-profile criminal cases in the West African country’s recent history. Howard-Taylor has denied the allegations.

By Willie N. Tokpah

MONROVIA – A Liberian court on Wednesday ordered the arrest of former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor and more than 20 others in a sweeping drug trafficking and money laundering case that also names former security officials, senior police officers and nationals of Croatia and Ukraine.



Judge Ousman F. Feika of Criminal Court “C” in the capital, Monrovia, issued an arrest warrant directing the county sheriff to take the defendants into custody and bring them before the court. The warrant follows an indictment returned by a grand jury in Montserrado County, which includes Monrovia.

The defendants face charges including illicit drug trafficking; unlicensed importation, exportation, sale and transportation of controlled substances; criminal conspiracy, facilitation and solicitation; money laundering; and offenses involving objects allegedly intended for lethal use.

Former Officials Named

Besides Howard-Taylor, the defendants include Gerald Foley Smith, a former deputy director of Liberia’s National Security Agency, and Mark Quiah, a former deputy director of operations at the Liberia Civil Aviation Authority. Two senior police officers, Deputy Commissioner Anthony T. Blaye and Assistant Commissioner Wadell W. Kwarbo, are also named.

Foreign defendants include Croatian nationals Nikola Ivancic and Mihovil Vrovac and Ukrainian national Taras Zadereiko. Others named include Srdan Seles, Johnn David Garces and Sheik Bashiru Kante. The warrant lists further individuals known only by first names or aliases and says others have yet to be identified.

The warrant does not set out the specific conduct attributed to each defendant, nor does it say whether any alleged offenses took place outside Liberia.

Arrested at the Airport

The case dates to August, when Howard-Taylor was stopped while attempting to leave Liberia at Roberts International Airport and taken to Liberia National Police headquarters, according to the Justice Ministry. The government also charged three foreigners in absentia for their alleged roles in the network: Ivancic, Vrovac and Zadereiko.

Howard-Taylor has denied the central allegation. “I don’t know them,” she told FrontPageAfrica, referring to the three foreign nationals.

A Political Heavyweight

Howard-Taylor, 63, served as vice president from 2018 to 2024 under former President George Weah, the ex-football star. She entered politics after her former husband, ex-President Charles Taylor, left office in 2003. Charles Taylor was later convicted by an international war crimes court for sponsoring atrocities in neighboring Sierra Leone, and is serving a 50-year sentence in Britain.

The case is widely seen as a test of President Joseph Boakai’s pledge that no office is too high for the law to reach.

Wider Crackdown

The indictment comes amid an intensified government push against international drug networks using Liberia as a transit point. In July, Liberia announced what it described as its largest-ever cocaine seizure — almost four tonnes, with an estimated value of about $317 million. Officials have stressed that the seizure and the case involving Howard-Taylor are separate investigations.

West Africa has long served as a transit route for South American cocaine bound for Europe, and authorities said the July seizure was believed to be headed there.

Next Steps

An indictment is a formal accusation, not a finding of guilt, and all defendants are presumed innocent. Once the warrant is served, the defendants are expected to appear before the court, where bail applications and the prosecution’s presentation of evidence will shape the next phase of the case.

Prosecutors will be required to prove each defendant’s individual responsibility through admissible evidence under Liberian law.

World.title: Liberia: Jewel Howard-Taylor Indictment Uncertain as Lawyer Awaits Confirmation
World.content:
Judiciary sources expect a grand jury to indict the former vice president, but her defense says it has received no official word

By Willie N. Tokpah

MONROVIA – Uncertainty surrounded the case of former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor on Wednesday. Judiciary sources said a Montserrado County grand jury was expected to indict her, but her lawyer said there was no confirmation that any indictment had been returned.



Sources within the Judiciary told FrontPageAfrica that the grand jury is expected to return an indictment against Howard-Taylor as early as today, October 7, 2026. The specific charges had not been made public as of press time.

Howard-Taylor’s lawyer, Attorney Gbawou Kowou, said the defense had heard similar reports but could not verify them. He said the defense was told that a first panel of special grand jurors failed to reach a conclusion and was disbanded on Monday. A second panel reportedly reached a decision early Wednesday.

“The second set reached a conclusion around 5 a.m. this morning,” Kowou said. “Again, we are hearing this from sources that we believe are credible. We do not have any confirmation to that effect at this point, but we are waiting.”

Neither the court nor the Ministry of Justice had publicly confirmed the grand jury’s decision as of press time.

What an indictment would mean

If returned, an indictment would move the case beyond the criminal complaint and the proceedings so far held before the Monrovia City Court and Criminal Court “C.”

The Ministry of Justice has charged Howard-Taylor with unlicensed importation of a controlled drug or substance. She is also charged with unlicensed sale, distribution, transit and transportation of a controlled substance, and illicit trafficking. Additional counts include criminal solicitation, criminal facilitation, criminal conspiracy and money laundering.

She was arrested on August 19 at Roberts International Airport, where security officers stopped her as she attempted to leave the country. She was then taken to Liberia National Police headquarters and held while investigators pursued the case.

4.2 tonnes of cocaine

The charges stem from a wider national security investigation into an alleged international cocaine network. Authorities have linked the investigation to the seizure of about 4.2 metric tonnes of cocaine, which they estimate to be worth hundreds of millions of U.S. dollars. Three foreign nationals have been charged in absentia in connection with the network.

Prosecutors allege that the network operated in Liberia and other countries. They also allege that Howard-Taylor had dealings with people accused of involvement in the trafficking operation.

Howard-Taylor denies the allegations. Her lawyers maintain that she is innocent and have challenged parts of the government’s case and the way the proceedings have been conducted. They have also stressed that a criminal complaint, an indictment and a conviction are distinct legal steps.

First female vice president

Howard-Taylor served as vice president from January 2018 to January 2024 under former President George Manneh Weah. She became Liberia’s first female vice president after the Coalition for Democratic Change won the 2017 presidential election.

If indicted, she would formally stand trial on the offenses set out in the indictment. An indictment is not a finding of guilt, and the prosecution would still have to prove its case before a court of competent jurisdiction.

World.title: Liberia: He Pressed for Modad’s Exit. Now Witherspoon Says His Campaign Relied on False Information
World.content:
Spoon Network’s executive alleges that government insiders sought the former commerce minister’s removal, reopening questions about the controversy that preceded his resignation.

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh

MONROVIA — When public anger over a government vehicle engulfed Amin Modad, Stanton Witherspoon used his media platform to press for the commerce minister’s departure. Now, the Spoon Network executive is offering a different account of the campaign he helped advance: He says the information supplied to him was wrong.



According to an account of recent Spoon Talk appearances provided for this article, Mr. Witherspoon alleges that people within the Unity Party administration worked to force

Mr. Modad from office. He says he possesses recordings of discussions about the effort.

He is also calling for the former minister’s return to government, saying Mr. Modad brings “credibility and discipline.”

The reversal revives questions about a controversy that ended with Mr. Modad’s resignation in October 2024. It also raises a question about the public campaign against him: Was it driven by legitimate scrutiny, misleading information or, as Mr. Witherspoon now alleges, a deliberate effort by political insiders?

The material available for this article does not settle that question. The broadcasts and the recordings Mr. Witherspoon reportedly cited have not been independently reviewed. The alleged participants have not been identified, and the dates and precise contents of their discussions remain unknown.

For Mr. Modad, the reported remarks return attention to an argument he has maintained since leaving office: that accusations hardened into public judgment before the evidence received a fair hearing.

“I was condemned by the very public I was diligently serving and pushed to honorably resign,” he wrote in a Facebook statement supplied for this article.

The statement, titled “Accusations Are Not Evidence or Facts: A Lesson from My Experience,” describes his resignation as an effort to protect his family and reputation, remove a distraction for the administration and give investigative processes room to proceed.

At the center of the dispute was a vehicle purchased for his official use. Public criticism portrayed it as an extravagant personal benefit. Mr. Modad has disputed both that characterization and widely circulated descriptions of its price and specifications.

In his account, the Liberia Revenue Authority purchased the vehicle for the Ministry of Commerce and Industry and paid the vendor directly. He says the ownership documents named the ministry, and that the vehicle remained with the government after he resigned.

An LRA statement dated September 23, 2024, cited in the material supplied for this article, confirmed the authority’s role in the purchase and rejected accusations surrounding the transaction. Mr. Modad also pointed to documents and testimony presented during a Senate hearing as support for his account that the purchase followed legal requirements.

The difference between the vehicle as publicly described and the purchase documented before the Senate forms a central part of his defense.

Claims circulating during the controversy described a US$150,000 bulletproof vehicle comparable to one used by the United States president. According to the supplied account of documents presented at the hearing, the purchase price was approximately US$88,000 before taxes. Mr. Modad described it as an off-road vehicle intended to support work in rural communities.

“Our agenda was to make sure we take the Ministry to the people and supported the growth of Liberian business across the country,” he wrote.

His statement also challenged allegations involving a privately owned boat and a bank loan associated with Bella Casa Hotel. Those matters, alongside the vehicle purchase, formed part of his broader complaint that claims about his finances had been presented without sufficient regard for the underlying records.

The Liberia Anti-Corruption Commission examined his assets and financial records, according to the supplied material. Mr. Modad maintains that the examination and the Senate proceedings vindicated him. The underlying findings were not provided for independent assessment in this article.

Mr. Witherspoon’s reported acknowledgment shifts attention toward the origins of the information that drove the controversy, and the checks applied before it reached the public.

But an acknowledgment that information was inaccurate does not establish that it was deliberately fabricated. Nor does it, on its own, prove a coordinated effort within the government to remove a minister. Those allegations would require examination of the recordings, supporting communications and accounts from the people involved.

No response from the Unity Party leadership was included in the material supplied for this article.

Mr. Modad’s stated demand is for a standard of public scrutiny that gives evidence and a response their place before judgment is passed.

“We must demand evidence, hear both sides, allow due process to work, and give investigations the time and space necessary to establish the truth,” he wrote.

World.title: Liberia: LNP Seizes US$400,000 in Undeclared Cash at Cape Mount Checkpoint
World.content:
Grand Cape Mount County — The Liberia National Police has intercepted US$400,000 in cash during a routine security operation at the Tienii Checkpoint in Grand Cape Mount County, with authorities saying the money had not been declared at the Liberia-Sierra Leone border.

According to a release, the cash was discovered Tuesday, October 6, at about 1:52 p.m. during a search of a Liberian-registered vehicle, A53191, driven by Abu Toure, 58, of Brewerville, according to the police.

Preliminary police findings indicate that the money was not declared to authorities when it crossed the Liberia-Sierra Leone border.



Toure reportedly told investigators that the money represented proceeds from his cocoa business.

Following the discovery, police took Toure into custody and referred the matter to the Financial Crime Division of the Liberia National Police and the Liberia Revenue Authority (LRA) for further investigation.

The LNP stressed that the investigation remains ongoing and that no final determination has been made regarding whether any law was violated.

The police said the interception underscores the importance of security checks at border points as authorities seek to prevent financial crimes, money laundering and other activities that could threaten Liberia’s economic and national security.

The LNP commended officers assigned to the Tienii Checkpoint for what it described as vigilance and professionalism, reaffirming its commitment to working with relevant government institutions to combat financial crimes.

Authorities have not indicated whether the US$400,000 has been forfeited or what further action may be taken against Toure pending the outcome of the investigation.
