World.title: 'Canada is not our enemy': Michigan Republican Senate candidate breaks with Trump on trade war
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

The Republican candidate in a pitched battle for Michigan's open Senate seat is calling on U.S. President Donald Trump to end the trade war with Canada.

Mike Rogers released a new 30-second ad criticizing the tariffs while sitting in a sports bar with a Labatt beer, a Canadian brand popular in border states like his.

"Here in Michigan we know that Canada is not on our enemy. We need to end this tariff war now," Rogers says in the ad, as an image of the Ambassador Bridge, which connects Windsor and Detroit, appears on screen.

"As Michigan's senator, I'll bring both parties together to lower your prices. That's job No. 1," Rogers says in the spot.

Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office later Wednesday, U.S. President Donald Trump was dismissive of the ad, recasting Rogers's trade war message.

"Well, I viewed it as though he wanted Canada to make a deal," Trump said.

"We don't want them to make cars for us.... It's a long story, but they've been ripping us off. Canada has been ripping us off for many, many years and they're not going to rip us off anymore," he said.

About-face for Rogers

This is an about-face for Rogers, who earlier had endorsed the tariffs Trump levied on Canadian goods.

In an interview with Fox News this summer, Rogers said Trump's trade policy designed to "reindustrialize" the U.S. was "huge for us ... all of these things are really positive."

He said Canada wants to sell hundreds of thousands of cars into Michigan and that should be "absolutely unacceptable" because those exports "undercut the people who build cars and car parts."

"The Canadians have not been good partners on this," he said.

WATCH | Trump adviser warns Canada against election interference: 'You will pay': Trump adviser warns Canada not to 'interfere' with U.S. midterms | Duration closed caption 2:54 White House trade adviser Peter Navarro warned Canada not to 'interfere' with U.S. midterm elections in border states such as Maine and Michigan by lobbying against the Trump administration's tariffs. Navarro said Canada would 'pay even more dearly' for doing so.

Rogers has long been closely associated with Trump. When the U.S. president endorsed Rogers earlier this year, the candidate said he was "thrilled" to receive it.

"Together, President Trump and I will unleash a great revival in the state of Michigan," he said at the time of the endorsement.

Tariffs unpopular in U.S.: polls

Rogers's break with the president on Canadian trade policy comes as polls suggest Trump's tariffs are deeply unpopular in the U.S.

Only 26 per cent of Americans surveyed for a Politico poll late last month said levying tariffs on Canadian goods was the right thing to do.

LISTEN | Canada's choices: Front Burner 23:47 Should Canada have taken the U.S. deal?

Rogers is also trailing his Democratic opponent, Abdul El-Sayed, in most public opinion surveys. After the ad was released, El-Sayed said Rogers "must have had one too many of those Labatts."

"You cheer-led this tariff war from the beginning and you’re flip-flopping now because your poll numbers are in free fall. Donald is the reason we’re in a trade war. And he’s the reason you’re running," he wrote in a social media post.

Canada, U.S. auto industries deeply intertwined

The Canadian and U.S. auto sectors have one of the most deeply intertwined cross-border manufacturing relationships in the world.

Canada does not "undercut" the U.S. industry, as Rogers describes; rather, it supplies critical parts used in assembly plants throughout the U.S.

Some of those components cross the border a half-dozen times or more because these sectors are so integrated after decades of free trade, with Canadian plants specializing in particular parts and powertrains.

WATCH | How tariffs are affecting our auto industry: How are tariffs affecting Canada's auto industry, really? | Duration 2:28 Car parts can cross international borders six, seven or even eight times before ending up in a vehicle. But amid a trade war, as both Canada and the United States raise tariffs up to 50 per cent, it's getting more expensive — and complicated — to build cars. The CBC's Acton Clarkin breaks it down.

It's a relationship that experts say has helped the North American auto market compete against low-cost overseas manufacturers.

Plus, Canada is a huge customer for what American auto plants churn out every year. About three-quarters of all vehicles sold in Canada are imported, with the majority coming from U.S. plants in Michigan, Indiana and Texas.

Dearborn, Mich.-based Ford has been the No. 1 vehicle brand in Canada for years, with the American-made F-Series being hugely popular among Canadian consumers.

And, despite Republican claims that Trump's tariff policies are boosting industrial employment, data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics compiled by the Economic Policy Institute shows that some 62,000 manufacturing jobs have been lost since Trump took office for his second term in January 2025.

World.title: Don't support Trump tariffs then blame Stelco job cuts on 'act of God,' Joly warns Cleveland-Cliffs
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Canada's industry minister said Wednesday Stelco Holdings Inc. cannot use the trade war to justify cutting jobs it committed to when it bought the Hamilton-based steel plant, particularly when the head of its U.S. parent company has publicly backed steel tariffs.

Melanie Joly told reporters that the chief executive of U.S.-based Cleveland-Cliffs has supported steel tariffs and therefore cannot characterize the company's plan to lay off up to 500 workers due to tariffs and market pressures as beyond its control.

"He's in favour of these U.S. tariffs against steel," she said, referring to Cleveland-Cliffs CEO Lourenco Goncalves' public support of American steel tariffs.

"They cannot say that this is now an act of God or force majeure."

If the company does not respond to the federal government's demand for a plan outlining how it will meet all of its commitments, including maintaining more than 1,500 jobs, Ottawa will pursue enforcement action, Joly said.

"They need to comply," she said. "If not, we will use the full force of the law."

Canada gave U.S.-based Cleveland-Cliffs the green light to purchase Stelco back in 2024 under the Investment Canada Act.

Canada's approval of that takeover was contingent on the new owner maintaining the number of union jobs and the majority of non-union positions, Joly said.

She sent a letter to Stelco president Paul Simon on Monday demanding a plan outlining how Cleveland-Cliffs intends to comply with all of the undertakings it made to Ottawa when it acquired Stelco, including its jobs commitment.

Ottawa has not yet received a response from Stelco on the letter, Joly said.

Meanwhile, she distinguished Stelco's planned job cuts from recent layoffs and plant disruptions in the auto sector, saying Cleveland-Cliffs made legally binding employment commitments when it acquired the steelmaker.

"These obligations are binding."

World.title: Ottawa to indefinitely extend MAID exclusion for people solely suffering from mental illness
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

The federal government will introduce legislation this fall that will indefinitely extend the ban on access to a medically assisted death for people who are solely suffering from mental illness, Justice Minister Sean Fraser said on Wednesday.

"Canada has made a decision not to move forward with the expansion that is scheduled in the Criminal Code of medical assistance in dying in circumstances where mental illness is the sole basis," he said in the foyer of the House of Commons.

Fraser said the government's decision reflects the position expressed by a special parliamentary committee report released in June along with his own department's probing of the issue.

"While there is not a perfect consensus on this issue, we believe this is the correct approach at this particular time," he said.

WATCH | Justice minister on forthcoming MAID changes: Ottawa 'landed in the right place' with changes to MAID: justice minister | Duration closed caption 2:33 Minister of Justice Sean Fraser says his perspective on the new legislation on medical assistance in dying (MAID) that will be tabled this fall comes from the experiences and conversations he's had with people he knows. 'These are not easy conversations, but my experience is not unique,' he says, adding that he understands the reticence some people may have about the legislation.

Fraser said the promised legislation will also "open the door" for people to give advance consent for their own medically assisted death in circumstances where the illness they are suffering from will eventually eliminate their capacity to make that decision.

The minister explained that while the details of advance consent will be worked out in House of Commons committees, it will require a person's illness to be incurable and result in intolerable suffering.

2 key reasons for MAID exclusion

Fraser said there are two significant points motivating his government to indefinitely extend the current prohibition on receiving MAID for people who only have a mental illness.

He said there are "very real concerns about people who live in communities with inadequate access to mental health services."

The second reason was the lack of consensus over when a mental illness is incurable, along with other issues raised in the June report .

WATCH | Review urges indefinite exclusion for mental illness: MAID should 'indefinitely exclude' people with mental illness, review urges | Duration closed caption 2:48 A newly tabled parliamentary report urges the Canadian government to amend the criminal code to indefinitely exclude people whose sole underlying condition is mental illness from Medical Assistance in Dying (MAID). The decision now lies with Justice Minister Sean Fraser.

The government passed MAID legislation in 2016. But the Superior Court of Quebec struck the law down in 2019 because it was limited to those whose deaths were "reasonably foreseeable."

Bill C-7, which passed Parliament in March 2021, removed that requirement, in line with the court's ruling. The legislation also temporarily pushed back the expansion of MAID to cases involving only mental illness to March 2023.

That was further delayed to 2024 and again to March 2027.

Fraser says Conservative bill isn't enough

Fraser said that he was announcing the legislation before it was ready, in part, to explain why his government will not be voting for a Conservative private member's bill, C-218, which is up for a vote in the House later in the day.

Fraser thanked Conservative MP Tamara Jansen for introducing the bill but said it fell short in two areas. The first area was the bill's use of the term "mental disorders," which the minister said could be interpreted to include neurologically degenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer's or Parkinson's.

Under existing MAID legislation, people with neurologically degenerative diseases can recieve a medically assisted death.

He also pointed to the fact that C-218 does not address advance consent.

"This second issue is extremely important to communities of people who've been diagnosed with very, very serious illnesses [that] may cause them to lose capacity subsequently," he said.

Accusations of political games

After Fraser's announcement, Jansen accused the minister of playing games "hours before" the House of Commons was set to vote on her bill.

"We have no idea what his bill's going to say. He's telling us all sorts of things, he hasn't even seen the bill himself," she said. "I find it incredibly negligent. He had the entire summer to put this together."

Jansen asked Liberal MPs to consider voting for her bill regardless, "because people's lives are at risk, very vulnerable Canadians," and said Fraser was attempting to sink C-218 based on a promised "phantom bill."

She said the Conservatives have been clear that they are open to changing the bill's wording in order to get it passed.

World.title: How much sugar is in these 'sugar-free' Starbucks protein drinks? As much as a candy bar, claims lawsuit
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

It's fair to say you probably have some idea what you're in for, sugar-wise, when you order a pumpkin spice latte or caramel macchiato from Starbucks.

But what should you expect if you're ordering a drink that's labelled "sugar-free?"

That's the question behind a proposed U.S. class-action lawsuit that claims the coffee chain falsely advertised eight protein beverages as "sugar-free," when they actually contain between 13 and 21 grams of sugar per venti-size serving due to the naturally occurring sugar in milk.

The lawsuit, filed Friday in a Seattle federal court and viewed by CBC News, accuses Starbucks of trying to capitalize on "the protein craze" and nutritional preferences of customers.

"By naming its beverages 'Sugar-Free,' Starbucks makes a specific, quantitative and verifiable claim about the nature of these beverages. Consumers rely upon such claims when deciding to purchase such products," the lawsuit says

"The 21 grams of sugar contained in a venti Sugar-Free Caramel Protein Matcha is roughly equal to five teaspoons of sugar. This is almost as much total sugar as is contained in a standard Kit Kat bar."

A screen grab of an Instagram post by Starbucks from Oct. 23, 2025, that advertises some protein beverages as sugar-free. (@Starbucks/Instagram)

A spokesperson for Starbucks told CBC News Wednesday they believe the lawsuit's claims have "no merit."

"Starbucks has consistently and clearly provided information about its protein beverages, sugar-free options, customization choices and nutritional content ... and we intend to vigorously defend ourselves," the spokesperson said.

So, are the drinks sugar-free, or not? Is the labelling misleading? And is it just U.S. drinks, or Canada, too?

Let's take a closer look at the lawsuit and what we know.

What are the drinks in question?

The lawsuit lists eight protein beverages that Starbucks labels as sugar-free:

Sugar-free vanilla protein latte.

Sugar-free caramel protein latte.

Sugar-free vanilla protein matcha.

Sugar-free caramel protein matcha.

Iced sugar-free vanilla protein latte.

Iced sugar-free caramel protein latte.

Iced sugar-free vanilla protein matcha.

Iced sugar-free caramel protein matcha.

Each item is available on both U.S. and Starbucks Canada websites under "protein beverages." And while the eight drinks are listed under a "no added sugar options" heading, each beverage currently has "sugar-free" in its title.

Starbucks launched the beverages in September 2025, citing statistics claiming that " 71 per cent of Canadian consumers want to eat more protein." In a news release at the time, Starbucks noted its new protein drinks will be " available unsweetened or sugar-free and are designed to support customers looking to add protein to their order."

WATCH | Coffee chains cash in on protein craze: Coffee chains look to cash in on protein’s popularity | Duration closed caption 2:01 Starbucks will soon follow Tim Hortons as the latest coffee chain to offer additional protein in its caffeinated drinks, a move experts say is likely to benefit profit margins more than customers’ health.

Are they sugar-free, or not?

No, each beverage contains sugar — anywhere between 13 and 21 grams per venti-size serving. At the higher end, that's about equivalent to the grams of sugar in a KitKat or Coffee Crisp chocolate bar, according to Health Canada.

When you click through the individual drinks on the company website, Starbucks lists nutritional information for each "sugar-free" protein beverage, including the grams of sugar by size. A venti iced sugar-free vanilla protein latte, for instance, is listed as containing 13 grams of sugar, and a venti sugar-free caramel protein matcha has 21 grams of sugar.

As the lawsuit points out, "the sugar-free products all contain milk, which contains lactose, a naturally occurring sugar."

If it's natural sugar, what's the issue?

The issue isn't where the sugar comes from, but the sugar-free labelling, the lawsuit argues.

"Despite knowing that Sugar-Free products contain milk, and knowing that this milk contains lactose, and knowing that this lactose is a sugar, and despite actually classifying this lactose as a sugar, Starbucks nonetheless calls these beverages 'Sugar-Free,'" the lawsuit says.

"Starbucks calls these beverages 'Fugar-Free' because it knows that consumers rely on such representations when deciding what products to purchase."

What are the consumer protection laws?

U.S. federal law prohibits Starbucks from using "sugar-free" to describe beverages containing more than 0.5 grams of sugar per 12-ounce serving, the complaint said. Even if the sugar comes from milk.

Similarly, in Canada, for something to be labelled as sugar-free, the food must contain less than 0.5 grams of sugars per reference amount and serving of stated size, according to the Food and Drug Regulations.

WATCH | Are the new labels on Canadian foods visible enough?: Are the new labels on high fat, sugar and sodium foods visible enough? | Duration closed caption 1:59 New nutrition symbols are now mandatory for many packaged goods in Canada. They indicate if the product is high in saturated fat, sugars or sodium. But some experts worry they’re not obvious enough to make a difference.

In both countries, there's a difference between labelling something as "sugar-free," like Starbucks has done with the protein drink names, or as having "no added sugars," which is how Starbucks also describes the drinks in the nutritional information because it uses sugar-free syrups.

Lactose is listed as a sugar in both Canada and the U.S.

Food producers are regularly sued for alleged false advertising, including in dozens of recent cases challenging "sugar-free" or "zero sugar" claims for products containing a sugar substitute known as allulose.

What happens next?

The complaint seeks unspecified damages for false advertising and violations of various state consumer protection laws. It also seeks to have the lawsuit certified as a class action and demands a trial by jury "on all issues so triable."

The lawsuit was filed on behalf of three individual consumers who bought Starbucks's sugar-free protein drinks in California, New York and Washington.

Consumers avoid sugar for various reasons, including health-related issues such as diabetes, Steve Berman, a co-founder and managing partner of the Seattle-headquartered firm that filed the lawsuit, said in a news release.

"And for many, a staunch mislabeling like this is significant," Berman said.

“Beverages with this much sugar are like drinking a candy bar.”

World.title: NASA's Curiosity rover takes striking image of dawn on Mars
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

NASA has released a striking image of dawn on the Martian surface taken by its Curiosity rover, showing sunlight bathing ‌jagged crags formed billions of years ago as the car-sized vehicle continues to explore Earth's planetary neighbour.

Curiosity landed in 2012 in Gale Crater near the Martian equator, and since 2014 has been climbing Mount Sharp, a five-kilometre-tall mountain rising from the crater floor.

The image was taken by the six-wheeled rover's Mastcam camera about ​an hour after the sun rose above a landscape featuring wind-carved ​cliffs in the distance.

"The bright craggy peaks in the distance are a rock layer that is quite different in appearance from all the layers the rover has driven through so far," said planetary scientist Ashwin Vasavada of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California, the Curiosity project scientist.

NASA believes that some kind of wind-blown sediment landed in the crater from nearby volcanic activity. Once it hardened into rock, "eons of wind carved ‌up the rock layer into ridges called yardangs," Vasvada said.

The yardang layer most likely formed about three billion years ago, around the same time as the rest of the mountain, according to Vasavada. This layer spans about 16 ⁠kilometres across the northwestern reaches of Mount Sharp.

But the layers appears to have been added on later, he said.

"It's above what geologists call an ‌unconformity: a gap in time where previous layers eroded down before new layers were deposited on top."

Rover making gradual ascent up mountain

The rover on its gradual ascent up the mountain has gained upwards of nearly a kilometre in elevation, the most ever climbed on Mars, according to NASA.

Mount Sharp is built of layers, each recording a ​period of the planet's geological past. In studying these layers, scientists have learned more about bodies of water — lakes and streams — that long ago covered this region, at ⁠a time when Mars was wetter and warmer than the cold and desolate place it is today.

Vasavada said NASA hopes ⁠Curiosity will reach the yardang layer in 2027 or 2028, at which time it will use its instruments to ⁠scrutinize ⁠the geology there.

Curiosity has been studying the ​geology and climate of Mars and examining whether it once bore conditions conducive to harboring microbial life. It is one of two ​NASA rovers operating on Mars. The ⁠Perseverance rover is currently traversing the margins of Jezero Crater in the northern hemisphere.

Curiosity's new image of Martian dawn is certainly otherworldly.

"This scene has a wildness that reminds me of a road trip through Monument Valley, Arizona. You can almost feel the silence and the endless open space under the sky," Vasavada said.

"But as familiar as that sounds, the sky is orange and the sunrise has shades ⁠of blue. It's like Earth, but ‌it's definitely Mars."

World.title: WHO wants more answers from Russia about lab worker's death, as pneumonic plague concerns linger
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

A top official with the UN's health agency doesn't know how a lab worker in Siberia died amid concerns about plague, and she's urging Russia to provide more information.

There have been questions and concerns about the death of the 28-year-old woman, identified in Russian media as Darya Shipilova, amid speculation she died of pneumonic plague and that her death may be connected pathogens she worked with at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East.

Maria Van Kerkhove, director of epidemic and pandemic management at the World Health Agency (WHO), said the agency doesn't know the cause of the woman's Oct. 2 death, and "this is why we need more information."

"We don't understand how she was infected," Van Kerkhove said during a news briefing in Geneva.

The WHO is also seeking more information about unconfirmed media reports of a second case of pneumonia of "undetermined cause" connected to the Irkutsk lab, in southeastern Siberia.

WHO director general Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the agency could not verify the credibility of the reports but is seeking clarification from the relevant officials in Russia.

In a tersely worded statement, Russia's official public health and consumer watchdog, Rospotrebnadzor, does not link the first case to pneumonic plague, saying only that "extensive" testing found no evidence the lab worker's illness was caused by any of the pathogens she worked with.

Russia has said she died of pneumonia — a "typical" acute respiratory viral infection — and its health authorities have found no cases of plague recently, the WHO has said, acknowledging that pneumonia is commonplace and that cases of COVID-19 and rhinovirus were present among the some 200 people monitored since that death.

Pneumonic plague is a less common but severe form of plague that can spread from person to person.

Plague is an infectious disease caused by a bacterium known as Yersinia pestis, or Y. pestis, that is carried by small mammals and generally spread by the fleas that feed off them. It can be treated with antibiotics but can be deadly if left untreated.

Plague is endemic to Siberia, which was recently confirmed as the location of the first known prehistoric human outbreak of the disease.

WATCH | Questions, concern surround death: What we know about the suspected plague death in Russia | Duration closed caption 2:01 Two-hundred people have been placed under medical observation in Siberia, Russia, after a laboratory worker died after a reported accident at a plague research facility. The World Health Organization says the public health risk remains low.

Russia insists no plague cases

Moscow previously informed the WHO that no case of plague has been registered in the Irkutsk region.

Russian health authorities reported a full range of preventive measures had been carried out —including tracing the dead woman's contacts, medical monitoring and lab tests, the WHO said.

The Russian note relayed to The Associated Press by the WHO said the test showed "no presence of dangerous infectious disease pathogens in any of the contacts."

The organization said it has requested further information to clarify the cause of the severe pneumonia, the pathogen that prompted the public health measures, and media reports of the second case.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov referred all questions to Rospotrebnadzor, which does not mention suspected plague in its reports.

In its latest statement Tuesday, the agency said "the sanitary and epidemiological situation in the Irkutsk region … is calm."

Authorities were completing a "complex of prophylactic measures and medical observation over contacts," it said, adding that so far they have found two cases of COVID-19 and two of rhinovirus.

Mother not notified

The news outlet Lyudi Baikala identified Shipilova as the deceased lab worker and said she first was hospitalized with cold symptoms Sept. 29, in the nearby town of Shelekhov, and died three days later.

It quoted colleagues as saying she was a highly qualified and diligent researcher, and emphasized that security rules at the facility are extremely strict.

The report quoted Shipilova's neighbours as saying a team of disinfection experts did several cleanups of her apartment, leaving a strong antiseptic smell.

Researchers work in the institute's lab in this undated photo released in 2019. (Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and Far East/Handout/The Associated Press)

Shipilova's mother, who worked as a doctor in the past, described her daughter as hard-working and dedicated, according to independent Russian news outlet Glubina, adding that she had not received official documents describing the cause of death.

Irkutsk Gov. Igor Kobzev said she died of a "particularly dangerous infection" and everyone who came into contact with her has remained under medical supervision.

The hospital where she died was placed under quarantine, no longer admitting or discharging patients, although its outpatient clinic has continued operating, according to Mayor Maxim Modin.

WHO urges transparency

Russian authorities have, however kept a tight lid on information and the speculation she died of pneumonic plague.

While the case has grabbed international attention, Russian state TV and other national state-controlled media have steered clear of the subject. Some state-sponsored news outlets withdrew earlier reports about the case.

Vasily Vlassov, professor at the department of health-care administration and economics at Russia's Higher School of Economics, says it's not clear whether more transparency was possible if those dealing with the situation didn't have enough certainty, and "maybe, they still don't."

Deceiving the public "always turns out to be harmful," he said, and distrust of Russia's official narrative is "natural" and "almost inevitable."

Judy Twigg, professor of political science at Virginia Commonwealth University, notes that Russia criminalized "false information" about threats to public safety in 2020 amid the COVID-19 pandemic, "so silence is the one safe move for everyone below the top."

"Personalist regimes without electoral accountability tend to treat bad news as a loyalty problem rather than focusing on the actual problem to be addressed," she said.

World.title: Maya Turner named 1st female captain in University of Manitoba Bisons football history
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Maya Turner just keeps putting the boots to the history books for Canadian university football.

The placekicker and punter with the Manitoba Bisons — who became the first woman to score in U Sports football during a pre-season game in 2022 — is now the first female captain in the century-long history of the Bisons football program.

"It's really a huge honour and means a lot that they have that kind of respect for me, just as a player and a teammate, and that they see me as someone who's a leader and has a place on this team regardless of gender," Turner said.

The 24-year-old was named one of the team's seven captains — representing the many different positions — at the end of training camp.

Head coach Stan Pierre announced the names to the team, "and yeah, my name was in there," Turner said, still sounding a bit surprised.

"Yeah, I guess I wasn't totally expecting it."

Maya Turner was the first woman to play and score in a pre-season U Sports football game, then became the first to do it in a regular-season game, and later became the first female Canada West football all-star. (Mike Still/Manitoba Bisons Athletics)

Handing the specialist captaincy to Turner as she enters her senior year was " a pretty easy decision," Pierre said.

"Maya is an exemplary student athlete. She does everything you ask of her, and she does it at a very high level," he said.

"She's a great student, she's a great person, she works extremely hard. She doesn't miss anything and she doesn't make excuses for anything. She just does everything correct.

"I can't think of a better mentor for our young players and a better example as a leader on our football team."

It's possible Turner's the first to break that gender leadership barrier in any Canadian university football program.

"I don't even know how many women have played U Sports [football] — I don't think it's five," Pierre said.

"So I would venture a guess that there's a really good possibility that she is ."

Bisons football head coach Stan Pierre says Turner is an exceptional player, period, with no asterisk required because she's female. (University of Manitoba)

Turner first inscribed her name into U Sports history (the national governing body for Canadian university athletics) with her 2022 pre-season boot, but she fully carved it in the following year.

On Sept. 23, 2023, she became the first woman to play and score in a regular-season game, hitting a 21-yard field goal. Then she repeated that distance for the game-winning points in double overtime .

She finished the year with a 79 per cent accuracy mark — third-best percentage in Bison football's century-old history.

One kick was a 48-yarder, the eighth-longest in the nation.

In 2024, her field goal percentage of 75 led the Canada West conference and she hit another one from 48 yards out. Her performance led to her being named a Canada West all-star — another first for women in U Sports football.

She kicked 76 per cent in 2025, including a 15-point contribution on Oct. 18 (four field goals and three extra points) to help the Bisons erase a 10-point deficit and win 33-31.

Turner, who is from Maple Grove, Minn., about 15 kilometres northwest of Minneapolis, played soccer at Loyola University in Chicago before transitioning to kicker with its club football team.

She attended multiple kicking camps in the U.S. and reached out to hundreds of schools to see if any would consider adding her to their men's football team.

"I was just super determined to play this sport at a high level. I knew that I had the abilities, and so I was confident that there would be someone who would be able to recognize that," she said.

She was invited for a tryout with the Bisons and impressed enough to be offered a roster spot.

"Ever since I've been here, I think everyone's done a really good job of just seeing me as football player first and trying to not have me being a woman impact anything," Turner said.

Pierre agreed, saying the attention Turner gets from outside the Bisons program is understandable, but within the team, she is beloved "not because she's a female but because she's a really good person and a really good player. For us, she's just one of the players.

"It really doesn't feel like anything all that peculiar."

Still, her marks on history are directly linked to her gender, and Pierre hopes Turner has mowed a path for others to follow, though he acknowledged the gender barriers haven't exactly been kicked down.

"I hope she loosened those barriers a little bit and that there is more opportunity. But I'm not naive," he said.

"If there's another female out there that is capable of doing it, I hope that it inspires her. But Maya is a special athlete and what she's done isn't easy.

"She's exceptional to be good enough to compete at this level."

World.title: Michael Murphy: The students glorifying terrorists as they riot across France
World.content:
Article content

Much of the mainstream coverage, meanwhile, has taken the protests more or less at face value: young people rightly angered by a dysfunctional — and increasingly heavy-handed — state. This is only part of the picture. It cannot explain the chants for a jihadi who murdered Jewish children; nor the lyrics in the same song revelling in the murder of 90 innocent people in the Bataclan massacre. It is true that many of the schools affected by shortages are in the banlieues, where ethnic minorities have long been concentrated on the edges of French cities, sprawling concrete suburbs, afflicted with crime and ennui, that have been a thorn in the side of the Fifth Republic for decades. But that fact does not illuminate the glee with which some students have embraced violence against their teachers, many of whom share their grievances. Figures from what one might call the Global Right have observed that many of these scenes, circulating on social media, have shown a disproportionate number of perpetrators hailing from migrant-descended backgrounds. Donald Trump posted on Truth Social: “This isn’t about schools, this is about Islam wanting to take over a once great Country!” Like sympathetic mainstream accounts, the U.S. president is only partly correct.

World.title: De la Espriella announces first $309M in aid for earthquake reconstruction
World.content:
President Abelardo de la Espriella announced that his Miracle Fund received COP1 trillion ($309 million) for the reconstruction of western Colombia, which was hit by a 7.4M earthquake on August 10.

The announcement followed announcements by the press, which reported that the Finance Ministry allocated ($192 million) COP625 billion to the fund almost two months after the disaster.

Thank you for your patience, but please understand that the government’s bureaucratic inertia and the situation we’ve inherited are extremely complex. However, we’re working to resolve the issue, and the Milagro Fund is now up and running, thanks to God and the efforts of all the officials in this administration. President Abelardo de la Espriella

“In November, the government will move forward with contracting another COP2.7 trillion ($835 million),” Vice-President Jose Manuel Restrepo told Caracol Radio.

The money is the first of an estimated COP30 trillion ($9.3 billion) that would be needed to rebuild the damage to airports, roads, hospitals and other public works.

The fund will be managed by De la Espriella’s general secretary, Carlos Rios, and a handful of businessmen with ties to the administration.

The announcement followed increased unrest about the government’s lack of response to the earthquake, which affected more than 400,000 people in the Valle del Cauca and Choco province, and the coffee region.

The government’s initial response was delayed because De la Espriella suspended the process to transfer power a month before he took office on August 7.

World.title: Colombia seeks to expand definition of terrorism in draft “counterterrorism statute”
World.content:
The government of President Abelardo de la Espriella will present Colombia’s Congress with a comprehensive “counterterrorism statute,” which would give authorities enhanced powers to fight designated terrorist organizations.

A 116-page draft bill, which was leaked to Caracol Radio, would facilitate a military approach to combat illegal armed groups and organized crime groups, for example through air strikes.

The Antiterrorism Statute would additionally create a National Registry of Terrorist Organizations and Actors, which would make it easier to freeze the assets of suspected terrorists and their financiers.

Last but not least, the bill creates a presidential Terrorism Commissioner and a special prison regime for leaders of designated terrorist organizations.

Broader definition of terrorism

The bill seeks to change Colombia’s criminal law and define terrorism as any individual or collective conduct that produces “fear, panic or terror, creating risks, threats or the use of violence.”

A technical body of the National Security Council (NSC) will advise the council on the inclusion of organizations or individuals that ought to be included to its public National Registry of Terrorist Organizations and Actors.

Anyone who believes he was falsely put on the terror list can challenge this decision before the NSC and the Council of State, Colombia’s top administrative court.

The bill additionally seeks that “the Council of State shall hear, in the first instance, constitutional protection lawsuits filed against the President of the Republic or against defense authorities for acts or omissions related to operations by law enforcement agencies to preserve national security.”

This would make the suspension of military operations more difficult for citizens, who now can seek legal support to protect their constitutional rights at lower courts.

The bill also creates new crimes and modifies the penalties for conduct related to “terrorism,” such as the use of drones, illegal mining, oil theft, the extraction and sale of gold, kidnapping, smuggling, human trafficking, drug trafficking, extortion, cybercrimes, election crimes, riots, and attacks on critical infrastructure.

In the case of riots, “the penalty shall be increased by up to double when the riot is directed against law enforcement units conducting operations; or is carried out in conjunction with listed terrorist organizations.”

The bill also allows Colombian authorities to investigate and prosecute terrorism, terrorism financing or providing material support for terrorist organizations abroad.

High Counterterrorism Commissioner

The bill additionally seeks to expand presidential powers to create the Office of the High Counterterrorism Commissioner.

The expanded power would additionally give De la Espriella six months to regulate the powers of this new advisory office and to appoint its first commissioner.

World.title: Mayor from Colombia’s north claims De la Espriella’s armed men intimidated him
World.content:
The mayor of Sincelejo claimed Sunday that armed men intimidated him during a meeting with Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella.

In a video message, Sincelejo Mayor Yahir Acuña said that armed men positioned themselves behind him while the president accused the mayor of corruption and threatened to pull municipal funds.

The accusations were partly published on the social media pages of the president, who accused Acuña of being “a person who, like you, faces 13 corruption charges, has a video in which he explains how to embezzle funds from the PAE, and, on top of that, is set to stand trial in the Supreme Court of Justice on charges of illicit enrichment.”

So let’s see what we do with Sincelejo, but I do not work under your scheme of corruption. And if you think you can continue engaging in those practices, know that someone has arrived who is going to prevent it and that I am going to concentrate on it. This money, mister mayor, I will take care of it, and to take care of it I have to keep it away from your control. President Abelardo de la Espriella

In his response, Acuña claimed that De la Espriella’s video “has been edited and digitally manipulated.”

I ask you, please, to show the full video, where you can see how disciplinary and criminal codes are being violated in Colombia, where you can see how a mayor is being intimidated with rifles in the hands of civilians. How can a mayor be constantly flanked—for the entire duration of an event—by a person armed with a rifle, with the sole purpose of intimidating him? Sincelejo Mayor Yahir Acuña

Investigative journalist Laura Ardila said on social media platform X that sources from the province confirmed Acuña’s allegations.

Sources from the department who were present say—fearing they might be named—that they left the scene terrified. They claim that Acuña was indeed surrounded by heavily armed men in civilian clothing, that the president’s office was recording the entire time, and that, based on details like these, they believe it was a scene staged in advance to go viral. Journalist Laura Ardila

The mayor subsequently pointed out that the investigations into his alleged corruption existed before the presidential campaign, during which the De la Espriella campaign may have violated electoral laws, according to Acuña.

Among other things, the mayor said that he had been approached by De la Espriella’s parents to support the far-right president’s campaign and that local print shops may have received unreported campaign funds.

Since this needs to be clarified, mister President, it would be a good idea for the oversight agencies to investigate whether any printing shops in Sincelejo incurred campaign expenses that have not yet been reported to the National Electoral Council, whether there was campaign financing, and where that campaign financing came from, Mister President. Sincelejo Mayor Yahir Acuña

The mayor also pointed out that two members of the De la Espriella administration are being investigated on corruption charges and that the president had ties to the now-defunct paramilitary organization AUC.

The president has repeatedly used corruption allegations to target political enemies.

World.title: Colombia’s top corporate lobbyist resigns over reported tensions with president
World.content:
The director of one of Colombia’s most powerful business associations, Bruce Mac Master of the ANDI, resigned amid tensions with President Abelardo de la Espriella.

In a letter to the ANDI, Mac Master said that “it is time for me to step down from my role as head of the National Association of Entrepreneurs of Colombia.”

According to the former ANDI boss, “unexpected and troubling circumstances” made working for the association “particularly complex” and ‘multiple pressures have affected its ability to act freely and carry out its functions autonomously.”

In recent weeks, unexpected and troubling circumstances have arisen that have made the Association’s operating environment particularly complex, with potential adverse effects on its members and staff. Multiple pressures have affected its ability to act freely and carry out its functions autonomously. In the face of these challenges, I have sought to act with firmness and prudence, always prioritizing institutional channels and placing the interests of the ANDI above any personal considerations, in an effort to resolve this situation. Bruce Mac Master

Mac Master’s resignation followed news suggesting that De la Espriella instructed his cabinet of boycotting the ANDI chief.

According to political news magazine La Silla Vacia, the rift between the ANDI and the government was because De la Espriella’s law firm was never allowed to join the ANDI and the association’s donations in response to the august 10 earthquake bypassed the First Lady’s newly founded and very controversial foundation.

“The General Board of Directors, its Executive Committee, and I did everything in our power to facilitate a solution and create conditions that would allow the Association to fully fulfill its role, seeking to keep channels of dialogue open and to continue contributing,” but “all of those attempts were unsuccessful.”

I deeply regret this, because I have always believed in collective intelligence and in the need for the government, the private sector, and institutions to work together—even in the face of differences—with respect, independence, and a sense of national responsibility. We tried, but we were unsuccessful. Bruce Mac Master

Mac Master said that he hoped that his resignation would restore “collaboration between the national government and the business community—as represented by the General Board of Directors, the members, and the various divisions of the Association.”

The former ANDI chief had been trying to represent the business interests of its approximately 1,600 members since 2013.

World.title: Colombia seeks to tighten checks on public protests
World.content:
Colombia’s government published a draft decree that seeks to tighten regulations on public protests.

The draft was published weeks before labor unions and social organizations plan regional anti-government protests ahead of a national strike that is set for November.

The draft seeks to update the Decree #3 of 2021, which was issued months before a national strike that was violently repressed by the police and the military.

In an attempt to prevent another bloodbath, the decree seeks to regulate authorities’ response to protests and the coordinated use of force in response to acts of vandalism and violence.

The decree regulates dialogue between the protesters and law enforcement authorities to promote the peaceful nature of protests.

The decree additionally limits the use of police intelligence against those organizing and participating in the protests.

Last but not least, the decree seeks the effective prosecution of those arrested during protests through increased surveillance and a permanent police presence.

The decree comes amid social tensions that surged after the far-right President Abelardo de la Espriella took office in August and announced counterrevolutionary measures that seek to undo reforms by his leftist predecessor, former President Gustavo Petro.

Swelling student protests have been publicly accused of being fueled by insurgencies and De la Espriella has warned that police may enter universities if they find evidence they are used to prepare acts of vandalism or terrorism.

World.title: Colombia breaks diplomatic ties with Iran
World.content:
Colombia’s Foreign Ministry said Thursday that it had broken diplomatic ties with Iran and designated the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organization.

The foreign ministry made the announcements in two separate statements that were published in its website.

In the first statement, the government claimed that the decision claimed to defend “national and hemispheric security, and the fight against transnational crime.”

According to the foreign ministry, the Iranian government has “alleged ties to international terrorist groups and other narco-terrorist groups that threaten [Colombia’s] security.”

Colombia also took into account the documented human rights violations committed by the Iranian government on its territory, the verified attacks against countries not involved in the Middle East conflict, the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, and the authorities’ obstruction of the International Atomic Energy Agency’s (IAEA) efforts to verify the scope of Iran’s nuclear program. Foreign Ministry

In regards to the IRGC, the foreign ministry claimed that the Iranian armed force “poses a serious threat to international peace and security” through “covert operations beyond Iran’s borders.”

“Colombia will strengthen its control and security measures to prevent individuals associated with the IRGC from entering its territory,” said the foreign ministry in a second statement.

In his 2017 book “Watch Your Backyard,” Foreign Minister Omar Bula claimed that “Iran and Islamic extremist groups such a Hezbollah and Al Qaeda have profusely penetrated Latin America.”

As part of his foreign policy, President Abelardo de la Espriella has renewed ties with the United States, Israel and the United Arab Emirates.

In a response, the Iranian government said that the accusations of the De la Espriella government go “against the principles of mutual respect” and damage both countries’ “interests and benefits.”

“It is clear that none of the arguments put forward by the Colombian government to justify this decision are valid or logical, and that this measure was adopted solely under the influence of the Zionist regime and the United States,” said Iran’s foreign ministry.

World.title: ACSN extends lockdown of Colombia’s Caribbean coast to Friday morning
World.content:
Santa Marta-based organized crime group ACSN said Wednesday that the lockdown it has imposed on parts of Colombia’s Caribbean coast will be lifted on Friday morning.

In its first formal statement, the ACSN said that “the armed strike announced for 72 hours will end at 7:00AM on Friday 25 September 2026.”

The lockdown, which was initially called for 48 hours on Monday, has devastated the legal economy in the port city, particularly after ACSN assassins uploaded videos of them opening fire at stores that ignored the order to social media.

The online videos and half a dozen burnt buses and taxis all but cleared the streets of Santa Marta, which became a ghost town on Tuesday.

“We have never seen anything like this,” one Santa Marta resident told news program El Reporte Coronell.

President Abelardo de la Espriella announced the militarization of Santa Marta, but this was barely visible in the city’s downtown area and in the majority of Santa Marta’s neighborhoods.

“There are no police or soldiers in the streets, the people feel unprotected and are in panic,” said journalist Javier Manjarres on social media platform X.

“The current situation is a consequence of the behavior of the security forces and the decisions taken by the National Government in regards to our organization,” the organized crime group said in their statement.

The ACSN admitted that the clandestine lockdown was the result of the killing of Jose Luis Perez, a.k.a. “Cholo,” one of its commanders in the region around the Sierra Nevada mountain range just outside the city.

According to the group, security forces executed Cholo in front of his wife after his arrest.

An 18-year-old farmhand with no ties to the organization was also executed by the security, his family told media.

The lockdown has been imposed throughout the Magdalena and La Guajira provinces, a region where the group dominates organized crime and controls drug trafficking route to the Caribbean.

World.title: Messi leaves Argentina's national team after 21 years with a fortune Forbes puts at US$1.1 billion
World.content:
Messi leaves Argentina's national team after 21 years with a fortune Forbes puts at US$1.1 billion

7th Wednesday, October 2026 - 10:00 UTC Full article

He announced his international retirement after the 2026 World Cup: “I emptied myself; I have nothing more to give.”

Lionel Messi played his last match for Argentina on Tuesday, a friendly against Benin that ended 3-0 at Buenos Aires' Monumental stadium before more than 80,000 spectators. At 39, he closes a 21-year international career while consolidating a fortune that Forbes estimates at US$1.1 billion.

The captain set up Nicolás Otamendi, who was also bidding farewell to the national team, for the first goal and Nico Paz for the second, and scored the third from the penalty spot in the 70th minute, his 126th goal for Argentina, a national team record. “This is surely the saddest day of my career and I will miss you,” he said after the match. The anthem was performed by Fabio Santana, a veteran of the 1982 war.

With the national team he won the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, the 2021 and 2024 Copa América, the 2022 Finalissima, Olympic gold in Beijing in 2008 and the 2005 Under-20 World Cup. He announced his international retirement after the 2026 World Cup: “I emptied myself; I have nothing more to give.”

His activity off the pitch has grown. Forbes calculates he earned around US$1.8 billion over his career, before taxes and fees; other estimates put his net worth between US$850 million and US$1 billion. In the magazine's 2026 list of the highest-paid athletes he ranks third, with US$140 million, half from sport and half from endorsements and business.

At Inter Miami, where he is under contract until 2028, he receives US$28.3 million in guaranteed compensation, according to the league's players' union, and the club has said he will become a partner when he retires. He has had a lifetime contract with Adidas since 2017.

Messi owns or co-owns five clubs in four countries: Inter Miami; Leones de Rosario, chaired by his brother Matías; Unió Esportiva Cornellà and Club Deportivo Eldense of Spain's second division, whose purchase awaits approval; and Deportivo LSM of Uruguay's third division, which he joined in May 2025. He also owns six MiM hotels in Spain and Andorra, wine and fragrance lines, and real estate stakes in Rosario and Barcelona. The family holding company that manages his businesses, Limecu España 2010, moved its headquarters to Andorra in 2025.

“Business is something that interests me. I would like to keep learning because I know nothing and I am just starting out,” he said in November 2025.

World.title: Trump promises payments to voters ahead of midterms dominated by the cost of living
World.content:
Trump promises payments to voters ahead of midterms dominated by the cost of living

7th Wednesday, October 2026 - 08:07 UTC Full article

The promise of US$5,000 per adult, made in September, is not an approved measure and would require authorisation by Congress

US President Donald Trump has announced a series of direct payments to various groups of citizens in recent weeks and has promised US$5,000 to every adult if Republicans keep control of Congress in the November 3 midterm elections, in which the cost of living is shaping up as the central issue.

The latest is a cheque of around US$90 for more than 20 million retirees, intended to help them pay their Medicare Part B premium, the public health insurance for people over 65. “My Administration will immediately begin sending checks of almost $100,” Trump wrote on Truth Social. According to an analysis by health policy foundation KFF, the payment will not reach the 35 million beneficiaries enrolled in private plans, and the standard annual premium of US$2,435 will rise by US$79 next year, absorbing much of the cheque. The administration also announced in early October a US$500 payment to around one million people insured under the programme known as Obamacare.

The promise of US$5,000 per adult, made in September, is not an approved measure and would require authorisation by Congress. The announcements have drawn criticism for coinciding with the election campaign.

The payments come amid economic discontent. According to an AP-NORC poll published last week, almost three in four Americans describe the economy as poor and 69% disapprove of the president's handling of it, including 57% of those identifying as Republicans. Obamacare premiums rose this year after a pandemic-era tax credit expired, and the war with Iran has driven up energy costs.

“We keep telling the American people not to believe what's in their own checkbook. That's not going to work,” Republican Senator John Kennedy of Louisiana warned in an interview with NBC.

Republicans hold narrow majorities in both chambers. Five election forecasting models give Democrats between a 56% and 73% chance of controlling the Senate and between 76% and 99% of winning the House of Representatives.

World.title: Former Venezuelan Supreme Court justice says she was coerced into barring Machado
World.content:
Former Venezuelan Supreme Court justice says she was coerced into barring Machado

7th Wednesday, October 2026 - 07:11 UTC Full article

“My relatives' lives were used to force me to sign key decisions that affected the democratic course of the country,” said César Siero

Former Venezuelan Supreme Court justice Bárbara César Siero has alleged that the detention of two of her brothers and her sister-in-law in late 2023 was used to force her to sign the rulings that kept opposition leader María Corina Machado barred from office. She made the claims in a 43-minute video posted on YouTube on Tuesday.

“My relatives' lives were used to force me to sign key decisions that affected the democratic course of the country,” said César Siero, a justice since 2014 and until 2024 vice president of the Political-Administrative Chamber. According to her account, General Guillermo Enrique César Siero, Major Guillermo Henry César Siero and Major Diana Victoria Justo were detained and disappeared from December 15, 2023, the same day Machado filed her appeal to recover her political rights under the Barbados agreements. The former justice says that, fearing for their lives, she signed the rulings in December and again in January 2024, and was later forced to resign: “They told me that if I didn't resign, it would go worse for me.”

Her three relatives were sentenced last week — the general to 12 years in prison and the other two to three — in the case known as Brazalete Blanco, over an alleged plot to assassinate then president Nicolás Maduro, a case she describes as “fabricated”. Human rights defender Rocío San Miguel was acquitted in the same proceedings.

César Siero says she appealed without response to then Supreme Court president Gladys Gutiérrez, then attorney general Tarek William Saab and Defence Minister Vladimir Padrino. She says she also wrote to acting president Delcy Rodríguez, and that only the new ombudsman, Eglée González Lobato, agreed to review the case; her amnesty request was rejected. None of those named has commented. The former justice has requested protection from the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights, the UN human rights office and Human Rights Watch.

Machado was unable to register for the 2024 presidential election and the opposition fielded Edmundo González Urrutia instead. The UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission has repeatedly questioned the independence of Venezuela's judiciary.

The allegation comes as the interim government and the National Assembly negotiate, at US-backed talks, a complete overhaul of the Supreme Court, whose number of justices has been expanded from 20 to 32. The committee that is to select them has yet to be formed.

World.title: British Airways restores non-stop London-Buenos Aires flights and adds a daily Santiago service
World.content:
British Airways restores non-stop London-Buenos Aires flights and adds a daily Santiago service

6th Tuesday, October 2026 - 22:31 UTC Full article

According to the airline, it will be the only non-stop flight between London and Buenos Aires

British Airways will operate a daily non-stop flight between London Heathrow and Buenos Aires from March 28, 2027, continuing on to Santiago, Chile. A direct route between the British and Argentine capitals has not operated since October 2023.

The service, flights BA245 and BA244, will use a Boeing 777. According to the airline, it will be the only non-stop flight between London and Buenos Aires. The Argentine capital is currently served via Rio de Janeiro; from March, the daily London–Rio flight will no longer continue to Buenos Aires, freeing seats for the Brazilian market.

For Chile, the change means a new daily one-stop service via Buenos Aires, in addition to the non-stop London–Santiago flight the airline operates three times a week, according to the release and specialist aviation media.

“Buenos Aires has always been a key part of our South American network, and we are delighted to strengthen our commitment with a daily non-stop service from London,” said Neil Chernoff, British Airways' director of network planning and strategy, as the airline marks 80 years of flights to the region.

The announcement, made on September 17, is part of a 25% increase in the airline's Latin American capacity for the European summer 2027 season, which also makes its San José, Costa Rica route year-round and adds new routes to Tanzania from May.

Chile's air traffic shows a market in decline. According to the Civil Aeronautics Board, 2,188,070 passengers flew in August, down 2.1% year on year; international traffic fell 2.8% and arrivals from Europe 2.2%.

World.title: Lula targets non-voters and over-70s to overturn the first-round result
World.content:
Lula targets non-voters and over-70s to overturn the first-round result

6th Tuesday, October 2026 - 22:15 UTC Full article

Since Brazil returned to direct presidential elections in 1989, no candidate who came second in the first round has won the runoff.

Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will focus his campaign for the October 25 runoff on mobilising those who did not vote on Sunday, particularly people over 70, and on winning over centrist voters, after finishing almost two points behind Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round.

The challenge is historic. Since Brazil returned to direct presidential elections in 1989, no candidate who came second in the first round has won the runoff.

From the age of 70, voting is no longer compulsory in Brazil, and in 2022 abstention in that group was around 60%, according to figures cited by the newspaper El País. The last Datafolha poll before the vote gave Lula an 11-point lead among older voters. The president had already appealed to them in the final stretch: “Don't think that because you're 70 you shouldn't vote. Go, get up and vote.”

According to Reuters, Lula is also considering announcing that his vice president, Geraldo Alckmin, a centre-right figure, would be his finance minister in a new term, as a gesture to business. The Workers' Party is also hoping Congress will this week approve its proposal to cut working hours to guarantee two days off a week without a pay cut.

“The runoff is another election. It involves a direct clash of projects,” party president Edinho Silva told Globo, adding that Lula would attend “all the debates he can”. On election night, the president linked his rival to organised crime in Rio de Janeiro; Bolsonaro is under investigation in the Banco Master case, without formal charges, and there is no known case against him for organised crime.

Bolsonaro, of the Liberal Party, appeared in Brasília on Tuesday alongside São Paulo governor Tarcísio de Freitas, re-elected on Sunday, and is seeking the backing of his Republicanos party and other right-wing groups. The candidates eliminated in the first round won around 8% of the vote. The senator said he would attend the debates if Lula does: “I want to compare government programmes.” Neither took part in a debate in the first round. The first runoff debate is scheduled for Sunday 11.

World.title: UK agrees £190m Airbus deal to boost RAF's strategic airlift fleet of A400M Atlas
World.content:
UK agrees £190m Airbus deal to boost RAF's strategic airlift fleet of A400M Atlas

6th Tuesday, October 2026 - 09:08 UTC Full article

The British Forces South Atlantic Islands command utilizes the A400M's long-range capabilities to secure and monitor the remote British Overseas Territory.

The UK Ministry of Defence has signed a £190m contract extension with Airbus to deliver a 30% improvement in the availability of the Royal Air Force's tactical and strategic airlift fleet.

The 31-month extension to the medium-term contract will see Airbus continue its maintenance, repair and support for the RAF's A400M Atlas fleet from its UK Support Centre at RAF Brize Norton.

The contract extension through to April 2029 will mean that there will be a significant boost to operational capability and will increase the number of fully capable aircraft available each day from 10 to 13 by the end of next year.

One of them is permanently stationed at MPC in the Falkland Islands as part of No. 1312Flight

Defence Readiness and Industry Minister Luke Pollard said that the deal was a “vote of confidence” for the industry and Brize Norton.

“By boosting availability, we're strengthening the RAF's ability to conduct global operations and deliver on Nato commitments when it matters most,” Mr Pollard said.

The deal comes after “intensive” negotiations led by a small team from the A400M In-Service Support Delivery Team within the NAD Group at Brize Norton with the RAF, industry partners and Airbus.

The A400M Atlas is a cornerstone of the UK's air mobility capability, which is involved in supporting operations ranging from humanitarian relief to rapid troop deployment.

The continued support at Brize Norton will mean that the fleet is ready to meet the demands required without interruption.

“Airbus is proud to be a trusted partner to the Ministry of Defence, and this contract extension reinforces that commitment,” Kata Escott, Airbus Defence and Space UK's managing director, said.

“The A400M Atlas is the backbone of air mobility. Our highly skilled teams work side by side with Royal Air Force personnel and are fully focused on enhancing operational readiness, keeping the fleet mission-ready.”

The A400M Atlas, which has a 42.4m wingspan, is a strategic airlift aircraft powered by its four turboprop engines. The aircraft entered into service with the RAF more than a decade ago, and it is designed to go where other aircraft cannot.

It can fly at up to 40,000ft, while it can hold anything from a Chinook helicopter to 37 tonnes of freight. It can take off and land on beaches or rough terrain meaning it is indispensable for missions in remote areas.

World.title: On first Monday in October Falklands celebrates Peat Cutting Day
World.content:
On first Monday in October Falklands celebrates Peat Cutting Day

6th Tuesday, October 2026 - 09:04 UTC Full article

Peat for decades was used in Falklands to heat homes and cooking food

Monday 5th October has been a public holiday in the Falkland Islands. This is because the first Monday in October every year has been declared Peat Cutting Day, which is a way of celebrating a long standing tradition and recalling the primary fuel that for decades kept Islanders and their homes warm.

October was the time of the year when Islanders wnet out to cut cubes of surface-soil peat, predominant in the Islands, and was used as fuel for heating homes and cooking food in the Islands.

In 2002, the Executive Council of the Falkland Islands made it an official public holiday to be celebrated on the first Monday in October every year. Little peat cutting takes place in modern times, since the Islands have other sources of energy, fossil fuels, electricity (mostly eolic) and other green alternatives.

For decades the smell of peat heating was a distinctive pattern of Stanley and Camp settlements.

World.title: Paraguay's opposition takes Asunción from the Colorado Party and holds Ciudad del Este
World.content:
Paraguay's opposition takes Asunción from the Colorado Party and holds Ciudad del Este

5th Monday, October 2026 - 22:09 UTC Full article

In Ciudad del Este, Daniel Pereira Mujica of the opposition Yo Creo party won with 72.83%, keeping the city in the hands of the party previously led locally by Miguel Prieto

Paraguay's opposition won the mayoralty of Asunción and held that of Ciudad del Este, the country's two most populous cities, in Sunday's municipal elections, according to preliminary results from the electoral authority. The ruling Colorado Party, however, won the vast majority of districts.

With 99.92% of polling stations counted, civil engineer Soledad Núñez of the Alianza Juntos por Asunción won 47.78% of the vote to 45.98% for Colorado candidate Camilo Pérez, president of the Paraguayan Olympic Committee, a margin of 5,024 votes. Núñez was backed by the Patria Querida and Authentic Radical Liberal parties. “Asunción voted, Asunción won. Today the people who don't give up, who resist, who can't be bought, won,” she said on election night.

In Ciudad del Este, Daniel Pereira Mujica of the opposition Yo Creo party won with 72.83%, keeping the city in the hands of the party previously led locally by Miguel Prieto. Prieto has expressed interest in running for president in 2028.

The Colorado Party, to which President Santiago Peña belongs, was winning in 187 of 263 districts and 11 of 17 departmental capitals, and regained the mayoralty of Encarnación. The figures from the preliminary results transmission system must be confirmed by the official count.

After the vote, Núñez said the opposition would file a complaint with prosecutors over the publication of exit polls during election day. A consultancy posted trends for several cities on social media an hour before polls closed, without naming candidates. The Electoral Code prohibits publishing such polls until an hour after closing. “This goes against electoral participation,” said Núñez, who argued the publication may have discouraged voters. Liberal senator Celeste Amarilla called the poll “illegal” and said she would file a complaint if no one else did. The consultancy was not publicly identified and did not comment. Turnout in Asunción was 61.75%, up from 59.65% in 2021.

Municipal elections serve as a political barometer ahead of the 2028 general election.

World.title: El Jalapeño: Bomb squad heroically ‘defuses’ suspicious churros found on Mexico City Metro
World.content:
All stories in El Jalapeño are satire and not real news. Check out the original article here.

MEXICO CITY — Emergency protocol gave way to quick-thinking heroism on Metro Line 7 Friday afternoon after elite bomb disposal units successfully neutralized a highly volatile cardboard box containing dozens of freshly fried, cinnamon-sugar-dusted churros.

The high-stakes incident began when an alert commuter flagged an unattended package sitting isolated on a southbound train traveling from El Rosario toward Barranca del Muerto. Within minutes, officers from Mexico City’s Policía Bancaria e Industrial (PBI) established a safety perimeter at the Mixcoac station, donning heavy protective gear to approach what tactical analysts classified as an imminent threat to local waistlines.

“Initial field assessments indicated a dangerous combination of crispy exteriors, soft doughy interiors, and a dusting of sugar that presented a clear and present hazard,” said lead bomb technician Commander Arturo Gómez, wiping a trace of cajeta filling from his chin during a press briefing. “Standard procedure dictates controlled detonation, but given the golden-brown quality of the target, our team made the tactical decision to neutralize the threat orally, piece by piece.”

Witnesses reported that the multi-stage defusal operation took approximately six minutes, with officers systematically consuming the pastries alongside small tactical cups of warm champurrado supplied by a nearby platform vendor. According to official police logs, all units involved displayed exemplary discipline, ensuring that not a single drop of chocolate sauce was left on the train car floor.

Metro authorities praised the rapid response, citing it as a testament to the department’s unwavering commitment to public safety and street-food preservation. Officials confirmed that while the owner of the box was not located, the vendor’s lost inventory had been thoroughly and safely processed and deemed entirely non-lethal, albeit slightly heavy on the digestion.

“In operations of this nature, every second counts before the dough loses its crunch,” Gómez added, adjusting his tactical vest. “We urge the public to remain vigilant, report any suspicious, freshly baked goods immediately, and allow trained professionals to handle the situation before the churros go cold.”
