World.title: Father of 3: The first child benefit should be very generous in Estonia
World.content:
Director Madis Ligema, who recently became a father for the third time, told ETV that while money does not necessarily motivate people to have children, more generous benefits could increase the number of births in Estonia.

"The benefit for the first child in particular should be massive to encourage people to have that first child because once you have the first, then the second and third — and perhaps even a fourth — will follow," Madis Ligema said.

Economist and Family Foundation supervisory board member Raul Eamets, however, stressed the importance of supporting families having a third child.

"When people are planning a third child, it actually means a kind of qualitative change in their living arrangements because it means needing an extra room or a larger car, as three child seats won't fit in every car. Why is the issue of a third child so important? Half of Estonia's children live in families with three or more children," Eamets explained.

Parental benefit and a fixed percentage of GDP

As one way of increasing the birth rate, Eamets suggested extending parental benefits to parents who stay at home: "There are certainly parents, whether fathers or mothers, who do this, but we have taken that option away from them. I, for example, really liked Heido Vitsur and Indrek Neivelt's proposal that if you have decided to raise children full time, you receive the Estonian median wage — their proposal was €500 per child, so if you have three children, that would be €1,500," Eamets said.

Member of the European Parliament Jana Toom (Center Party) said Estonia should make supporting families with children a national priority and allocate a fixed share of the budget to it.

"Our child benefits are shamefully low. We have an extraordinarily high percentage of children living in relative poverty and outright poverty," said Toom, a mother of five. "We need to develop a national policy specifically focused on children and allocate a certain percentage of GDP to it, just as we do with defense," Toom said.

Inconsistent support measures rob people of certainty

According to Elin Järvsaar, editor-in-chief of "Pere ja Kodu," stability in benefits is important to parents, while constant changes to legislation discourage young people from becoming parents.

"More important than the amounts is a sense of security. In recent years, we have made a great many changes to the system of family benefits and allowances. That provides no sense of security whatsoever — up and down, back and forth, the rules keep changing," said Järvsaar, a mother of four. "The system has been made so complicated and it gives me no confidence that I will have support for 18 years. Even if parental benefits or other benefits are extremely generous, I know that four years from now they could be completely different and I don't dare take that step," Järvsaar explained.

Raul Eamets agreed that the demographic problem requires a long-term agreement similar to that on national defense. "Family policy and demographic issues are every bit as important as security, meaning that we need a consensus across society and across party lines. By now, I think all parties have realized that this is a problem, but what we need now are decisions that extend beyond election cycles and strategic decisions. One coalition raises benefits, the next lowers them — I completely understand women wondering how they can dare take those risks under such circumstances. Otherwise, we will simply die out," Eamets said.

A total of 9,240 children were born in Estonia in 2025, a record low. During the discussion, Eamets predicted that the number of births could fall below 9,000 this year.

World.title: Estonia might struggle to fill conscript ranks with men alone in the near future
World.content:
Filling the required number of conscript positions with men alone could soon become difficult as the number of male births declines, Anu Rannaveski, director general of the Defense Resources Agency, said.

Rannaveski said the commander of the Estonian Defense Forces determines the number of conscripts each year. That figure, in turn, is based on the number of reservists needed. In recent years, the number of conscripts has ranged from around 3,600 to 3,800. Starting next year, up to 4,100 conscripts will be called up for military service.

According to Rannaveski, around 50 women enter military service each year. Women have been able to volunteer for military service since 2013 and the figure has generally remained at around 50 since then. "There have been a couple of years when there were 60 women and there have been years when there were 45, but it has remained at around 50," Rannaveski said. She added that women account for 1 to 2 percent of conscripts.

Conscript need must be met

Rannaveski noted that demographic trends show the number of boys being born is declining and the situation will get progressively worse. Rannaveski added that the Defense Forces will nevertheless have to find a way to reach the target of 4,100 conscripts.

In 2025, Estonia's total births came to 9,240, including 4,789 boys.

She explained that more than half of Estonian society currently has little opportunity to contribute to national defense. Rannaveski said women do have the option of entering military service, but they have to find the motivation to do so themselves. By contrast, the state actively reaches out to men, she noted.

Women can currently serve in a variety of units. "The concern that there are specific roles for women is certainly unfounded — women perform very well across the board," Rannaveski said.

Both men and women improve their physical abilities during military service. "When we talk about young men entering military service, only about a third meet the physical requirements that are actually needed," Rannaveski said.

She said that during military service, women want to have access to the same information as the rest of their unit. As a result, they stay in the same barracks and rooms as the men. "They use the lockers there to divide up the room and create some privacy for themselves," Rannaveski said. However, separate hygiene facilities are generally provided for women.

Changes in order

The director said that between 2035 and 2040, it will become difficult to fill the required number of conscript positions with young men alone. She added that in that case, a more compulsory system would have to be introduced.

Rannaveski said Estonia should develop a system that works for the country. She noted that in Norway, Sweden and Denmark, not all women are required to perform military service. "They have criteria: who is the most highly motivated and who has the knowledge, experience and skills that the Defense Forces need," she explained.

She noted she hopes Estonia will adopt a similar approach, adding that making military service mandatory for everyone would also not be a good fit as there would be more people than conscript positions.

World.title: Restaurant spaces in Tallinn do not stay empty for long
World.content:
Many eateries in Tallinn have closed over the past year. Real estate agencies say, however, that there are still plenty of entrepreneurs who want to open new places. Interest from business owners coming from Asia has grown, for example.

This year, restaurants such as Tai Boh, Boheem, Vatikan, Manna La Rosa, Ülo and La Tabla have closed. Even Siili Sahver, a lunch spot that survived the COVID crisis, shut down.

Aira Veelmaa, a commercial real estate broker at Uus Maa, said the situation is not as difficult as media coverage might suggest.

"Looking at the commercial property market, I would say restaurant spaces are among the most sought‑after. There are quite a few people who want to start something new. There is also a more exotic group of clients who have come to Estonia and want to start a business here. Not knowing the Estonian market, they often have more enthusiasm than locals," Veelmaa said.

By "more exotic regions," Veelmaa means people from the Middle East and other parts of Asia.

Popular restaurant spaces often have several interested tenants. Still, some areas are more difficult, such as Narva maantee, where places constantly change. Despite the busy location, restaurants there often do not last long, Veelmaa noted.

The situation is most challenging for eateries located in office buildings because many people work from home. Owners also have to make sure there are not too many food places nearby, since there may not be enough customers for all of them.

But the trend is slightly positive, and more entrepreneurs are looking to open new places, Veelmaa said.

Tanel Tarum of the real estate agency 1Partner also said the situation is not as bad as it may seem from media reports.

"If we look at how many new places are opening, the balance in Tallinn is zero," Tarum said.

He acknowledged that people's movement patterns have changed over time, and areas like Telliskivi and the Volta quarter now see more foot traffic than a few years ago. He added that one reason for closures is insufficient groundwork before opening a restaurant.

World.title: Tallinn Airport sets record for September, but winter traffic expected to fall
World.content:
Tallinn Airport reported it handled nearly 356,000 passengers in September, up 13 percent on the same month last year — the busiest September in the airport's history.

In the first nine months of the year, the airport reported serving a total of 2.89 million passengers, up 12 percent on the same period last year.

Despite the record, the airport expects a decline in numbers over the winter.

Tallinn Airport spokesperson Aet Härmaorg told ERR the past 12 months have all been records on the month, adding the "all-time record was exceeded in four months: May, June, July and August 2026."

Scheduled flights operated from Tallinn to 41 destinations in September. Passenger growth was driven primarily by no-frills carrier Wizz Air, which has expanded significantly in Tallinn over the past year.

In September, the airline carried 16 percent of all Tallinn Airport passengers and offered connections to nine destinations. airBaltic remained the airport's largest airline, with a market share of 27 percent. In total, 22 airlines operated scheduled and charter flights from Tallinn to more than 50 destinations during the month.

Scheduled flights accounted for 90 percent of passengers, while charter flights accounted for 10 percent. Antalya, Turkey, was the main charter destination, with holiday destinations in Greece and Montenegro also proving popular.

While winter is the off-season, there is a winter travel season, starting September, to destinations in Egypt.

Warsaw was the most popular direct destination for scheduled flights in September, followed by Helsinki, Riga, Stockholm and Frankfurt.

The number of aircraft movements also rose, by 5 percent compared with September last year. There were 4,031 landings and take-offs in total, averaging 134 aircraft movements per day.

Eero Pärgmäe, commercial director at Tallinn Airport, said the passenger records show the summer schedule was exceptionally dense. "The growth that Wizz Air started at the end of last year is still carrying us," Pärgmäe told ERR.

Nonetheless, some developments will lead to a fall in numbers over winter. "airBaltic has said it is cutting its schedule due to the restructuring it is currently carrying out. And the second thing is that, since the price of aviation fuel remains exceptionally high, most carriers have said that the high fuel price is hurting them and they will be scaling back their schedules in winter," Pärgmäe went on.

"If we look at next year, we are moving toward last year's level or even a little below," he added.

Passenger numbers also rose at Estonia's regional airports, which fall under the Tallinn Airport umbrella. Together, they served 9,078 passengers in September, compared with 8,191 in September last year. Tartu Airport took in 4,847 passengers, Kuressaare Airport 3,008 and Kärdla Airport 1,111. Pärnu Airport served 104 passengers and Ruhnu Airfield eight.

Tallinn Airport also says it expects higher passenger numbers during the busy school holiday travel period, October 21-November 4. For this reason the airport recommends arriving at the terminal at least two hours before departure time, as check-in, security screening and passport control can take longer than usual. Passengers arriving by car should allow extra time to find a parking space too.

World.title: Cost of new Iisaku school building nearly doubles
World.content:
The cost of building a new school for Iisaku Basic School in Alutaguse municipality has risen far beyond initial plans. The opposition is unhappy with how the process has been handled and intends to file a no‑confidence motion against the mayor.

Originally, most of the funding was to come from the state, which supported the municipality after it closed Iisaku's high school level. During the process, the scope of construction expanded and the price nearly doubled from the initial €6.8 million. For the municipality, this means contributing around €6 million, most of which will be covered by loans. Municipal leaders say they are confident the municipality can manage the debt.

"It was a simple choice: either accept the state support and build, even if our share becomes larger than planned, or not build. I'm glad the council decided to take the support and complete the school building as planned. I think it's a forward‑looking and correct decision for Alutaguse municipality," said Mayor Tauno Võhmar.

The opposition says several mistakes were made in the process.

"We were not shown the new budget strategy, nor was there a supplementary budget. The mayor had no right to enter a procurement with a much larger construction volume without council approval. The opposition will move forward with a no‑confidence motion because we do not trust this mayor and do not approve of this behavior," said opposition representative Annely Oone.

Iisaku Basic School currently has around 100 students. The new school building is expected to be completed next autumn and is designed for 135 students.

World.title: Iraq’s foreign reserves may fall to $60 billion by end of 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A Standard Chartered economist said on Wednesday that Iraq may resort to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) if oil revenues continue to fall and the currency’s devaluation fails to boost state finances as intended.

Standard Chartered chief economist for the Middle East and Pakistan Carla Slim said that any potential program with the IMF could entail structural reforms, particularly regarding the public sector wage bill, to enhance fiscal sustainability, Bloomberg reported.

If the current pace of depletion continues, Iraq’s foreign reserves might fall to roughly $60 billion by the end of the year, down from over $100 billion at the beginning of the year, according to Slim.

The economist indicated that the local currency’s exchange rate may be adjusted again in the future months, based on changes in oil earnings and foreign reserves.

According to IMF data, Iraq’s foreign currency reserves currently stand at approximately $85 billion.

Standard Chartered is a leading British multinational banking and financial services company headquartered in London.

World.title: Iraq to ban Israeli-developed GPS navigation app Waze
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has formally banned the Waze navigation application, pushing the effective date until the end of December 2026.

Iraqi Communications Minister Mustafa Sanad originally planned to start the block in early 2027. However, the government recently changed the timeframe, pushing the restriction ahead to late December 2026.

Waze’s Israeli roots influenced the decision, which aligns with Iraq’s strict 2022 legislation criminalizing rapprochement with Israel.

The Iraqi government raises security, data privacy, and geopolitical concerns over geographic tracking data.

While it is unclear how the Iraqi government would restrict access to the application, technology analysts expect local telecommunication providers to block Waze servers or ban the program outright from regional app stores.

The step triggered rapid online discussion among Iraqis. Drivers expressed disappointment at losing Waze’s extremely accurate, real-time traffic updates, which are critical for navigating crowded cities like Baghdad.

The Communication Ministry suggested using Google Maps as a primary legal alternative, even though Google owns both Google Maps and Waze.

World.title: Iraq lowers currency exchange rate to 1,500 dinars per US dollar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has officially depreciated its national currency, with the baseline dropping from about 1,300 Iraqi dinars to 1,500 dinars per US dollar.

The Iraqi cabinet approved on Tuesday the structural adjustment, which marks a 14.5 percent decline compared to the previous official framework that had been in place since early 2023.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) established a multi-tiered exchange framework to facilitate the transition across commercial and banking channels.

An exchange rate of 1,500 Iraqi dinars per US dollar is now used for government purchases from the Finance Ministry, 1,510 Iraqi dinars for official sales to commercial banking institutions, and 1,520 Iraqi dinars for public consumers who buy foreign currency directly from banks.

The forceful monetary policy shift acts as a direct fiscal stabilization mechanism in response to significant macroeconomic shocks.

The regional conflict has severely affected important marine trade routes, including partial closures and interruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. Since oil exports account for about 90 percent of Iraq’s national finances, transportation delays reduced real export capacity to around 2.34 million barrels per day compared to 3.6 million.

The Finance Ministry informed the Iraqi parliament that it would be unable to cover the domestic budget for 2026 unless the dinar was revalued.

By demanding more local dinars for every US dollar of incoming oil revenue, the Iraqi government generates artificial liquidity to meet rising public expenditure, local deficits, and civil service salaries.

The depreciation is intended to reduce the disparity between the government’s stated measurements and parallel market realities.

Following the announcement, parallel market rates in Baghdad and Erbil soared, with exchange shops reporting market gains of more than 1,700 Iraqi dinars per US dollar.

The Iraqi cabinet also prohibited the collection of advance customs duties on foreign imports to reduce unexpected operational disruptions within business supply chains.

World.title: Iraq’s trade exchange with China surpass $51 billion in 2025
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Chinese Ambassador to Iraq, Xiang Bo, revealed on Tuesday that the trade exchange between Iraq and China exceeded $51 billion in 2025.

In a statement to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), Bo noted that relations between China and Iraq are continually improving. He emphasized that Iraq is a crucial partner for China in the Belt and Road Initiative, which has yielded positive outcomes.

Major Chinese firms are involved in the construction and development of several industries in Iraq, such as oil, energy, and infrastructure, according to Bo.

Bo emphasized that the cooperation between the two countries is based on shared interests and is continuously developing.

The Chinese diplomat expressed his hope that this collaboration will continue and grow into other sectors, contributing to the development of a complete partnership between Iraq and China.

The two countries’ strong economic interdependence assures a bright future and enormous possibilities for collaboration, according to Bo.

Chinese companies have been heavily involved in the oil industry and in significant infrastructure projects, such as the construction of major bridges and schools, with more than 600 schools completed in various Iraqi provinces.

China’s investments in Iraq are also rapidly rising, notably in infrastructure and energy.

World.title: Iraq advances as Gulf-Europe data hub with iQ Networks, Ooredoo fibre deal
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s iQ Networks and OFN, the international connectivity arm of Qatar’s Ooredoo Group, have agreed to build a high-capacity fibre connection across Iraq, furthering ambitions to connect the Gulf and Asia to Turkey and Europe via Iraqi territory.

According to the arrangement, OFN will buy numerous dark fibre pairs from iQ Networks for international transit throughout Iraq.

The terrestrial network will link to Ooredoo’s proposed Fibre in Gulf (FIG) subsea cable infrastructure, creating a single route for international data traffic.

The project might boost Iraq’s position as a regional digital transit center, using the country’s geographical location between the Arabian Gulf, Turkey, and Europe to transport increasing quantities of international data.

FIG is intended to link Qatar, Oman, the UAE, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and Iraq with a capacity of up to 720 terabits per second across 24 fibre pairs.

OFN has also struck a landing agreement with the state-owned Iraqi Telecommunications and Post Company (ITPC) to send the undersea cable into Iraq.

From there, iQ Networks’ terrestrial infrastructure will transport connections north across the nation to Turkey and European markets.

According to the firms, the new corridor will serve as an extra route between the Gulf and Europe while also increasing network resilience and capacity.

The need for such infrastructure is fast expanding as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, data centers, telecom operators, and big technology businesses require increasing quantities of international bandwidth.

The deal was signed at the Ooredoo Group’s headquarters in Doha by top Iraqi communications authorities as well as executives from Ooredoo, OFN, ITPC, and iQ Networks.

For Iraq, the initiative is part of a larger attempt to transform its position into an economic benefit by attracting international data traffic that would otherwise utilize other regional routes.

The infrastructure might also help Iraq’s developing digital economy and data center industry, as well as provide new possibilities for foreign traffic passing through the country.

Implementation will continue in accordance with the agreed-upon plan, subject to regulatory and government approval.

The initiative is another step toward establishing Iraq as a digital bridge between Asia, the Arabian Gulf, and Europe, broadening the country’s significance beyond conventional energy and commercial channels.

World.title: US dollar surges past 180,000 IQD amid parallel market disruption
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Parallel currency exchanges across Iraq experienced severe disruption and sharp price swings on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, after the federal government abruptly modified the official exchange rate benchmark to 1,500 dinars per dollar for purchases and 1,520 dinars for retail sales to citizens.

The unexpected regulatory shift sent shockwaves through cash trading floors, propelling parallel dollar prices past the 170,000-dinar threshold per $100 and triggering deep regional rate discrepancies across major commercial centers.

Trading data collated across provincial exchanges reflected widespread variance as exchange desks struggled with price discovery. In Baghdad, cash selling rates settled at 170,000 dinars per $100 against purchase bids of 168,250 dinars. In Erbil, the commercial hub of the Kurdistan Region, prices surged even higher, with sales touching 180,000 dinars alongside a wide bid-ask spread anchored by buying offers at 166,500 dinars.

In the southern port city of Basra, trading desks quoted selling rates at 179,000 dinars per $100 against buying bids of 178,000 dinars, reflecting intense localized demand for physical greenbacks.

The rapid escalation in currency volatility coincided with growing legislative mobilization inside parliament, where lawmakers have begun organizing appeals for an emergency parliamentary session.

Proponents of the emergency hearing aim to legally compel the executive branch to reverse the sudden exchange rate hike and assess the broader economic and living strains imposed on households, warning that runaway parallel spreads risk amplifying retail inflation and destabilizing domestic supply chains.

World.title: Iraqi MP demands emergency session as official dollar hike paralyzes markets
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Member of Parliament Miqdad Al-Khafaji called on the Council of Representatives on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, to convene an immediate emergency session to compel the federal government to reverse its decision devaluing the Iraqi dinar against the U.S. dollar.

The legislative push comes as the official adjustment to 1,500 dinars per dollar triggers immediate price shocks, widespread commercial freezes, and severe market gridlock across Iraqi wholesale hubs.

In a formal statement, Al-Khafaji criticized the government’s fiscal priorities, pointing out that political factions continue to expand administrative overhead and create patronized public positions that bloat state expenditures, while forcing ordinary citizens to absorb the financial fallout of structural deficits.

Al-Khafaji warned that devaluing the currency directly erodes the real purchasing power of fixed-income public servants, daily wage laborers, and low-income families, emphasizing that a public already strained by regional tensions cannot endure additional economic shocks.

Currency analysts and market participants anticipate that parallel exchange desks will soon test psychological highs of 180,000 dinars per $100 as greenback liquidity tightens.

The rapid depreciation of the dinar in real terms has triggered public frustration across Iraqi cities, where consumer earnings and local commerce remain heavily denominated in local currency.

On the commercial front, the devaluation has delivered immediate ripple effects to retail and wholesale food supply networks:

Retail Food Surges: Nabhan Al-Ahmad, a commercial market owner in Saladin Governorate, reported that consumer food staples experienced an immediate price hike of roughly 25 percent within hours of the cabinet announcement. A standard sack of rice that previously retailed for 45,000 dinars spiked to 50,000 dinars, with proportional increases hitting sugar, cooking oil, and packaged goods.

Distribution Freezes: Yousef Al-Rubaie, a sales agent for food distributor Altunsa, confirmed that major regional food supply and FMCG distribution firms have suspended shipments and wholesale deliveries until further notice to protect operational capital against volatile replacement costs.

Shorja Commercial Stagnation: In Baghdad’s central commercial district of Al-Shorja, wholesale centers have ground to an effective standstill. Abu Ahmed Al-Asadi, a prominent commercial center owner in Shorja, described the wholesale sector as completely paralyzed. Al-Asadi explained that activity had already begun stalling two weeks earlier amid regional geopolitical tensions and rising exchange rates, adding that the official devaluation has shut down the market entirely, forcing most wholesale merchants to shutter storefronts and suspend trade until currency volatility stabilizes.

As legislative calls grow for parliamentary intervention, commercial friction and consumer uncertainty continue to mount, presenting the administration with significant economic headwinds following its statutory rate revision.

World.title: Iraq Integrity Commission uncovers 2.19B IQD embezzlement in Salah Al-Din
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Federal Commission of Integrity announced on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, the uncovering of a major embezzlement scheme within the Salah Al-Din Traffic Directorate, involving the fraudulent manipulation of more than 56,000 official traffic citation receipts and the misappropriation of over 2.192 billion Iraqi dinars ($1.46 million at the newly adjusted official rate).

Investigators seized original forged accounting records and brought five senior ranking officers—including a brigadier general and four colonels—under active criminal inquiry.

According to an official statement, specialized field teams from the Commission’s Saladin Investigation Office audited financial ledgers and cross-matched serial numbers, exposing two distinct schemes operating within the governorate’s vehicle registration and driver licensing divisions:

The First Operation (1.853 Billion IQD): Investigators identified that the head of the Fines and Thefts Division at the Vehicle Registration and Driver Licensing Complex—a police officer holding the rank of colonel who is currently detained—systematically altered 34,164 traffic violation receipts under his legal custody. He embezzled 1,853,200,000 IQD in cash receipts. Executing a warrant issued by the Saladin Investigation Judge for Integrity Cases, anti-corruption agents raided the directorate and seized the physical originals of all 34,164 manipulated receipts.

The Second Operation (339.135 Million IQD): Further forensic audits revealed a parallel scheme executed by a second detained officer, also holding the rank of colonel. The suspect manipulated on-the-spot traffic citation forms and doctored ledger remittances, embezzling 339,135,000 IQD.The team seized 22,000 altered payment vouchers, specifically official standard revenue forms “Account 38” and “Account 68”.

The Commission confirmed that legal proceedings have expanded to include three additional supervisory officers: a brigadier general and two colonels. The senior officers face prosecution for dereliction of supervisory duty and failing to verify fine remittances, negligence that allowed the multi-billion-dinar fraud to persist undetected.

Formal seizure records, confiscated ledgers, and forensic documentary evidence were submitted to the competent investigating judge.The cases are being prosecuted under Article 315 of the Iraqi Penal Code No. 111 of 1969, which governs the embezzlement of public funds by state officials and carries severe statutory penalties, as judicial authorities continue interrogations to identify all co-conspirators.

World.title: India’s first high-altitude snow leopard safari flagged off in Ladakh
World.content:
File photo: Ladakh Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena

LEH/JAMMU: Ladakh lieutenant governor, Vinai Kumar Saxena, Wednesday flagged off Indiaâs first high-altitude wildlife safari focused on snow leopard trails, with an aim of making local communities âequal partners in protecting and promoting Ladakhâs wildlife and benefiting economicallyâ.âWildlife should not be protected at the cost of people, nor should development come at the cost of wildlife. We must create a model in which both can thrive together,â the LG said after flagging off six safari vehicles.The project, operated by the Snow Leopard and High-Altitude Nature Conservation (SHAN) Society in collaboration with the UTâs forest department, has mapped the safari routes through Hemis National Park, Changthang and Karakoram Wildlife Sanctuary, besides Nubra, Zanskar, Sham, Kargil, and Drass districts.Ladakh has 477 snow leopards out of 477 across India. The region is also home to more than 38 mammal species, over 340 bird species, and around 1,800 vascular plant species.

World.title: Jammu and Kashmir: PoK woman repatriated via Poonch
World.content:
JAMMU: A 19-year-old woman from Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), whom the Army had detained along the Line of Control (LoC) in Rajouriâs Nowshera last week, was repatriated Wednesday through Chakkan Da Bagh in Poonch district.

Armyâs 6/1 Gorkha Rifles had apprehended the womanâSamiya Azeem from Bains Gala, Seri, in PoKâs Kotli districtâin Lam area on Oct 2 after she entered India. She was later handed over to local police.

âAfter the completion of necessary formalities, police and Army personnel escorted her from Lam police post to Chakkan Da Bagh, where she was repatriated through the designated crossing point,â an official said.

World.title: Oceans connect, not divide nations, PM Modi says, calls for secure maritime order
World.content:
Doubling down on Indiaâs stand that sea lanes must not be turned into war zones and proposal to end conflict on Black Sea, PM Narendra Modi said oceans donât separate countries but these connect them while calling for a free, open, secure and rules-based maritime order.

In a message that was read out at Great Oceans Dialogue in Delhi, PM said, âThe oceans do not separate us, they connect us, because what happens in one part of the world can have an impact far beyond its shores...Our vision is a free, open, secure and rule-based maritime that brings greater peace, prosperity and progress for all.â Modi said Indiaâs maritime vision extends across regions and oceans, and is built on âcooperation, trust, mutual respect and mutual benefitâ.

His remarks come amid efforts to push a maritime understanding between Russia and Ukraine to keep the Black Sea open for commercial shipping and prevent attacks on vessels and critical maritime infrastructure. Indiaâs three-part ceasefire plan seeks to halt attacks on energy facilities and other critical infrastructure; continuous and unhindered movement of grain, crude oil, LNG and LPG through Black Sea ports; and a complete stop to attacks on commercial vessels, merchant ships, and maritime operations to safeguard seafarers and global supply chains.





The emphasis on maritime freedom assumes significance as attacks and disruptions in the Black Sea have affected commercial shipping, ports and movement of agricultural commodities during the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war.

Participating in a panel discussion, Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan said that they donât make any distinction between national security and national economic security. Swaminathan added that maritime security affects all nations as he stressed on the need for partnerships.

Invoking PMâs SAGAR and MAHASAGAR formulations, Swaminathan said maritime threats are increasingly transregional because oceans are contiguous. Cooperation, therefore, must extend beyond individual regions, with regions working together for collective security and growth.

World.title: Oligarchs blocking Starlink service in India: Elon Musk
World.content:
NEW DELHI: US business tycoon

, in a veiled attack on certain telecom operators, alleged that "certain oligarchs" have blocked his company's satellite communication services in India to maintain their monopoly in the country.

In response to information posted by the DodgeDesigner handle on social media platform X about the non-availability of mobile coverage in over 11,000 villages, Musk said: "Unfortunately, we are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people.

"You can guess who they are... This is a crime against the people of India!" Musk posted on X.

A verified account operating in the name of DodgeDesigner (@cb_dodge), which is known to be posting information related to Elon Musk and his firms, said, "11,256 of India's listed villages still lacked 4G coverage as of May 2026."

The development comes on the day India started its apex telecom sector event, India Mobile Congress (IMC), which will be inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday.

World.title: Government should allow cultivation of HTBt cotton, farmers need technology: Seed bodies
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Seed industry bodies FSII and NSAI on Wednesday demanded that the government allow commercial cultivation of herbicide-tolerant Bt (HTBt) cotton at the earliest, as the crop variety is being grown illegally in some parts of the country, creating a Rs 1,500 crore informal seed market.

The Federation of Seed Industry of India (FSII) and the National Seed Association of India (NSAI) stressed the need to introduce high-yielding varieties and new technologies to boost domestic cotton production and reduce imports.

India's cotton production stands at around 29 million bales (of 170 kg each).

A study, Unauthorised Cultivation of HTBt Cotton in India: Extent, Drivers and Implications, was conducted by the South Asia Biotechnology Centre (SABC) with the support of these two associations.

It covered 16 districts across Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan, combining farmer surveys, supply-chain assessment and ELISA-based gene testing.

"Unauthorised herbicide-tolerant Bt (HTBt) cotton was grown on 65-72 lakh acres in Kharif 2025-26, or 24-30 per cent of India's total cotton area, sustaining an informal seed market worth an estimated Rs 1,500 crore," FSII Chairman Ajai Rana told reporters.





He informed that 1.25 crore packets of HTBt seed are being sold, currently worth Rs 1,500 crore. The total size of the cotton seed market is 5.5 crore packets worth Rs 6,000 crore.

Sales of legal Bt cotton seeds have declined.

"The government should fast-track the approval of HT Bt cotton," he said, adding that Mahyco has already made an application for this purpose in 2024.

The association also demanded changes in glyphosate label claims.

The product is used for weed management in the cotton crop.

"Farmers are not breaking the law out of choice. They are paying a black-market premium because the regulatory system has not given them the technology they need," Rana said.

The study found that farmers are actively bypassing formal channels and paying a premium technology fee to the black market just to secure operational survival and crop insurance, the FSII said.

"Unchecked use of unapproved genes and unmonitored glyphosate spraying could breed resistant pests and weeds that devastate cotton productivity," said Dr C D Mayee, President, Indian Society for Cotton Improvement and President, South Asia Biotechnology Centre.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The study pointed out that labour shortages are driving the shift. Weed control with glyphosate costs Rs 750-850 an acre, against Rs 12,000-15,000 for manual weeding.

Glyphosate use rose 26 per cent in a year, from 27,721 kilolitres in 2024-25 to 35,642 kilolitres in 2025-26.

"Due to a drop in productivity per acre, India has lost self-sufficiency in cotton production and become an importer of cotton. To regain self-sufficiency and revive the cotton economy, regulatory approval of herbicide-tolerant cotton and the pink bollworm trait should be a national priority," Rana said.

World.title: ‘You are doing your job’: Detained Rahul Gandhi offers water to police - watch
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi offered water bottles to police personnel while being detained during the opposition's protest in Delhi on Wednesday. Handing out the water bottles he was seen telling them, "You are all doing your work".

Rahul was later released from Barakhamba Road police station, where he had been taken after police stopped opposition leaders from proceeding towards Jantar Mantar.

Rahul Gandhi was among several opposition leaders and MPs detained as they attempted to reach the designated protest site to protest against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.

The leaders alleged that police stopped their buses and prevented them from moving towards Jantar Mantar.

Priyanka Gandhi alleges MPs were manhandled

The confrontation saw several opposition leaders detained, including Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, TMC Rajya Sabha MP Derek OâBrien and RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha. Priyanka Gandhi alleged that police personnel manhandled MPs during the confrontation.

"This is how they treat Members of Parliament who are asking simply to meet the election commissioner.





This is how they treat us. They are beating MPs. The Policemen have scratched me all over. They have thrown us to the ground. Now, we are not going to move from here. Let them crawl their forces back. I will not move from here."

Priyanka Gandhi and other detained leaders were later taken to Chhatrasal Stadium. She said the opposition would continue to defend the Constitution.

"What is the value of the Constitution in this nation? We will lay down our lives for the Constitution. No cost is too big for us"

Opposition protest followed Kharge's lunch meeting

The protest followed a lunch meeting hosted by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge for opposition MPs.

Rahul Gandhi had announced that the MPs would move to Jantar Mantar after they were denied permission to protest at the Election Commission office.

Kharge said the opposition would continue its agitation despite cases being filed against its leaders.

"No matter how many cases you file, No matter how much you try to scare us, We are not the ones to get scared, We will keep laughing and keep moving forward. We will continue the struggle."

Rahul Gandhi vows to bring PM Modi, Shah, Bhagwat and Gyanesh to justice

Rahul Gandhi later said Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat and Gyanesh Kumar would be brought to justice, accusing them of attacking the Constitution and the voice of the people.

"...They can do all this stuff, but we are going to bring them to justice. My guarantee is that all four (Union Home Minister Amit Shah, PM Modi, RSS Chief Mohan Bhagwat, CEC Gyanesh Kumar) of them will be brought to justice. This is all a panic reaction. This is all fear. Yes, they are going to be brought to justice...They have attacked the most sacred. They have attacked the Constitution. They have attacked the voice of the people.

They are going to pay for it on the streets"

World.title: India stresses constructive and ‘people-centric’ engagement with Bangladesh
