NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday reiterated that it wants to keep neighbourly relations stable and cooperative, and that its diplomacy with Bangladesh rests on a positive, people-focused outlook geared towards shared growth and regional development.At a press briefing on bilateral ties and regional cooperation, foreign ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that in high-level dialogues with Bangladeshi authorities, India continues to give priority to practical cooperation and joint economic progress, concentrating on initiatives that deliver direct benefits to the citizens of both countries."Our approach towards Bangladesh is to have positive, constructive, and forward-looking engagement with a people-centric focus for mutual growth and prosperity," Jaiswal stated. "We remain focused on this objective during our discussions with Bangladesh authorities."Earlier on Saturday, Indian high commissioner to Bangladesh, Dinesh Trivedi, said that former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's arrival in New Delhi two years ago was âunexpectedâ, adding that the Indian military had no part in arranging her extradition to India.Trivedi was speaking at the Bay of Bengal Conversation in Dhaka, an event hosted by a local think tank, the Centre for Governance Studies.He took questions on Hasina's legal status and the continuing debate over her extradition.Responding to those demands, Trivedi stated, "Hasinaji was not brought to India by the Indian Air Force or the Indian Army." He further noted, "It so happened because of the tragic circumstances in Bangladesh during that time. We hope and pray that should never happen, where innocent people get killed, doesnât matter in which part of the world."The high commissioner said the development took Indian authorities by surprise."The military aircraft came to Indiaâ¦ India was not prepared. I was watching on television, and the scroll was coming that she was going to some other country. At that point, Hasinaji was still the prime minister of Bangladesh. We had hardly any choice on that. It was our duty as a neighbour to accept the reality of life. Because situations are such that at times you are not prepared for such.""What was our [Indiaâs] choice?" Trivedi asked, noting that refusing "landing permission" could have fundamentally changed how events unfolded. He added that both countries are vibrant democracies whose respective "legal systems" are actively examining matters relating to bilateral legal procedures.The interim administration of Bangladesh lodged its first formal extradition request in December 2024. Since then, the government of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, which took office after the February 2026 general elections, has repeatedly renewed the call.

World.title: Loanees do not mortgage their constitutional rights with banks: Madras High Court
World.content:
The mere fact that a citizen of the country either raises a loan from a bank or stands as a guarantor for a loan availed by someone else does not mean that he has mortgaged his constitutional and legal rights lock, stock and barrel with the bank, the Madras High Court has observed.

Justice V. Lakshminarayanan made the observation while dismissing an application filed by Bank of Baroda to review his August 24, 2026 order revoking a Look Out Circular (LOC) issued against Kondepati Ganga Prasad who was a guarantor for a high value loan availed by GVR Infra Projects.

The judge highlighted that the right to travel freely across the world was a fundamental right enshrined under Article 21 of the Constitution as declared by the Supreme Court in Maneka Gandhi Vs. Union of India (1978). In order to have a restriction of that right, it should be in accordance with law.

“The term ‘law’ under Article 21 implies a legislation. A letter written by the Manager of the bank to the Bureau Of Immigration cannot be treated as ‘law.’ If a nationalised bank is permitted to do this, then every private creditor or non-banking finance corporation would also be emboldened to approach the police for issuance of LOC to prevent their debtors from going abroad,” the judge wrote.

He went on to state: “God forbid the debtors from being thrown at the mercy of wolves of creditors. All these observations are made only to point out that the constitutional rights of the petitioner does not come to an end with the commencement of mortgage with the review petitioner’s bank.”

In the present case, the guarantor proposes to go abroad to earn and repay the amount after returning. However, the bank was insisting upon him to repay the money first and then go abroad. “This is a catch-22 situation. If the bank wants the money, the petitioner has to earn it. The petitioner, in his wisdom, has decided to go abroad to earn it. The bank says till he pays the amount, he should not be permitted to go abroad. This vicious circle has to be broken.”

Justice Lakshminarayanan also said, no business venture gets started with an intention to create a loss but such was the nature of life that not every business ends up successful. The bank, while issuing the loan, was well aware that all loans were not going to be repaid and some were bound to become sticky or Non-Performing Assets (NPAs).

“I should point out that the Bank of Baroda, for the very purpose, has a separate branch called the stressed accounts branch. This shows that the number of sticky accounts with the Bank of Baroda is so high that it requires special attention of a team of officers,” he added.

The judge recorded the submission of the bank’s counsel that it had not lodged any criminal complaint of fraud against the guarantor either with the Central Bureau of Investigation or the State police. Even the bank officials who were responsible for clearing the loan in favour of the private company had not been prosecuted.

“The bank has not done so because it is very well aware that it was the business decision taken by the managerial authorities at that relevant point of time to clear the loan in favour of the petitioner. When there is no fraud, either at the instance of the petitioner or at the instance of the managerial staff of the bank, for the mere fact that the petitioner is a defaulter, he cannot be forced to stay within the four corners of this country in order to ensure that the amounts are re-paid,” the judge concluded.

World.title: Odisha govt. forms panel to study SEBC political backwardness
World.content:
The Odisha government on Wednesday constituted a commission to study the numerical strength, political representation and extent of political backwardness among the socially and educationally backward classes (SEBCs) in local self-government institutions.

The commission will be headed by retired Odisha High Court judge Justice Pramath Patnaik, according to a notification issued by the ST and SC Development, Minorities and Backward Classes Welfare Department.

Retired IAS officer Bijay Kumar Prusty will serve as a member of the commission and Sujata Mishra, Special Secretary in the department, will be the member-secretary of the panel, the notification stated.

The decision assumes significance as both panchayat and urban local body polls are scheduled to be held next year.

“Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has decided to conduct a study on the population of SEBCs in various local self-government institutions, both rural and urban, in the State, including panchayats and urban local bodies, their political representation, and the extent of their political backwardness in these institutions,” read a statement issued by the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO).

The commission will study the proportion of SEBCs in various local self-government institutions in both rural and urban areas of the State in relation to the total population of the respective areas. It will also examine their political representation in local self-government institutions and the nature and implications of their political backwardness in comparison with their population, the CMO stated.

‘Ensure adequate representation’

The exercise will facilitate appropriate measures to ensure adequate representation of people belonging to SEBCs in local self-government institutions in the State and safeguard their rights, the statement added.

Earlier, the Bharatiya Janata Party government had provided for 11.25% reservation for students belonging to this category in professional higher educational institutions, including engineering and medical institutions.

The Bharatiya Janata Party government had earlier decided to make a provision for 11.25% reservation for students belonging to this category in professional higher educational institutions, including engineering and medical institutions.

The Naveen Patnaik-led former Biju Janata Dal government had constituted the Odisha State Commission for Backward Classes for surveying the social and educational conditions of the people belonging to the backward classes. The commission had then put the State’s OBC population at 1.95 crore.

World.title: PM, HM likely to skip West Bengal govt’s mega Mahalaya event
World.content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi as well as Union Home Minister Amit Shah are likely to skip West Bengal government’s mega event organised on the occasion of Mahalaya on October 10.

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government, which came to power in the State in May 2026, had decided to organise an event at Kolkata’s Eden Gardens cricket stadium on the occasion of Mahalaya. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari had earlier said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi was supposed to attend the grand event. This will be the first time in recent public memory that the Eden Gardens was used for a non-sports event.

However, a few days ago it was learnt that the Prime Minister will not be available for the event. There was buzz in the administrative circles that instead of the Prime Minister, Home Minister Amit Shah may be present at the event. However, with the political situation in Delhi being volatile over the protests seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, neither the Prime Minister nor the Home Minister is likely to make it to event. While the Home Minister is likely to skip the Mahalaya event, he may visit the city during the festival and inaugurate Durga Pujas being organised by key BJP leaders.

Although the absence of the Prime Minister and the Union Home Minister has reduced the political attraction of the Mahalaya event, the State government is leaving no stone unturned to make the programme a grand spectacle. West Bengal Governor R.N. Ravi, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and members of his council of Ministers are expected to attend the programme.

Directions have been issued from the Chief Minister’s office that all the Ministers of the State government have to remain present at the event. Eminent personalities from different walks of life have also been invited, while several prominent artists from the cultural fraternity are expected to participate.

The rendition of “Mahishasura Mardini” will be broadcast over loudspeakers at five ghats along the river Hooghly in Kolkata early in the morning of Mahalaya.

The celebrations will also extend beyond Eden Gardens with a road show being scheduled along the Red Road.

The BJP leadership had criticised the former Trinamool Congress government for organising Durga Puja carnival on the Red Road, where prominent Durga Pujas idols would go past a stage with the former Chief Minister and other dignitaries being present.

The BJP government in West Bengal has said that unlike the past, Durga Puja celebrations will be held as per rituals and maintaining a proper religious calendar.

World.title: Bombay High Court asks Maharashtra to restore trust of MPSC aspirants, students to return to classes
World.content:
The Bombay High Court on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) asked the Maharashtra government to take steps to restore the trust of students protesting over the recruitment process managed by the Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC), and requested them to return to their studies. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna, hearing a petition about inconvenience caused to citizens in Pune, said the matter was before the court and the State must respond in writing.

Protests by students had blocked roads in Pune and caused inconvenience to citizens, the petition said. The students sought changes in the MPSC examination and recruitment process.

The State told the court that the students had demands. The State said it had accepted the demand to set the fee at ₹100, and the demand to hold examinations in person. It had sent a representation to the Governor on the demand that the MPSC Chairperson’s resignation, the State said.

The court noted that vacancies in government jobs ran to thousands. Students alleged that exams were not held in accordance with procedure, and papers were leaked. When students protested, it meant their grievances needed attention, the court said. The students were in Pune to secure an education and were not against the nation, the court said, adding that the State should take steps to restore trust.

The court asked the State to provide details in writing on the recruitment process, and on the vacancies in various departments. It issued notice to the State, and asked it to file an affidavit.

The court also requested the students to resume their studies. If they wanted to protest, they must seek permission and find a place that was not a road, it said. No inconvenience should be caused to citizens, it said. The matter was before it and it would ensure a response from the State, the court said, examining how the State dealt with the issue.

Recruitment should be held at pace, the court said. Students should have a chance to appear in exams. Parents who send their children to Pune faced worries, it said, adding that the careers of students should not be affected.

The State said the police had shown restraint.

Advocate-General Milind Sathe told the court that a First Information Report would affect careers of students.

Students are not against the nation, the court said, adding that the State should consider the position of parents.

The court called for peace, and said not adverse message on Pune, a centre of education, should go across the country. requested the parties to maintain peace.

It asked students to join classes, and seek permission for protests, without inconveniencing citizens. The court posted the matter for a later date.

World.title: Dept. of Posts to hold Dak Adalat meeting in Chennai
World.content:
The Department of Posts will conduct a Dak Adalat at the office of senior superintendent of post offices, Chennai city central division, to address customers’ grievances on October 12 at 11 a.m.

A press release said the chairperson of the divisional level dak adalat will hear the grievances related to the postal department’s products and services. Customers may send their complaints pertaining to the division to senior superintendent of post offices, Chennai city central division, Chennai-17 through ordinary or registered post on or before October 9. Only those cases, which have not been resolved at post offices would be taken up.

World.title: Civil Supplies officials seize one tonne of PDS rice in Ranipet
World.content:
A team led by Arakkonam Taluk Supply Officer of the Department of Civil Supplies seized one tonne of rice meant for supply under the Public Distribution System (PDS) at a railway station in Arakkonam town on Wednesday.

The police said that as per the orders of Collector N. Priya Ravichandran, special teams comprising police personnel and Civil Supplies officials were formed to prevent smuggling of PDS rice in the district. During a surprise check at the railway station, the team found 22 bags of PDS rice. The seized rice was sent to a godown maintained by the Department of Civil Supplies in Ranipet.

The police analysed CCTV camera footage in the area and found a group of people had loaded rice sacks onto the train. A case was registered by Arakkonam police. Special teams were formed to nab escaped suspects. A probe is under way.

World.title: CMC to organise conference on gene therapy in Vellore
World.content:
The 11th International Cell and Gene Therapy Conference (CGTCON 2026) will be held at Christian Medical College (CMC) in Vellore town on October 8.

According to a press release, the conference, including a workshop, will be organised by the Centre for Stem Cell Research, a collaborative unit of BRIC-Institute for Stem Cell Science and Regenerative Medicine (inStem), Bengaluru, and the CMC.

This year’s conference, which will end on October 10, will showcase developments in fields of major diseases, such as haematological, ocular, diabetic and metabolic, neurological, cardiovascular, and dermatological disorders. It will also cover organoids and disease modelling, nucleic acid delivery technologies, and the industry, manufacturing, and regulatory aspects of advanced therapeutics.

CGTCON 2026 aims to strengthen collaborations between clinicians, scientists, industry partners, and regulatory stakeholders, the release said.

World.title: INDIA bloc leaders in Bihar take out Aakrosh March against ECI
World.content:
INDIA bloc leaders on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) organised Aakrosh March at all 534 blocks in Bihar by burning the effigies of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged illegalities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).

In Patna, the march started from the Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) State office, located at Beerchand Patel Path, and moved to the Income Tax Golambar, where effigies of the three were burned.

INDIA bloc leaders alleged that the Election Commission of India (ECI) is acting as a puppet of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and that politics is underway to weaken democracy and the constitution.

“The truth has come to the public domain now about how Narendra Modi and Amit Shah are using the ECI to weaken democracy with the SIR process first in Bihar and other states,” said RJD spokesperson Ejaz Ahmed.

He added that the INDIA bloc, under the leadership of RJD National Working President Tejashwi Yadav, vowed to continue the struggle to save democracy. Demands were raised to expose the ECI allegedly involved in fraud and to hold fresh elections in Bihar.

During the protest march, a large number of INDIA bloc and workers hit the streets, chanting slogans such as “Gyanesh ko Bhagayo, Loktantra Ko Bacho (oust Gyanesh and save democracy)” and “Vote Chor- Gaddi Chhor (vote thieves, vacate the chair).”

“Policies weakening democracy will not be tolerated. BJP-ECI nexus, have some shame and stop the murder of democracy,” said a leader of Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist) Liberation.

On October 8, 2026, a Lok Bhavan march led by the Leader of the Opposition in the Bihar Legislative Assembly will also be launched from Patna’s Shaheed Smarak, and sit-in protest marches will be held in every district.

Leaders and workers from all parties of the INDIA bloc, including sitting and former MPs, MLAs, and MLCs, will participate in this Lok Bhavan March. The march will commence at 11 a.m.

Meanwhile, K. Ravi Kumar, Chief Electoral Officer of Jharkhand, said that eligible Indian citizens from Jharkhand who have not yet been enrolled must ensure that their names are added to the electoral roll by attending the digitisation camps, which will be on October 8 and 9, or the mega helpdesk on October 10.

“Eligible Indian citizens who, for any reason, have not yet been able to get their names added to the electoral roll during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) should visit the special digitisation camps organised at their respective polling stations on 8, and 9 to register their names using Form-6,” Mr. Kumar said.

He has directed District Election Officers (DEOs), Electoral Registration Officers (EROs), Assistant Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs), and Booth Level Officers (BLOs) to identify such citizens and provide them with the necessary assistance during the enrollment process.

World.title: DG ISPR says Pakistani troops present in Saudi Arabia 'for decades' across multiple domains
World.content:
Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry has said that Pakistani troops are in Saudi Arabia, adding that they had been in the kingdom “for decades” and across multiple domains.

The military spokesperson made these remarks during an interview with CNN correspondent Ivan Watson, who posted a small clip on his X account.

“I can confirm that the forces of Pakistan are already there (Saudi Arabia),” Lt Gen Chaudhry said.

Watson then sought a confirmation that Pakistani troops were already on the ground in Saudi Arabia as part of the Makkah Defence Alliance between Pakistan, the kingdom and Turkiye.

To that, the military spokesperson replied, “Pakistan troops have been there for decades […] The Makkah alliance is not something that has come out in a vacuum. So there is a sustained diplomatic, political, military and people-to-people relationship between Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia. So, I can share with you that Pakistani forces, in multiple capabilities and domains, are already there.”

Lt Gen Chaudhry’s remarks come after Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye agreed to the deployment of military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom during an emergency meeting of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in Riyadh on Monday.

The three countries had held an emergency meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) of the Makkah Defence Alliance to address the security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia.

“The committee decided to move immediately to the practical implementation of the collective defence commitments and to take the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in the kingdom, in accordance with the approved arrangements and the national legislation of the parties, thereby enhancing readiness, military integration, and the collective capacity to confront and counter threats,” a statement issued by the Foreign Office after the meeting said.

While the statement did not specifically name any threat, the development comes against the backdrop of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia in the Yemen conflict.

Separately, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, who was part of Pakistan’s delegation in the meeting, joined Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath’ via telephone the same day and said Saudi Arabia had made “gains and recovered some areas” in Yemen in the ongoing fighting with the Houthis.

When asked about a possible operational role by Pakistan and Turkiye, the defence minister replied that both nations had a “presence in theatre”, but only Saudi troops were involved in combat operations.

“Whatever assistance they require is being provided. But right now, the Turkish and Pakistani armies are playing a supportive role,” he said, noting that Pakistan was involved in reconnaissance.

Asif had earlier also reaffirmed that Pakistan would “practically and diplomatically” stand by Saudi Arabia against Yemen’s Houthi rebels if the situation escalated. The defence minister had said that Pakistan would fulfil all its obligations under the Makkah Defence Alliance in accordance with the terms of the agreement between the three countries.

The Makkah defence pact , signed on Aug 7, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

On Sept 25, the military chiefs of alliance members Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia met in Riyadh for urgently convened talks under the pact in light of the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

World.title: Govt raises petrol price by Rs1.82 per litre, reduces high-speed diesel rate by Re0.91
World.content:
The government on Wednesday raised the price of petrol by Rs1.82 per litre, but reduced that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.91 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs396.65 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs394.94 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 8 (Thursday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Emergency, governor's rule would 'definitely' be imposed if deemed necessary to 'save' KP: Kundi
World.content:
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi said on Wednesday that if the prime minister and the president deemed it necessary to impose an emergency or governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to “save the province” facing terrorism, it would “definitely be enforced”.

The governor’s remarks came during Geo News’ programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath’, where the possibility of emergency or governor’s rule was discussed.

Responding to questions on the subject, Kundi argued that there had been past instances of emergency and governor’s rule being imposed.

“In Balochistan, the PPP had to end its government for law and order and impose an emergency,” he remarked.

Asked whether an emergency or governor’s rule would be sustainable if imposed, Kundi replied: “The first thing [to decide] is when and whether it is imposed. We can discuss its sustainability in another programme.”

This prompted the host to prod Kundi further, saying his remarks indicated that only imposing an emergency or governor’s rule was being considered and its sustainability would addressed later.

Kundi said in response, “We have to save the province, we have to establish peace in the province.”

The Centre has warned the PTI-led KP government in recent days of sending it packing through an emergency or governor’s rule as the party goes ahead with a protest march to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. Federal ministers have also cited the security situation in KP in this connection, as reiterated by Kundi.

Meanwhile, the march remains a major bone of contention between the government and the main opposition party in the Centre, the PTI, with both taking entrenched positions.

On Sunday, Interior Mini­ster Mohsin Naqvi also called on Kundi to discuss the political and security situation amid speculations of ‘imminent’ governor’s rule in the province.

The meeting was also mentioned in the Geo News programme, with Kundi being asked whether preparations were under way for an emergency or governor’s rule. But Kundi said the PTI’s long march and security-related matters were discussed during the meeting.

The KP governor then went on the accuse the provincial government of “facilitating terrorism” and not doing enough to curb it.

World.title: CDF Munir reaffirms Pakistan’s commitment to international peace in meeting with UN chief
World.content:
Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir on Wednesday reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to international peace in a meeting with United Nations Secretary General Antonio Guterres, the military’s media affairs wing said.

The UN secretary general is currently in Islamabad on a two-day official visit.

In a statement on Wednesday, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said Guterres called on CDF Munir at the General Headquarters (GHQ) in Rawalpindi.

“During the meeting, matters of mutual interest, the prevailing regional security environment and the UN’s role in promoting international peace and security were discussed,” it said.

“The two sides exchanged views on regional stability, the Jammu and Kashmir dispute, India’s abeyance of the Indus Waters Treaty and terrorism emanating from Afghanistan,” it added.

During the meeting, CDF Munir also reaffirmed “Pakistan’s commitment to international peace and highlighted its contributions to UN peacekeeping missions”. He also lauded the UN’s role in “advancing peace, stability and humanitarian cooperation”.

According to ISPR, the UN secretary general paid tribute to the sacrifices and contributions of Pakistan and its armed forces in the war against terror and in UN peacekeeping missions.

“He also acknowledged Pakistan’s continued commitment to international peace and security,” ISPR said, adding that Guterres specifically appreciated “Pakistan’s efforts towards the peaceful resolution of regional conflicts”.

UN chief meets PM Shehbaz

Later, the UN secretary general also met Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who lauded Guterres for his “principled commitment to the UN Charter, multilateralism, international law, dialogue and the peaceful settlement of disputes”, a statement by the PM’s Office said.

It added that the premier acknowledged the UN chief’s “outstanding contribution to international peace and security during his tenure”.

PM Shehbaz also reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to an “effective, inclusive and representative UN, particularly at a time when multilateralism faces significant challenges”, the statement added.

Welcoming Guterres’ UN80 Initiative, he emphasised that UN reforms should be responsive to the priorities of developing countries, while strengthening conflict prevention, peaceful settlement of disputes, peacekeeping and peacebuilding.

Additionally, the premier also reaffirmed Pakistan’s longstanding contribution to UN peacekeeping and the maintenance of international peace and security.

“The prime minister highlighted Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts to promote dialogue and de-escalation, including its mediation role between the US and Iran,” the statement read, adding that PM Shehbaz reiterated that dialogue and diplomacy remain the only viable path to resolving disputes.

PM Shehbaz also reiterated the need for a peaceful resolution of the Jammu and Kashmir dispute, in accordance with relevant UN Security Council resolutions and the wishes of the Kashmiri people.

“He highlighted that the Indus Waters Treaty is a binding international agreement and that India’s unilateral decision to place it in abeyance has no legal basis,” the statement added.

Moreover, PM Shehbaz, noting that a peaceful and stable Afghanistan remains in Pakistan’s interest, expressed serious concern over the presence of terrorist groups and terrorism emanating from Afghan territory and emphasised the need for concrete and verifiable actions against such elements.

Reaffirming Pakistan’s steadfast support for Palestinian self-determination and statehood, PM Shehbaz reiterated Islamabad’s support for the implementation of the Gaza Peace Plan and UNSC Resolution 2803, which endorses the end of Israel’s military campaign in the Gaza Strip.

“The prime minister also underscored the need for greater access to affordable and concessional financing for developing countries to advance development and climate resilience,” the PMO stated.

According to the statement, Secretary General Guterres appreciated Pakistan’s longstanding contribution to the organisation and international peace and security, including its role in UN peacekeeping and the Security Council.

“He particularly appreciated Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts to promote dialogue, mediation and de-escalation, and welcomed its continued commitment to multilateralism and the purposes and principles of the UN Charter,” the statement read.

On the first day of his trip, the UN secretary general held a meeting with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar. During the meeting, Guterres appreciated Pakistan’s “longstanding contribution to the UN, as well as its diplomatic efforts to promote dialogue, mediation and de-escalation”.

He also addressed a joint stakeout with Dar, during which he lauded Pakistan’s “pivotal role” in mediating between the United States and Iran as he called on the parties to end the conflict and return to diplomacy.

President Asif Ali Zardari also conferred the Nishan-i-Imtiaz on Guterres in recognition of his “distinguished international service, leadership of the UN and contribution to global peace and development”.

The two also held a separate meeting, where Zardari appreciated Guterres’ principled leadership, his efforts for international peace, dialogue, diplomacy and peaceful settlement of disputes, as well as his constructive engagement with Pakistan and attention to the concerns of developing countries.

World.title: Will not allow military operations, KP CM tells march participants in Khyber
World.content:
The PTI convoy led by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Sohail Afridi reached the Khyber district on Wednesday with the provincial chief executive vowing that he would not allow another military operation in KP.

The route plan for the march, being carried out to demand the release of jailed PTI founder Imran Khan, has been changing since it began.

The PTI earlier planned that the chief minister would lead his convoy to Khairabad — which borders Punjab’s Attock — on Oct 8 and announce the next plan of action.

However, according to a statement released by CM Afridi’s office, he told the protesters in Khyber today that the long march would now go all the way to Swabi, where he would announce the next plan of action.

But a member of the PTI’s social media team, Omar Farooq, told Dawn that the final destination remained tentative for now.

He also confirmed that the march will reach Peshawar on Thursday and spend the night tomorrow in Charsadda. The plan was also shared by the focal person to the chief minister on social media, Yar Muhammad Khan Niazi.

PTI MNA Sajid Khan Mohmand told Dawn that the CM would reach Mohmand on Oct 9 and address a gathering at Mian Mandi Bazaar on Oct 10.

The march was announced as part of the PTI’s nationwide protest, initially scheduled for Sept 27 but was later postponed to Oct 4.

On Oct 4, the march began from Lakki Marwat and Karak, from where the protesters trekked to Kohat on the second day and arrived in Mattani, located on the outskirts of Peshawar, on Tuesday night.

While the plan for the trek after Oct 8 is yet to be announced, the PTI previously announced Islamabad as its final destination.

The Centre has warned the party against any protest or gatherings in Islamabad. However, the PTI decided to embark on the march after weekend talks with the federal government to bridge their differences failed for multiple reasons , particularly over the counterterrorism policy.

KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi again challenged the PTI today to go through Swabi, saying, “Let them cross through Swabi and show us”, while speaking on Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath’.

Afridi decries military operations

“I will not allow another military operation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa; I will resist anti-people policies till I am the chief minister,” Afridi said while addressing PTI supporters in Khyber.

Khyber is also home to Tirah, whose residents had agreed to vacate their homes to facilitate a military operation against terrorists in December 2025.

In recent months, the displaced families have expressed reservations over the government’s fulfilment of commitments following their displacement, including the provision of financial assistance.

The KP government, led by the PTI, has also been opposed to military operations in the province. Now, it also finds itself at odds with the Centre over the latter’s counterterrorism policy — a sticking point that is said to have led to the breakdown of negotiations between the federal government and the opposition in the Centre, including the PTI.

Mentioning those talks, the KP chief minister alleged in his address that attempts were made to compel the provincial government to 

“The people of Tirah were displaced in extreme winter,” he said, and added without naming anyone that “they did not have any realisation of the hardships faced by the people”.

CM Afridi claimed that people were happy in tribal areas before military operations, recalling that PTI founder and ex-prime minister Imran Khan had been voicing opposition to those operations since 2004.

He also decried what he described as the provision of insufficient funds for erstwhile tribal areas by the Centre, claiming that his government had released Rs21 billion for families affected by military operations.

Noting that the KP government was being accused of not cooperating on counter-terrorism, he argued that terrorism was also prevalent in Balochistan, where the provincial government was cooperating with the Centre.

He reiterated his allegation that the Centre had not released the funds allocated for the erstwhile tribal areas, including Khyber, after their merger with KP.

Additional input from Mohammad Ashfaq and Fauzee Khan

World.title: Bahrain's foreign minister arrives in Islamabad for 2-day visit
World.content:
Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani arrived in Islamabad on Wednesday evening for a two-day visit, where he is expected to co-chair the third session of the Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC), the Foreign Office (FO) said.

According to the FO, Al Zayani was received at the airport by Economic Affairs Division Secretary Muhammad Humair Karim and Additional Secretary (Middle East) Zahid Hussain.

“The visit reflects the close, cordial and brotherly ties between Pakistan and Bahrain and underscores the shared commitment to further strengthening bilateral cooperation,” it added.

In an earlier statement, the FO said that Bahrain’s top diplomat will be visiting the country at the invitation of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar.

“The two sides will review the entire spectrum of bilateral relations and discuss ways to further strengthen cooperation across diverse areas of mutual interest, including trade, investment, economic cooperation, defence and security, labour and manpower, and cultural exchanges,” it said.

The two sides would also exchange views on regional and international developments of mutual interest and cooperation at multilateral forums, the FO added.

“Pakistan and Bahrain enjoy close, brotherly relations founded on shared faith, common values, mutual respect, and longstanding people-to-people links,” it noted.

The FO further stated that the two countries maintain regular high-level exchanges and close cooperation across a wide range of areas.

“The visit reflects the strong momentum in Pakistan-Bahrain relations and the shared commitment of both countries to further deepen bilateral cooperation and advance mutually beneficial ties,” it said.

Earlier this month, Dar chaired an inter-ministerial meeting to review preparations for the Pakistan-Bahrain JMC, which he will co-chair with his Bahraini counterpart.

The deputy premier had directed the ministries concerned to finalise preparations in close coordination and pursue concrete outcomes from the Bahrain FM’s visit.

Dar and Al Zayani last met in September on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, where they discussed bilateral relations, including preparations for the forthcoming JMC session.

They also exchanged views on regional and international developments, with Al Zayani appreciating Pakistan’s constructive role in promoting regional peace and stability.

Following the last JMC session in July 2021, which was held in Manama, the two countries signed a memorandum of understanding to promote business between the two countries.

Islamabad and Manama had agreed to establish the JMC in 2014, when King Sheikh Hamad bin Isa bin Salman Al-Khalifa paid a three-day visit to Pakistan.

World.title: Remaining 3 Pakistanis rescued from hijacked vessel off Somalia return home
World.content:
The three remaining Pakistani crew members of MT Honour 25, an oil tanker that was hijacked off the coast of Somalia in April, landed in Karachi on Wednesday.

According to Shaheen Burney, the vice chairperson of the Ansar Burney Trust, the three crew members arrived in the city at 4:40pm via an Ethiopian Airways flight from Addis Ababa.

Sindh Governor Nehal Hashmi welcomed the crew members at Karachi’s Jinnah International Airport upon their return, according to a press release. Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab and other dignitaries were also present.

The governor met the returning Pakistanis, inquired about their well-being and presented them with bouquets. He expressed solidarity with them, saying that the incident was extremely painful and highlighting that the “sufferings and hardships of the affected Pakistanis were being shared as a collective national concern”, the statement said.

Speaking to the media, the governor said that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had taken special notice of the matter, issued necessary directives and remained continuously informed about the situation of the affected Pakistanis.

He said that, although no amount of money could compensate for the loss of a human life, the state would take “all possible measures” to support the affected families, particularly with regards to the education, healthcare and future of their children.

PM Shehbaz had issued clear directions regarding residential plots and arrangements for the education, upbringing and healthcare of the children of the affected families, he added, according to the press release.

Hashmi noted that the state would extend support to the affected families as far as possible, while any financial assistance received in this regard would also be given to the affected persons. The provincial government had also extended its full cooperation, he said.

“We are not here as representatives of any political party; we are here as Pakistanis. We have come to express solidarity with our brothers and assure them that they are not alone — the entire nation stands with them,” the statement quoted the governor as saying.

He added that the incident had once again demonstrated that “a united nation could face any kind of difficult situation”. He also prayed for the complete and speedy recovery of the returning Pakistanis.

In late September, the maritime police force of Somalia’s semi-autonomous Puntland recovered the Palau-flagged oil tanker, which had 19 crew members on board, including 10 Pakistanis.

Of those 10, the Foreign Office (FO) confirmed that three were among five crew members who died during the operation. Another four Pakistanis who were injured returned to the country on Sunday along with the remains of their three colleagues, with the government facilitating their repatriation via Ethiopia.

In an earlier post on X, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said the remaining three crew members of MT Honour 25 — Imran Ali, Husain Yousuf and Muhammad Yasin — were “en route to safely return home to Karachi from Addis Ababa later today and will be reunited with their families”.

He said the Pakistani ambassador in the Ethiopian capital “met the three crew members and ensured that they were provided all necessary facilities and services during their stay” in Addis Ababa.

Dar noted that the FO and the government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, “made every effort to secure the safe return of all our crew members”.

“While we welcome the safe return of our people, we remain deeply saddened by the loss of three Pakistani crew members. May Allah grant them eternal peace and give strength to their families.”

FM Dar reaffirmed that Pakistan “remains firmly committed to working with international partners to combat piracy and ensure the safety and security of seafarers and maritime routes”.

Apart from Pakistanis, the vessel’s crew also included seven Indonesians, an Indian and a Sri Lankan. After the April hijacking, months passed with no progress either in negotiations or the payment of the ransom, said to be around $3 million, for the recovery of the hostages.

The hostages were said to be victims of an “ ownership crisis ”, as it was not clearly established who owned the ship — the man previously thought to be an owner was later revealed to be more likely a middleman who hired them.

During its ordeal, the crew made several emotional videos and audio appeals , reporting that they had run out of clean water, food and medicine. Meanwhile, their families launched an international appeal, calling on foreign governments, the United Nations (UN) and the International Maritime Organisation (IMO) to take coordinated action to help secure the release of their loved ones.

For its part, FO maintained that it had remained “actively engaged” to secure the release of the sailors.

World.title: CM Afridi slams Governor Kundi for 'unconstitutional' meetings, claims move intended to provoke KP govt
World.content:
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Wednesday slammed Governor Faisal Karim Kundi for holding “unconstitutional” meetings, contending that the move was an “attack on democracy”.

His remarks came a day after Governor Kundi chaired a meeting with the KP chief secretary and inspector general (IG) on the province’s security situation.

Addressing the 60th cabinet meeting in Peshawar, Afridi said that the KP governor, who belonged to the PPP, staged a “drama” yesterday by summoning the meeting and termed the move “unconstitutional”.

“The governor convening such a meeting in the presence of a provincial government with a two-thirds majority is unacceptable,” he said.

“The provincial assembly, cabinet and government are fully functional and intact,” the PTI leader asserted, terming Kundi’s act an “attack on the Constitution and democracy”.

Afridi contended that the purpose of the governor’s “unconstitutional activities” was to “provoke the provincial government and force it to react”.

However, he advised PTI workers to stay peaceful and abide by the law and the Constitution.

Calling on the province’s chief secretary and IG, the chief minister urged them not to comply with any unconstitutional or illegal order from anyone if he does not order them to do so.

He reiterated that KP’s people and administration had made “countless sacrifices” in the fight against terrorism.

“If someone pushes you to follow any unconstitutional order, do not follow it. It can damage our province or the country.”

He also called on the chief secretary to urge the provincial administration not to indulge in any unconstitutional activity and to take action against those who were accused of corrupt practices.

The chief minister then took aim at Kundi’s PPP, blaming ex-president Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, along with General Yahya Khan, for the separation of East Pakistan, now Bangladesh.

He accused President Asif Ali Zardari of “intending to make another East Pakistan here“.

“We will not allow any conspiracy to break up Pakistan to succeed,” he asserted.

“The party that raised the slogan of democracy separated Bangladesh from Pakistan in the past for its personal interests,” he alleged.

“Prioritising personal interests over national interests has been the PPP’s practice,” he further claimed.

Responding to Afridi, Kundi said on Geo News’ programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath’ said he called the meeting in light keeping in view the prevalent terrorism in the province.

He then went on accusing the PTI of facilitating and supporting terrorism.

The remarks by the CM and the governor come amid heightened tensions between the Centre and the PTI-led opposition, with the latter going ahead with its long march despite warnings from the Centre of action against any such move.

Hours-long talks over the weekend between a joint delegation of the government and PPP, and the opposition alliance ended in a deadlock, with both sides blaming the other for the breakdown.

Political temperatures have also remained high due to speculations of the Centre imposing governor’s rule in the province, with Kundi and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi discussing the move on Sunday.

‘Policy shift is necessary’

The KP CM also reiterated his objection to the Centre’s counterterrorism policy and defended his government’s efforts in supporting the police in the fight against terrorism.

He contended that terrorism had been “imposed on the province again”, asserting that the PTI-led provincial government had always supported the police and the people of KP.

Afridi maintained that he had been making efforts to strengthen the police, the Counter-Terrorism Department and Special Branch since he took the oath on Oct 15, 2025.

“The KP police have the most modern weapons and equipment compared with any other police force in Pakistan,” the chief minister said.

He contended that the federal government had always treated KP like a “stepchild”.

“The tribal districts were merged into KP in 2018, but they have not been fully integrated financially to this day,” CM Afridi claimed, adding that the financial rights of the tribal districts agreed upon at the time of their merger had not been provided yet.

The PTI leader went on to claim that federal governments had “continuously imposed military operations” on KP since 2004.

“People displaced by the federal government’s wrong policies kept crying on the streets, but they have still not received full compensation,” he said, adding that nearly Rs100 billion in compensation were still outstanding.

“Those whose homes were destroyed, families affected and mosques demolished are still wandering from pillar to post for their compensation.”

He highlighted that while a compensation of only Rs400,000 per household had been fixed for tribal families, they had not even been paid the promised amount.

Afridi stressed that a commitment was also made to provide between Rs370million and Rs380m per month to displaced people from North Waziristan at the Baka Khel camp. “The displaced people of Baka Khel are still not being provided the monthly amount as promised.”

“It is the provincial government’s responsibility to stand with people displaced by the federal government’s wrong policies,” the chief minister stated, adding that his government had provided Rs21bn for displaced people.

“The provincial government also has to bear responsibility for losses caused by military operations and collateral damage as a result of drone attacks,” Afridi said.

He also remarked that the individuals making decisions in the federal government had no sense of the difficulties faced by the people as a result of those decisions.

“If the federal government is sincere with KP, it should upgrade the province’s NFC (National Finance Commission) share and pay its outstanding dues of around Rs125bn to the province that has sacrificed 80,000 precious lives,” he demanded.

Afridi reaffirmed that KP had to fight terrorism as well as deal with the situation created by the federal government’s policies.

“The KP government and police are serious about maintaining law and order. Turning the police into personal servants and assigning them other tasks is wrong,” he declared.

“If the policy of KP’s stakeholders is followed, peace can be established within 100 days,” the PTI leader insisted.

He questioned why peace could not be established in the province “despite 14,000 intelligence-based operations and 22 major military operations over 22 years”, terming it a “failure of the federal policy”.

Afridi maintained that if the issue of peace still exists in KP even after 22 years, the federal government should change its policy against terrorism if it was “serious in doing so”.

“The excuse that KP is not cooperating is unacceptable; the same policy is also failing in Balochistan,” he claimed, as both provinces have witnessed an increase in terrorist activities in recent years.

“The Balochistan government is cooperating with the federal government, but peace has still not been established there,” Afridi said, claiming the Centre’s counterterrorism policy was neither effective in KP nor in Balochistan.

“A shift in policy is necessary. KP can establish peace within 100 days,” he reaffirmed.

In his address, Afridi also once again criticised Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz’s remarks that her province faced no threats from India, despite the state’s narrative of the presence of Indian proxies in Pakistan in the face of Fitna al Hindustan.

Asif says ‘enough is enough’

Meanwhile, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif assailed the PTI-led KP government for continuing its “complete detachment from terrorism in the province and criminal indifference”.

“Enough is enough!!!” he wrote in a post on X.

“The PTI provincial government is roaming the streets for a so-called failed political long march, while its facilitators have unleashed a fresh wave of terrorism against the people of KP during this very time,” he said.

The minister recalled Tuesday’s attacks in Dera Ismail Khan, where customs officials were among five people killed.

He remarked that the entire provincial cabinet, including the chief minister, was “numb to this serious matter and fully engrossed in their politically failed long march”.

“As always, these insensitive and shameless people did not even condemn the innocent murder of these five individuals in DI Khan, offered no condolences to the grieving families, did not attend their funerals or, at the very least, visit their homes to express regret,” Asif regretted.

“This is inexcusable by any standard.”

Instead, the defence minister noted, the KP CM had scheduled a meeting today at his party’s behest to reprimand the IG and chief secretary for attending the governor’s security meeting.

“The chief minister and his cabinet of a province under the scourge of terrorism have completely abandoned the province’s people to the mercy of the terrorists. That is why the people of KP are protesting against the provincial government on the streets in various areas.

“This can no longer be tolerated,” Asif declared.

The defence minister accused the KP government of being in “complete collusion” with terrorists, saying there was evidence available of “its facilitator ecosystem, which every Pakistani has witnessed with their own eyes over the past three years”.

Recalling past arrests of ex-premier Nawaz Sharif and his family members, as well as PML-N leaders, Asif asserted: “Time has proven that the allegations were just allegations and they were imprisoned on Imran Khan’s behest.”

Yet, he stressed, the PML-N fulfilled its parliamentary role responsibly under the Constitution and did not hold the country and institutions “hostage”.

“It fought a legal and constitutional battle in the courts and parliament. It did not ally with the Taliban,” Asif declared.

The defence minister said that the “time has come to make crucial decisions”.

“KP cannot be left any longer to the mercy of incompetent, insensitive rulers and Taliban allies,” he avowed.

Asif further stressed that the unity of the country cannot be put at risk. “An entire province cannot be held hostage. Enough is enough.”
